9.title: A fitting end
9.content:
What makes the Batman so appealing? Essentially a caped and cowled crusader earning his bread by his ability to strike fear, albeit with lots of cash and technology to boot, Batman is easily the most human of all superheroes. Tormented, often ridiculed, and always looking for relevance, he is but an enhanced everyman.

The Dark Knight Rises picks up eight years after the fateful events in The Dark Knight, where the Batman lost his love (Rachel Dawes) and also struck a Faustian deal with Police Commissioner Gordon where he disappeared from the public taking the rap for Harvey Dent's death. Bruce Wayne has become a recluse, only to be drawn out into the world when cat burglar Selina Kyles as Catwoman stirs his fancy.

Something is rotten in Gotham, though there is an uneasy peace prevalent, for Commissioner Gordon thinks it is the lull before the storm, and he is prophetically proved as masked terrorist Bane explodes into the scene literally. In a thrilling and audacious opening sequence, Nolan sets the tone by orchestrating a mid air kidnapping. The Batman trilogy deals closely with post 9/11 terrorism than any other movie- and here too the context is evident as Bane destroys first the stock exchange, then a football stadium and cuts off Gotham from the rest of the world, throwing it into complete anarchy. He might not be a jihadi and might speak with a cheerful English accent, but comes from a hell-hole in the subcontinent, and is clearly socialist- wants to turn over power to the people, obliterate the symbol of law and order, Batman, and bomb the living daylights out of Gotham. Like a well orchestrated symphony, Bane sets things in motion that create overwhelming odds for the Batman who now has the fight of his life on his hands, because for the first time he faces an adversary that is more powerful than him and staggeringly smart too. Broken, battered and bloodied, but like an All American hero, the Dark Knight rises up one final time for a fitting climax to the best superhero trilogy ever.

But Christopher Nolan is wrapping it all up here, so there are strands from the earlier movies woven in. To his credit, Nolan makes a brilliant crime drama playing out of a superhero movie elevating the genre to art with its entertainment quotient intact- grandiose and emotional at the same time. There are soul searching moments, as there is plenty of action along with super-cool gadgets. This movie is as much about ends as about beginnings. Bane is following what Ra's Al Ghul set out to do in Batman Begins- ie. In a world without redemption, destroy this corrupt society so that a new one can take its place. Alfred wishes Bruce Wayne to start a new life, even the Catwoman is running after for a clean slate. At the same time, The Dark Knight Rises explores recurring themes such a) As a villain instilling fear (Scarecrow through chemicals, Joker through random unpredictability, and Bane through brute force), b) "what you are in the dark"- Bruce always believes the people of Gotham are inherently good, while his adversaries think the opposite, and c) the Batman's desire to save the city at whatever cost.

Key highlight of the movie are powerhouse performances by an eclectic mix of actors from whom we expect, and some new surprises. Gary Oldman as Commissioner Gordon, Morgan Freeman as Lucius Fox, and Michael Caine as Alfred are series regulars that like wine kept getting better with age. The newcomers are scene stealers in their own right- Joseph Gordon- Levitt as rookie cop John "Robin" Blake brings earnestness and gravitas to every scene he is in- a working man hero. And as Selina Kyle/Catwoman, Anna Hathaway just blows apart all her previous wonderful performances by getting just the right amount of catty, ass-kicky and supreme sexy. Hers' is the best character in the movie- ethically and morally ambiguous, you really can't help but keep thinking what she will do next.

The movie's weaknesses are in a way linked to its strengths- this is a heavy and dark, nay, almost black film with an apocalyptic future that treads the fine line between entertainment and lessons in morality. And even with a 3 hr running time, too many characters do spoil the broth. Comparisons are inevitable, and this one lacks in intensity as compared to its predecessor. The Dark Knight made me squirm in my seat, and gave sleepless nights. I had kept playing myself on one of those ferries with THAT choice to make, and never found an answer. Any comic film is as good as its villain- Tom Hardy as Bane radiates intensity and presence, but now I realize how crucial Heath Ledger's Joker was to the epic-ness of The Dark Knight. To be fair, it is not right to expect Bane with his mask and one dimensional character to come up trumps when up against the insidious Joker, but I did wish for some more swagger and style from the only man that ever "broke the bat". Christian Bale as both Bruce Wayne/Batman looked tired throughout- might be what the script required but it kind of felt that he has had enough. He looked like a rubber stuffed toy in that overdone suit, and after building the sacrifice friendly legend of Batman in the earlier movies, shouldn't it all have ended in an explosion in the sea? Was the final happy moment necessary? Oh, but superheroes never die. Mildly disappointing, but maybe I am nitpicking, but only so because expectations were sky high.

To sum up, this is a near perfect effort from currently the best movie-maker in the world at the height of his powers. It is a fitting and satisfying end to a blockbuster series which will inspire future generations of movie makers. Easy to say film of the year and a must watch for all- 9/10

9.title: The Dark Bane Rises
9.content:
At first I couldn't wait until this film got out in theaters. I had seen every film of nolan and seeing that they keep getting better, I expected The Dark Knight rises to be his magnum opus. But I should have known better: how could someone, even a Christopher Nolan, outdo the Dark Knight.

Watching the movie I was blown away by the opening scene. For the second time Nolan has found an extraordinary and brilliant way the introduce the main villain Bane. And it must be said, Tom Hardy is as wicked and genius as Heath Ledger was. After having seen this movie multiple times I'm still amazed with what Hardy does with his face. Although he has besides his eyes no other facial means to express himself, he uses these eyes in a magnificent way.

As I was saying the opening scene and Bane in general is without doubt the greatest thing there is to mention concerning this movie. Because despite the fact that The Dark Knight Rises starts huge, the film quickly changes into a fantasy film that doesn't manage to keep up with its predecessors. It is painful to see just how many plot holes this movie has.

Why than the high rating? Simpley put: despite everything the last batman movie is still pretty amazing. As said is Tom Hardy his performance Oscar worthy, don't let yourself be fooled by the negative comments of his voice, the voice AND the accents are a perfect fit. Of course there is also the astonishing music score, I don't think there is any movie who has a more entertaining score than this trilogy. And at last you can't neglect the special effects which were once more pure art.

In short Nolan knows one more just how to combine the unrealistic Bane with the realistic character Bruce Wayne has become. Despite the fact that the movie loses its pace in the second part, the movie still has a better pace than most modern action movies.

9.title: Far too many holes
9.content:
I've just come back from the cinema after watching Batman - The Dark Knight Rises and am really surprised at the ratings this film has. I think it's IMDb's highest rated film ever now??? Wow, I actually think I have something wrong with my brain functionality if this is how people are rating films these days!!

Firstly, I am a huge fan of the previous 2 films but, this one left me feeling really confused as to what was going on. It seemed as though the film just jumped to new scenes and and you were meant to know what was going on?? For example. There was a mention of the worst prison ever, next thing you know Batman has been beat up and is in the prison. Quite feasible really?? Well no, not really. I'm not sure the exact location but I'm pretty sure it was somewhere like Russia, Siberia or Tibet. How on earth did they get there? They had a fight and he was there??? Then, this is even better, he manages to climb out of the hole to escape from the prison, after having his spine that was sticking out of his skin pushed back in. ha ha, yes this really does happen!! He escapes from the prison and then ends up back in New York, OK its Gotham, but we all know it meant to be NY. Did anyone see an explanation of how this happened? Im pretty sure these parts were filmed but left out of the edit. Which then poses the question, do they think we wont ask, and, are we stupid??

Also, I thought the acting throughout was very cheesy and quite badly acted to be quite honest. Some of Gary Oldman's lines and movements were ridiculous. I'm not blaming Gary, he is one of the greatest actors ever, I just thought it was as if the director just accepted the first take. Joseph Gordon-Levitt, who is also a fabulous actor. I just thought he sounded really false. It was probably due to the deep ridiculous accent that he was using. I don't know if that was him or the director doing it, but he really should of just used his own voice.

Anne Hathaway, Christian Bale, Tom Hardy & Marion Cotillard played their parts really well. Except when they were asked to do the ridiculous. I thought the star of the show was definitely Anne Hathaway. Visually the film is stunning, the action was great and I think that is the reason why it has been so highly rated. It was just the lack of flow and just expecting people to know whats going on because something was maybe suggested, or not at all, totally spoils the film. The the past few years I feel films are doing this. Surely films should be getting better with the amount of technology directors and film makers have at their disposal. But it seems to be the reverse. Is it down to the people who edit the film and put it all together at the end? This is where it seems the magic is lost in so many films these day. Like they have tried to throw everything in and the film loses its way??? I don't know if this is the case but it certainly seems this way... That said, this should surely should the blame of the director as its his vision that should make that final flow.

5 out of 10. Great action film spoiled by bad story line and more wholes than fishnet tights.

9.title: A Conclusion For The Ages
9.content:
Out of each and every superhero film ever made, 'The Dark Knight' trilogy truly stands as arguably the greatest of all time. With it's moderately-paced story, to its well-developed character adaptations...from its realistic flesh tone cinematography, to its phenomenal editing and special effects, TDK has earned its place among cinema's modern classics. With the conclusive 'The Dark Knight Rises', we see Batman/Bruce Wayne as he confronts his biggest (literally) challenge yet: An idealistic, and something of an intellectual, terrorist named Bane (played to perfection by Tom Hardy).

This film deals with purely modern themes, paramount of which is the growing income gap between the rich and the poor, and the animosity that is erupting among the middle-class. On a technical scale, I rate this movie about a 7 because the effects - while they were impressive and superbly executed - did not stand out from the tremendous acting and storytelling in the film. The film was masterfully shot and edited, as you might expect with Christopher Nolan at the helm. Having said all that, here are my predictions for this film's chances at some Oscar nominations:

Best Picture, Best Director, Best Supporting Actor (Tom Hardy), Best Supporting Actress (Marion Cotillard), Best Adapted Screenplay, Best Cinematography, Best Film Editing, Best Sound Mixing, Best Sound Editing.

9.title: The Storm has arrived.
9.content: This one is the Best of the trilogy. Christian is as usual awesome. this time we have stunning Anne Hathaway in action. Starts with plane destruction beautifully shot,goes in a slow pace but then starts with the ride..This time the villain BANE(Tom Hardy) really looks terrifying and brutal. Morgan freeman,Michael Caine, Gary Oldman are as usual.Joseph Gordon-Levitt got more role in this. Every second of 2nd half is gonna thrill you.and the suspense of Marion cottilard is very nice.You need to look the prequels Batman Begins and The Dark Knight as many times they had connected the old stories.I couldn't believe when i went 9 am show and saw the cinemastar housefull. I must say Hollywood cinemas are getting more space than ever. Thumbs up for Nolan.

9.title: Loved almost all of it, Nolan knows how to end an epic trilogy
9.content:
I was lucky enough to see The Dark Knight Rises in one of its earliest showings.In some great seats.

The Dark Knight Rises takes place eight years after the events of The Dark Knight and shows that Gotham is turned very peaceful with no organised crime due to Harvey Dents heroic lock ups. This means that Bruce Wayne no longer needs to become Batman, but Catwoman and Bane come along and force Bruce to return to his true Gotham colours.

Let me just say that i really enjoyed the first half of the movie, it was gritty, dark and very action packed. But i wasn't as impressed with the second half. Purely because i compared it to The Dark Knight to much. But i realise now that it all makes sense and comes together very well for a final act in Nolans trilogy. All the characters from the previous films were great as usual and even the new characters such as Catwoman, John Blake and Bane. All three actors/actress were great too. I especially love Bane because his whole image and voice was completely menacing and dark.

Overall i loved the film but i do still see more in The Dark Knight.

9.title: Astounding EPIC
9.content:
Firstly, a note to everybody who's watched it or planning to watch it soon, PLEASE DO NOT compare The Dark Knight Rises (TDKR) with The Dark Knight. The fact is that however epic TDK was, TDKR is quite different in terms of treatment and flavor. When Christopher Nolan announces that he's going to make an 'epic' ending to his Batman series, one can't help but raise hopes from the third and last installment. And Nolan has really lived up to his words.

TDKR is an epic in many ways, and a different kind of epic than TDK. Right from the superb opening sequence where we get to witness the gruesomeness in Bane's character, TDKR lets you right in to the story, scene by scene, (sometimes) rushing through various new characters as well as some old ones. In terms of story development, there's not a stone left unturned to take a good v/s evil storyline to such astounding level. The film does justification in every form to the comic book as well. Christian Bale is too good as the dark crusader of Gotham city. He plays Batman with certain smugness that George Clooney (Batman & Robin) and Val Kilmer (Batman Forever) could not when they had their chance in Tim Burton versions. Gary Oldman as Commissioner Gordon is in perfect form. Anne Hathaway is competent as Catwoman and has a character worth looking for. Morgan Freeman and Michael Caine are top notch as Lucius Fox and Alfred respectively, and they add some emotional quotient to the film. Joseph Gordon Lewitt has an important role, which one could guess from the trailers itself! Marion Cottilard as Miranda Tate (a new character) has a role to watch out for. Lastly, Bane is not the best villain so far, but has been earnestly played by Tom Hardy. Bane's presence is quite menacing throughout the movie. He may not be as smart as Joker, or may not have quirky dialogues like him, but is definitely scary enough. Liam Neeson as Ra's Al Ghul and Cillian Murphy as Dr. Crane have short and important roles. Although TDKR isn't completely devoid of loopholes too, but we can surely overlook those as a cinematic liberty. The film is paced so fast that even at a runtime of 2 hours 42 minutes, one feels as if he's been rushed through scenes and there should have been a little more character development (specially a little more attention could've been given to Catwoman). At some places Bane's voice isn't quite audible and same can be said for Batman too (or it may be the faulty sound systems at the theatre in which I was watching it). The movie finally brings to full circle the Batman legend, and tries to tie up all loose ends. The unexpected twist in the end seemed really surprising and disappointing to some extent. TDK's epicness lied in its solid characters, splendid acting and befitting dialogues, whereas TDKR's epicness is defined by its breathtaking scenes and action sequences, remarkable camera-work and cinematography, spectacular special effects and CGI and most of all an honest intention to give complete justice to the legend of Batman! My rating 4.5/5 A piece of advice – Do watch batman Begins, and The Dark Knight back to back before watching TDKR and chances are you'll enjoy this movie more!

9.title: A fabulous Rising of the silent guardian for one last time!
9.content:
In the first film of director Christopher Nolan's Batman series, Bruce Wayne's father asks him " Why do we fall Bruce? " and answers "So we can learn to pick ourselves up", these wise words form the theme for this grand finale . It is a completely satisfying and a respectable send off to the resurrected franchise.

When an incredible film like 'The dark knight' is a sequel, then the follow up movie would have expectations so high, that it's often never met. It would be extremely unfair to the director when media hypes up such a film and the paparazzi go on frenzy every time there is an outdoor shoot.The Dark knight rises clearly went through all of this. Yet, it manages to please the fans and unlike the 'forced third' of some franchises it feels like a vital continuation and a meaningful conclusion to the batman story.

Bruised and retired as the batman for seven years, Bruce Wayne limps through his manor and watches helplessly as the sassy thief Selina Kyle, steals his mother's pearls. There is a new embodiment of evil in Gotham called Bane who is equal amounts brain and brawn. This forces the Dark knight out of his retirement and plunges him into a dark, gritty and personal fight against anarchy. The past haunts him and the future is ominous while the present sees him separated from the handful of people who care for him. This is perhaps the most emotional and hard hitting Batman story that the Nolan Bother's clearly meant as a Frank Miller tribute.

The movie runs for a lengthy 2 hour 45 minutes but it never feels slow. Action scenes have the Nolan signature and is edge-of-the-seat guaranteed. New characters like Miranda Tate, Selina Kyle(never called the 'cat woman') and Detective John Blake are seamlessly integrated into Nolan's Gotham and although many would like to, it would be inane to compare Bane to the joker. Although both of them wanted mayhem, Joker stood as a benchmark for just how low and treacherous the mind of a modern man can fall while Bane stands for how far a deeply wounded man would go to seek warped justice through revulsion & vengeance. Although Hardy gives a fine presentation, he may not seem as good as Heath Ledger simply because his character was differently written.If nit picking for the sake of a balanced review must be done then the only flaw one can find is the pacing of movie was uneven at times.

All actors seem to be perfectly in tune with their characters; Christian Bale gives his best performance and a fitting swan song to the iconic character while Anne Hathaway shines the most amongst the new cast, leaving the audience wanting more of her screen time. Gary Oldman as Gordon, Michael Caine as Alfred and Freeman and Lucius Fox are some of the finest supporting roles both in terms of the deep characterization and their performance.

The Batman franchise is definitely up for a reboot in the near future but Chris Nolan's Batman would probably be the most realistic and gritty version ever. The Dark knight rises may not surpass its predecessor but it is still going to be a modern classic and that for a super-hero movie is a Plaudible feat.

9.title: An incredible conclusion to a defining trilogy.
9.content:
With this final part of his trilogy, Nolan has completed his grand vision for one of most important and long-standing superheroes ever created, Batman. His trilogy will go down as one of the greatest and coherent in cinematic history, and I try here not to be hyperbolic.

4 years it has been since The Dark Knight subverted what many expected of the superhero genre, blowing audiences away with its maturity, its scope and its grim, dark tone. Admittedly, Burton's early films were steeped in Gothic imagery, but Nolan's Batman has always been uncompromisingly dark and realistic in tone. Many superhero films have been released in The Dark Knight's wake, and all have failed to best Nolan's work, in my personal opinion. So did The Dark Knight Rises improve upon Nolan's near perfect sequel?

No.

Granted, TDKR is a fantastic film, a spectacular blockbuster with an almost unparalleled intelligence in its field. Rarely has a summer blockbuster challenged my mind to such a degree as TDKR. It is a serious film that asks serious questions, and undoubtedly carries a political message (regardless of what the cast and crew say to the media.) The production is flawless, the performances stellar and the pace was brisk and consistently engaging. The first hour was rather slow, but to my mind this was necessary in order to re- engage us with the characters and to build towards a mesmerising final hour. Michael Caine was particularly moving as Alfred, and this should go down as one of his strongest performances to date, and arguably the most impressive within the film. Hardy's 'Bane,' was another standout, providing a great physical performance. Every movement he made, every reaction and position, conveyed sheer ferocious power. His voice, however, seemed slightly disconnected from his actual actions, as if his voice was simply dubbed over his performance and he wasn't really saying it in that situation at all. Ultimately, this didn't truly ruin his performance for me, but it occasionally felt slightly jarring to see his neck and cheeks not move while he was supposedly talking. Hathaway was also excellent as Selina Kyle, as was Morgan Freeman as Lucius Fox. Christian Bale proves yet again what a truly excellent actor he is, providing audiences with the best Bruce Wayne ever committed to screen, his pain and anguish finally coming to the stoic surface. The film is incredible and absolutely worth seeing. But it has not, in my opinion, bested its predecessor.

The Dark Knight was truly ahead of its time. A mature, excellently crafted crime opus with a dark, sadistic edge. Ledger's 'Joker,' is one of the greatest villains ever put to screen, primarily because of Heath Ledger's stunning, Oscar-winning performance. The film tackled issues no other comic book film had ever even attempted to integrate, and in doing so elevated itself beyond the pale previously set by Batman Begins. I have not a bad word to write about The Dark Knight. And herein lies the problem; Nolan set the standards so highly that not even he could replicate such dizzying heights with his second sequel. Bane is not as engaging a villain as The Joker, TDKR had a slightly bloated running time and the plot of TDKR was occasionally, only slightly occasionally, a bit far-fetched and hard to follow. Expectations were so high for this film that it would have been impossible for Nolan to match them all. But he's done an amazing job of trying, TDKR may not have been the best of Nolan's trilogy, but is certainly an absolute masterpiece.

What Nolan has done with this film is come full circle. TDK didn't link to Batman Begins in many ways, but TDKR has integrated Batman Begins into its story to such a degree that there isn't an ounce of closure needed here, no exposition. TDKR is a magnificent conclusion, the trilogy as a whole is Nolan's undoubted masterpiece. It's sad to arrive at our final destination, but what a journey it's been.

9.title: A gripping and realistic film which misses out on few small aspects
9.content:
Christopher Nolan is back with the last chapter in the franchise and its grim action and fast paced, multi-layered storytelling which is mindblowingly good in terms of of how the story unfolds which is both real and compelling at the same time. Character development for the new characters is not brought out convincingly. The emotional aspect is brought out in a couple of scenes out of which the romance is sudden and not at all believable. The Bane character was built up well only to be let down in the end. But it just cannot be compared with Joker whose screen presence was amazing. The catwoman is a much more lively character and is very much part of the plot than just helping Batman. The batmobile just got a whole lot cooler and the 'Bat' a nice addition. Batman/Bruce Wayne is a lot more vulnerable and the movie concentrates more on the fate of Gotham city than being focused only upon Batman to save them. There isn't much connect with the characters and it feels like it doesn't matter whether they live or die which is both good and bad thing as it focuses our attention to the city as a whole rather than a few characters. The ending seems more like a logical conclusion to what has happened than being very cliché. And it will appeal to the masses. There are some epic dialogues/moments. The BGM complements the action without intruding too much. The 1st half is too good whereas the 2nd half is where many feel Nolan let us down. Do not go with too much expectations. It is a very good movie nevertheless.

Rating: 9/10

9.title: Soo good but I liked the joker version better
9.content: Just saw the movie in Malaysia even before US! and really liked it.. really nice... Christopher Nolan again does a great job. I must say that it could be shorter in time as there are some cliché US patriotic scenes - I don't mean there shouldn't be but there is more than enough of these scenes in every films - so he could more go with the details and time laps of the whole story. (no spoiler!) Finally I want to say that I cant remember the last time people clapping at the end of a movie till this one...

9.title: A bit of a mess, but still great......
9.content:
Well it is here. The conclusion to the best super hero trilogy ever. Period. Even though I still think that the best single superhero film ever made is Richard Donner's Superman: The Movie, the subsequent sequels and even the reboot attempt by Bryan Singer failed. Spider-man 2 also should be in the conversation as one of the best, but Christopher Nolan's trilogy is the most consistent in quality of the Big 3 superhero franchises. TDKR was inevitably going to suffer the comparisons to its predecessor because that film is as perfect of film of its as there could be. The new film is more ambitious than its 2 predecessors as is usually the case with 3 acts in a trilogy.

The film picks up 8 years after the events in TDK. I will not discuss any plot points, but all can say is that even though I don't think it is the masterpiece that TDK is, it is close. The biggest difference between the films is the villains. The villain in the new film is Bane, played by Tom Hardy. He is physically imposing but the fact that he has a mask doesn't help, you only see the actor's eyes. Also the fact that he speaks in an electronically assisted voice that at times is hard for the viewer to understand, takes away from his menace. With the villain lies the biggest difference between TDK and TDKR. The fact that Heath Ledger's performance as The Joker was one for the ages, That performance was unforgettable, and any actor's performance in the new film would fall short. The performances by everyone else in this film are uniformly good. I think that Christian Bale as Bruce Wayne/Batman deserves a lot of credit for creating a 3 dimensional, complex, heroic character. No one has been better in the role. Michael Caine as Alfred is great again, and has some of the best scenes in the trilogy here. I would love for him to get an Oscar nod. Anne Hathaway is very good as Selina Kyle/Catwoman. She is funny and sexy and has great chemistry with Bale. Everyone in the cast is good, Christopher Nolan is very good at choosing his actors.

The only other thing that I though about the film is that it did feel a little long. Both its predecessors were about 140 minutes, this film is 165 minutes and I think could have been cut a bit. The truth is that even though it isn't better that TDK, it is a terrific film. It is a grand, emotional ending to a a great Batman trilogy. I think that Christopher Nolan took the comic book film to a new level. He treated this story great intelligence and elegance.

It is in no way a disappointment.

Grade: A-

9.title: The Bat Rises.
9.content: Dark Knight Rises (2012): Dir: Christopher Nolan / Cast: Christian Bale, Tom Hardy, Anne Hathaway, Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Gary Oldman: Conclusion to the Christopher Nolan Batman trilogy with a title that echoes the need for good over evil. Nolan brilliantly concludes the trilogy on a note that will satisfy without a cliffhanger. Christian Bale is at his best here as Batman. Alter ego Bruce Wayne is secluded in his mansion hobbling about with a cane. He will meet his biggest challenge when receiving a beating and thrown in a prison that has a past of its own. Tom Hardy steals the film as villain Bane who apparently escaped this prison. With a face mask that renders him a Sean Connery type voice, he is a brutal dominant presence who delivers the ultimate physical challenge to Batman. He is set to destroy Gotham City with a massive bomb. Anne Hathaway is slick and sexy as Catwoman who attempts to steal a necklace during a party at the Wayne home. She is a conflicted character who benefits from the fact that Batman can see the other side of her character. Joseph Gordon-Levitt plays a young police investigator who grew up in an orphanage and has a future secret of his own. Gary Oldman returns as Commissioner Gordon who answers the press with regards to Harvey Dent but ends up in the hospital after narrowly escaping Bane. Marion Cotillard plays a wealthy contact who adds yet another interesting twist. Nolan once again strikes gold presenting the classic comic book hero in its best presentation. Visually captivating with ominous escapism that rises above and beyond. Score: 9 / 10

9.title: Excellent, a lot of quick fixes tho.
9.content:
okay, so i went into this film thinking there is no way that they can make a batman film, better than batman begins, or a comic book film better than the dark knight...and i was right.

Its very good, and Tom hardy's Bane is phenomenal, but a lot of things in this film annoyed me.

Magic Knee Brace, sending the entire police force into the sewers, (who is writing speeding tickets and keeping the peace). and how the hell does batman get from the middle of a desert to inside Gotham, when he has no money, no-one knows he is alive, and no-one is allowed in or out of Gotham.

9.title: A fine conclusions to Christopher Nolan's 'Batman' trilogy
9.content:
Eight years after the events portrayed in 'The Dark Knight' Gotham is a peaceful city but the Batman is still wanted for the killing of Harvey Dent and Bruce Wayne has become a recluse. Then one day cat burglar Selina Kyle breaks into Wayne mansion and as well as stealing his mother's pearls she takes a copy of Bruce's fingerprints. She gives these to an accomplice of masked criminal, Bane, an expelled member of the League of Shadows. Bane then launches an attack on the Stock Exchange where he uses Bruce's fingerprints to authorise the transfer of all of his wealth thus bankrupting him. He manages to find Bane but is defeated and left, severely injured in an apparently inescapable prison. It is only then that we learn Bane's ultimate plan; he seizes the core from a nuclear fusion reactor that Wayne Enterprises had developed and, after setting off explosives that cut Gotham off from the rest of the county, announces that he will detonate the device and kill everybody if anybody tries to leave. And so begins his reign of terror. The months pass and Bruce struggles back to health and manages to escape and return to Gotham; he is now up against the clock as it emerges that the bomb is unstable and will soon detonate whether triggered or not.

This film provides a fine conclusion to this trilogy. Bane is a suitable bad villain for this finale and his schemes were the most dastardly yet. He is definitely a human villain not a cartoonish super-villain. He has a good back story although, thanks to a late twist, some of what we are lead to believe isn't quite true. Then there is the fact that this is more a Bruce Wayne film than a Batman film; first he must overcome the death Rachel Dawes which kept him a recluse for eight years then after he finally becomes Batman again and is beaten by Bane he must heal physically and mentally before he can escape. We also have new characters Selina Kyle, an ambiguous thief who may ultimately prove to be a hero or a villain and policeman John Blake who rises from a young uniformed officer to help lead the fightback while Batman was not there. The cast does a fine job; notably returning cast members Christian Bale, Michael Caine and Gary Oldman. New cast members also impress; Tom Hardy is imposing as Bale; one can believe that he could beat Batman in a fight, Anne Hathaway is likable as Selina and Joseph Gordon-Levitt is good as Blake; the closest thing to an ordinary everyman of the film's main characters. There is plenty of spectacular action from an attention grabbing opening scene, through a series of chases and fights to an explosive conclusion. The end nicely wraps up the trilogy while still leaving things open for us to imagine what might happen next. Overall I'm sure fans of the series will enjoy this; I'd certainly recommend the first two films first though.

9.title: Not Nolan's best movie but still better than many
9.content: The dark knight rises was full of excitement and emotion and it did deliver what Nolan promised. but the reason I'm giving it a 9star and not 10 was the storyline. i think it wasn't what you really expected of Nolan, for example, in the movie you see bane making speeches with his great voice, you see him take over a city and have an army, but then suddenly at the end you realize that he was nothing but a mercenary who did Miranda's dirty work and then just ends by cat woman. i was kind of let down by that because i didn't expect that from his greatest enemy. another great mistake of Nolan's was that he tried to come up with a story that not only concludes his trilogy but concludes batman and he really focused on this part, instead he should've come up with a story that ends his trilogy but not batman because superheros never end that's one of their qualities. all in all despite these mistakes he did a really good job on a story that ends batman (but not Bruce Wayne),i think its one of the hardest things a writer can do and still be able to make it turn out really cool.

9.title: Best Batman film ever and best film of the year thus far.
9.content:
Today, I watched one of the greatest films I've ever seen in my life. This film is called 'The Dark Knight Rises'.

Here's the official synopsis of TDKR: "It has been eight years since Batman vanished into the night, turning, in that instant, from hero to fugitive. Assuming the blame for the death of D.A. Harvey Dent, the Dark Knight sacrificed everything for what he and Commissioner Gordon both hoped was the greater good. For a time the lie worked, as criminal activity in Gotham City was crushed under the weight of the anti-crime Dent Act. But everything will change with the arrival of a cunning cat burglar with a mysterious agenda. Far more dangerous, however, is the emergence of Bane, a masked terrorist whose ruthless plans for Gotham drive Bruce out of his self-imposed exile. But even if he dons the cape and cowl again, Batman may be no match for Bane."

Now, onto my review, some minor spoilers ahead though:

Story: The Dark Knight Rises started as a slightly slow paced film and quite frankly I got a little bored but as it progresses the pacing became much better. Even though boredom may occur at the first act of the film, you must not waste even a minute of watching this for as every second and minute is essential to the films continuity.

Acting: The acting in this film is just superb, everybody in the cast did a stellar and unforgettable performance, but the one who really shines in this awesome spectacle is Anne Hathaway and Michael Caine, every lines delivered, every action made, just wow! Christian Bale also did great and for me this is his best portrayal of the billionaire playboy and caped crusader. Tom Hardy was a menacing Bane but let's face it, The Joker is still the best villain. Joseph Gordon-Levitt plays a good ally of Batman and also puts on a great performance. Gary Oldman, same as before, perfect casting for Jim Gordon. Marion Cotillard also puts on a good performance but a forgettable one (for me). Morgan Freeman and Matthew Modine, even though only a short screen time also showed a good performance.

Soundtrack: I thought Hans Zimmer will not be able to top himself after 'The Dark Knight' but he did top himself in this one, the soundtracks was just mesmerizing, haunting and memorable. He is definitely one of the best working composers today.

Cinematography: One word. Awesome. Wally has never been this good, every shot is just perfect.

Direction: Chris Nolan did it again and delivered not only one of the most memorable Batman film but he also gave us one of the most memorable films ever that will be talked about for the years to come. Nolan gave it his all, and in my opinion this the best film that he ever made.

Final Verdict: The Dark Knight Rises is the perfect way to end a trilogy. A 2 hour and 45 minutes of sheer awesomeness and utter brilliance, all from the mind of a master filmmaker (well for me anyways) Christopher Nolan. For me this is the best film in the trilogy and epic is the perfect word to describe this film. This is much more action-packed than all the other Bat-films. I am sure to catch this one again on theaters. 10/10 A brilliant masterpiece by Christopher Nolan.

My top 5 comic book movies: 1. The Dark Knight Rises 2. Watchmen 3. The Dark Knight 4. The Avengers 5. Batman Begins

P.S. My condolences to the families of the people involved in the shooting at Colorado. May God bless their souls.

9.title: The Big Daddy of all Superhero Movies is finally upon us....
9.content: After being fortunate enough to watch an advanced preview screening, I can safely say that.............................. TDKR is a fitting finale and a grand conclusion to the epic trilogy of the Batman series, as envisaged by Christopher Nolan, who definitely cements his place as one of the best directors of the modern generation with his trademark "relentlessly intense storyline, utterly chaotic dystopian society riddled with totalitarian government & cyber-genetic technologies, stark and bleak portrayal of human pessimism and misanthropic attitude as well as superbly spectacular big-budget Hollywood set-pieces of massive destruction, chaos, catastrophe and pandemonium." The real world threats of global terrorism, political anarchy and economic instability make deep incursions into the cinematic comic book domain in TDKR. Even though indispensably it lacks an element as unique as Heath Ledger's immortal and memorable turn in "The Dark Knight", it compensates for that by being fully enveloping and at times unnerving in a relevant way one would never have imagined. The director daringly pushes the credibility of a Gotham City besieged by nuclear-armed revolutionaries to such an extent that it momentarily seems absurd for a guy in a costume who refuses to kill people, unmasked and debilitated, emotionally shattered and physically drained, leading the life of a retired recluse, to conceivably show up to save the day but due to the laconic, succinct yet lucid storyline, manages to do so impeccably and masterfully. As before, the production values are opulent and sensational; nothing short of the highest praise can be lavished on the work of the production designers, The only conspicuous faux pas is a big continuity gaffe that has the raid on the Stock Exchange take place during the day but the subsequent getaway chase unfold at night. While Some of the action scenes have something of a "deja-vu", familiar feel the others are fresh and brilliantly rendered, manifesting the brilliant visual spectacle of epic proportions. Despite the high level of suspension of disbelief, dark tone and sometimes lugubrious approach, this is a finely crafted and prudently structured plot, providing just about sufficient and adequate time for character development, tying all the knots from the previous iterations & installments, yet avoiding UN-necessary confusions and myopic plot twists, never allowing levity to intrude the conflicted, sinister and flawed outlook of the principal characters. The stellar performance by the entire cast and the dramatic, haunting background score alleviates and effortlessly transforms the sheer scope of Nolan's vision – with emotion and spectacle thundering across the screen – for its entire running time of nearly 3 hours. Most importantly, TDKR unequivocally manages to achieve the impossible, which is to bring a cherished cinematic chapter to a close, yet manage to leave the fans feeling neither desolate nor forlorn but essentially cheerful, one steeped enough in self-contained mythology to reward hard-core fans while giving less invested viewers a rousing, adroitly executed piece of popcorn entertainment. In the end, this is a sequel that not only succeeds but easily surpasses the enormous weight of hyped-up lofty expectations built ridiculously high by fan culture and savvy marketing. TDKR transcendence the art of movie-making into an entirely different level, that had been hitherto unseen and unheard of previously in any kind of super-hero, comic-book adaptations to the big screen till date. This Brilliant and Exemplary exercise of groundbreaking accomplishment in movie-making must not be missed by any movie buffs, let alone "Batman affectionados". 10/10.

It does come close to being too contrived, but if it weren't, it'd be a simple linear, no frills, run-of-the-mill plot.

What I noticed was the themes from the graphic novels like "The Dark Knight Returns", "No Man's Land", and the "Knightfall" books. Also, don't expect the gadgets to be so prominent here. This one goes for raw, visceral action. Even a Batman in daylight! If you pay close attention, you can pick up the subtle and not so subtle shout-outs to the Dark Knight universe.

A robust, and satiating finale to a venerable character and trilogy.

9.title: The epic conclusion of Christopher Nolan's Trilogy
9.content:
"Batman: The Beginning" has set a new tone for the narration of stories from the world of comics. Realistic, gloomy and dynamic. The continuation of the Batman story in The Dark Knight turned out to be much more spectacular than the original 2005 picture thanks to the high-quality work of the entire film crew and a very vivid image of the antagonists: Joker and Two-Face. Such a success is certainly difficult to repeat, but the final part of Nolan's trilogy "The Dark Knight Rises" diligently does it.

The final film, it should be noted, came out quite long, closely approaching the mark of 2 hours and 45 minutes. Whatever this story was, it turned out to be difficult to watch it for so long. The whole film does not leave the feeling that Nolan took this step consciously, trying to fully reveal the characters, as well as effectively finish the narrative about the defenders of Gotham, a city that was plunged into the darkness of violence and lawlessness on a very large scale. In principle, from the point of view of scale, the film pulls on such timing, taking a new peak for itself and demonstrating that Gotham and its inhabitants are in a situation that they have never experienced before.

Bruce Wayne's life seemed to stop after the events of the second film. The creators skillfully show us from the very first frames that Bats retired, became decrepit, became a recluse. The events of The Dark Knight seriously affected Batman, and he never seems to have recovered from them. The atmosphere of the work is literally saturated with apathy, gray colors, oppressive atmosphere. The last challenge for Batman - probably the biggest threat to the Bat-Man and to the entire metropolis is in the person of Bane, who raises the stakes much higher than his predecessors Ras al Ghul and the Joker. But after watching the picture, there is still a feeling that this large-scale project was a success for Nolan an order of magnitude worse than the previous one, where the Oscar-winning Heath Ledger shone so. Actor Tom Hardy failed to present his hero so colorfully, although here, I think, the problem is already in the script and the character himself.

Bane is a colorful enemy of Batman, a creature, as if not even a person, who will definitely test the strength of not only the mind of the protagonist, but also his body. This is a new challenge for the protagonist, who, it seems to me, no longer believes that he can cope with the enemy. Batman is hard not only because he is already tired of life and losses in his superhero role. Batman has aged, has become haggard, does not have such an important support and motivator in the person of his butler Alfred Pennyworth. Michael Caine's performance in this film is very memorable. Despite the man's short screen time, his words, messages, requests and pleas to Bruce sit in the depths of his soul and are remembered for a long time even years after viewing. Kane is a gorgeous actor who so colorfully conveys to us the image of a tired man who had to wait with horror every night for many years that Batman might not return from his next battle with crime. At the same time, it is important to note Kane's dubbing. The voice actor coped perfectly, subtly immersing Russian viewers in all the pains of Alfred's soul.

As for Tom Hardy, he is a good actor who had to not only transform physically globally for the sake of this role, but also play essentially only with his eyes and voice, since his face is hidden under a mask. On the one hand, this mask gives it colorfulness, highlighting just the eyes of the character, and, on the other hand, it significantly complicates the game, because you need to be able to convey various emotions through the look. Also, as before, the dubbing actor Ilya Isaev, whose voice is always penetrating and strong, is on top. Tom Hardy's Bane is a real test for both Batman and the viewer. It is literally a machine for destroying everything around. He and his squad plunge Gotham into an abyss from which there seems to be no way out.

Other heroes are also good: Lucius Fox, Catwoman, Miranda Tate, John Blake, James Gordon. Each of the characters is intelligently played by cool actors. Through their actions and dialogues, we see how Gotham itself is revealed, which, no matter how hard anyone tries, is also going through its worst times. And the last struggle of people for their lives, for their hometown is an evolution, an important step, a manifesto - you can call it whatever you want - for their freedom from tyranny and constant crime.

All the dots over the "I" will be placed here, the director will say everything he wanted within the framework of the completed trilogy. Nolan says goodbye to the franchise well, leaving behind a great legacy - a series of films about an ordinary man who was ready to lay his life on the altar of victory in order to finally show people that they can be free and become who they so want to be.

9 out of 10.

9.title: An incredible finale
9.content:
In its own right, The Dark Knight Rises is a fantastic story about hope and defining heroism, a gripping crime thriller and another great adaptation of the beloved Batman comics. As a conclusion to Nolan's Dark Knight trilogy and a continuation of its stellar second installment, however, the film absolutely soars.

Firstly, in terms of spectacle, The Dark Knight Rises is at a high. The action scenes - in typical Nolan style - mix CGI with unbelievable practical effects, making every second thrilling to see what stunt will be pulled next. In melee combat, the choreography is all around solid and viseral when it comes the brawls between...

Batman and Bane. The undeniable highlights of the film. Both Christian Bale and Tom Hardy give amazing performances as two fighters struggling to overcome goofy voices, and both born into darkness but sent down polar opposite paths. Where Bruce Wayne's experience of hitting rock bottom inspired him to persevere upwards and hold out hope for the people of Gotham, Bane's rejection by Ra'as Al Ghul led him to give up hope, letting the darkness mould him into the ruthless mercenary we see in the film. Hardy's physicality and the character's twisted view on the concept of pain make Bane an undeniably imposing figure, a real threat to an increasingly weary Batman and a test of his resolve after the Joker's siege of Gotham. As for Batman, the film perfectly portrays the character's pure determination despite everything standing against him and seemingly all having been lost. The ending serves as a satisfying send-off to Bale's run as the Caped Crusader as well as the trilogy as a whole.

Inkeeping with its predecessors, Jonathan and Christopher Nolan's dialogue is Batarang-sharp, expertly using subtext to convey character and leaving no line to be deemed unimportant. As a result, the 164 minute film never seems to drag.

The Dark Knight Rises also boasts a top-notch supporting cast: industry veterans Michael Caine, Morgan Freeman and Gary Oldman all ace their performances. Newcomer to the trilogy Anne Hathaway, playing Selina Kyle aka Catwoman, makes the character come off as cunning and witty but passionate, and Joseph Gordon-Levitt plays a likeable and strong-willed police officer with great chemistry with Bruce Wayne.

Overall, a terrific end to a terrific trilogy on par with even the commonly regarded best of the best, The Dark Knight. Would recommend to comic book, crime thriller and Batman fans.

9.title: Super Good Film. A Must Watch for All
9.content:
DARK KNIGHT RISES REVIEW

The Dark Knight Rises is a continuation of the story of Batman (Christian Bale). It is a film filled with redemption. It has been 8 years since any one has seen or heard from Batman because he has taken the fall for Harvey Dent's death. Commissioner Gordon (Gary Oldman) is about to resign and wants to free Batman from the lies that have held him down and to what Bruce Wayne has become, but he decides against it. Gordon is captured by Bane (Tom Hardy) and a cat burglar Selina (Anne Hathaway) steals Bruce Wayne's fingerprints. Bruce becomes bankrupt and Gordon is saved by Officer John Blake (Joseph-Gordon Levitt). This cause of events leads Bruce to turn over his company to Miranda Tate (Marion Cotillard). Bane has plans to destroy Gotham as Ra's al Ghul's intentions were. After Bane declares he will follow out al Ghul's plans, he critically injures Bruce and leaves him in a prison underground. Bane then lures the police department underground and collapses the exits. This is when Bane takes control of Gotham and initiates a revolution. Bruce eventually breaks out of the prison and returns to Gotham as Batman to save the city.

There are many thematic ideas that are portrayed in this film. Redemption is by far one of the strongest. Each character in the film is on the road to redemption, may it be good or evil. From Miranda Tate to Bruce Wayne, each character is determined to redeem themselves or someone close to them. Justice is always a popular thematic idea when it comes to any superhero/villain movie. Justice must be served and the good will prevail. This is evident in this film. It is evident with Bruce Wayne himself, as Batman, Police Commissioner Gordon, and even down to John Blake. After all, Bruce Wayne is only an orphan because of the brutal murderers of his parents. Politics is also a thematic idea present in this film, the rise and fall of the Gotham City politicians and police officers shows this. This film is similar to Sin City with its thematic ideas of redemption, justice and the fight between good and evil. It is ultimately better than Sin City though.

Many of the scenes in The Dark Knight Rises use low- lighting to make the scenes more intense and scary. The most notable motif would the symbol of Batman. The light has been out for eight years that calls out this super-hero but it is still a prominent symbol throughout the film.

The Dark Knight Rises is an epic Batman film that is filled with characters trying to redeem themselves and what is rightfully theirs.

9.title: As a spectacle: it's a 10/10. But not a good script.
9.content:
As far as the Christopher Nolan Batman trilogy; Batman Begins has great writing but terrible action. The Dark Knight has superb writing and the action was some of the best I've ever seen. The Dark Knight Rises has action on par with its predecessor but the writing is not just bad, it's laughably bad!

Take the opening scene for example, Bane and his men are picked up by some 'smart professionals'. Only for Bane and his goons to crash the plane and kill almost everyone. The sound and visuals really felt like a plane hijacking. But the circumstances of how this came to be is just...not good.

I'm not the first to bring up the part where Gordon sends (his words, not mine) every cop in the city down into the dim, crammed sewers to supposedly getting Bane and his goons. It not only makes no sense, it's impractical. Say Gotham city was NYC with a combined population of 8,000,000 and a combined police force of 40,000 police officers. That's 40,000 people being shoved underground, how in the hell is that gonna help anyone?

This may be an unpopular opinion, but it's honest; I actually really like Bane. He's threatening, looks gigantic despite Tom Hardy being only 5'11", and if his plan was a bit less convoluted, he'd be a worthy successor to the legendary Heath Ledger's Joker.

The Dark Knight Rises did the same mistake Spider-Man 3 (2007) made, throw in so many subplots that it feels like watching two different uninteresting plot lines rather than one big plot. If Bane started the movie throwing Bruce in prison and the entire movie was him training and truly becoming Batman again. But the entire first 3rd of this film is setting up many subplots that actively hurt the pacing with 'Robin' and Catwoman.

If it had just cut to black right after Alfred nods at the camera, the ending would've been a LOT better. But there's a cut to Bruce nodding back at that exact same cafe, Blake finding the Batcave.

Was it just against the law to make a comic book film in the 2010's and not have it tease a sequel? I feel like Warner Bros got their hands way too involved in the development.

Best thing I can say about this is I actually really like it despite my flaws with it. I'd much rather watch the worst of Christopher Nolan than the best of Micheal Bay any day.

It's still a 9/10 and still a good ending to a trilogy.

9.title: A perfect and stunning conclusion to Nolan's BATMAN Trilogy
9.content:
After The Dark Knight, a sequel to both Batman Begins and The Dark Knight was in the works, but had to go through some intense re-writing due to the tragic and unexpected death of Heath Ledger. The Joker was originally scheduled to appear in this film, which is why Batman left him hanging on the building at the end of THE DARK KNIGHT and his fate is left a mystery. The film featured the villains Bane and Selina Kyle / Catwoman and our new heroes, Miranda Tate / Talia al Guhl and John Blake.

The release of this film was widely anticipated by fans and critics and the film received widespread acclaim and was a huge success at the box office, going on to outgross it's predecessor and become the eleventh-highest-grossing film of all time grossing over a billion dollars. The film was titled The Dark Knight Rises and it was released on July 20, 2012.

The story takes place eight years after Harvey Dent's death. Feeling guilty for covering up Dent's crimes, Police Comissioner James Gordon writes a speech confessing the truth, but decides not to use it. Batman has disappeared and Bruce Wayne is in retirement, but he is once again called to become Batman again and faces a new foe: Bane, a powerful villain who breaks Batman's back in the first fight. But he is able to recover after months of re-training and stops Bane from destroying Gotham, who plans to blow up Gotham into ashes. Batman gets help from John Blake, Selina Kyle / Catwoman, Lucius Fox and Miranda Tate and is able to take out Bane.

The story is okay. Christopher Nolan and his brother wrote one hell of a story using inspiration from a few of the comic books. The film's run time is over three hours long (165 minutes) and it is really long and I saw the whole movie, but there's more to this film.

The action is just top-notch and I saw this movie for the first time and I just wanted to cry when Bane hit Batman in the back and also, at the end when Batman died in the explosion, but I found out that he wasn't really dead. The final fight between Batman and Bane at the end of the film was amazing, and to have Catwoman help him was really good.

I think the only main criticism and issue that I have with THE DARK KNIGHT RISES is when Batman and Bane first fight. There's no music playing during the film and all you hear is the punches and grunting. Also, the other issue is when Bane breaks Batman's back. I found myself saying, "Why would Bane do such a crazy thing to Batman?" and then I could not come up with a simple answer for the question.

That part was overkill for me because I was expecting Batman to take out Bane easily, but because Bane is more stronger than Batman, he really broke his back and that is the worst thing you can do to Batman.

The acting is okay. Christian Bale makes a final appearance as Batman / Bruce Wayne and he gives a good decent performance. Michael Caine is emotionally powerfully as Alfred Pennyworth. Gary Oldman is great once again as Comissioner James Gordon. Marion Cotillard as Miranda Tate / Talia al Guhl was really fun to watch, but when she started acting evil, that is when I said, "Really?". Morgan Freeman as Lucius Fox, does a decent job as well in this film. Anne Hathaway is hot as Catwoman / Selina Kyle. When I first saw this, I was like, "She's gonna nail this part." And she did.

Joseph Gordon-Levitt as John Blake is really cool and he plays a great part and gives me one hell of a performance. The last person to mention is Tom Hardy as Bane, and I have to admit, he was confusing to hear talk, because all of his lines of dialogue sound like it was muffled, but I could really hear what he was saying once I saw this for a second time.

The music and visuals are just amazing and fantastic, especially the music composed by Hans Zimmer. I was sad that James Newton Howard did not return with Zimmer to compose the music for this film, but Hans Zimmer did a great job. The visuals are impressive and it was a wise to chose for Nolan to shoot this movie entirely in IMAX.

Overall, with THE DARK KNIGHT RISES, I think it's really cool and I like and hate it at the same time. Christopher Nolan concludes his Batman trilogy with a bang! I give it a 9.3 out of 10, while some of the movie can drag after a few minutes, I still love this movie and Christopher Nolan's trilogy in total. The film is not the best Batman film ever, but it could have been a hell of a lot worse, but it does not become worse. It is definitely one of the best films of 2012 and the second movie based on a DC Comics character to gross over $1 billion worldwide.

9.title: A perfect ending to a PERFECT TRILOGY!
9.content:
While it may not top The Dark Knight, The Dark Knight Rises is still a close second to me. A great ending to Christopher Nolan's take on Batman and he ended it in spectacular fashion.

Some might think that The Dark Knight Rises is the weakest film in the trilogy. I understand why people didn't think that this movie was better than The Dark Knight, like some of the convinces and circumstances that seem contrived (for example sending all of the police officers down into the sewers to smoke out Bane and his henchman), but I feel that people didn't get the point about why all of the police officers were sent down into the sewers. It was because it was a policy part of the Dent Act to bring peace into Gotham City. With Batman' back broken, and all of his armoury in the hands of Bane, Bane sees the faults of the Dent Act and uses them to his advantage. His plan was to make the people of Gotham think that their is hope still about despite a massive nuclear bomb on the knifes edge of blowing up, and Batman and the police no longer around to save the city.

Hope is one of the main themes of the movie. And I think it's a real shame that people don't see The Dark Knight Rises that way, especially since they're coming off the high heels of The Dark Knight. And Anne Hathaway as Catwoman is a real treat in the movie, especially during the climax when she gets to drive the Bat-pod. A match made in heaven for me.

Overall though, I personally think The Dark Knight Rises is the second best film of the trilogy and up there as one of my personal favourite films made by Christopher Nolan. It's a perfect ending to a great character in Bruce Wayne, a perfect send off to an outstanding trilogy of films that in my eyes are inspirations for me growing up as a young filmmaker. 9/10!!

9.title: The Dark Knight Rises: A Movie that Rises Over Other Superhero Films
9.content: When you think of every type of superhero movie there are a couple of things come to mind. First, there is a superhero that everybody loves, who struggles throughout the film, but overcomes his weaknesses at the end of the film. There is a villain that has a very troubled past that wants revenge or payback for the unfair treatment or environment that he or she grew up in. Lastly, the superhero saves the day, gets the girl and everybody is happy. The Dark Knight Rises follows this exact generic superhero plotline, but at the same time it does not. The Dark Knight Rises is a classic superhero movie that everybody loves, but at the same time differs from all others in its class and is a timeless film. The Dark Knight Rises follows the dark nature of an unlikely hero, Batman. The movie starts off by focusing on the already deceased character of Harvey Dent, the city of Gotham's supposed hero. Batman has gone rogue. However news of a powerful new villain, Bane, starts to come to light. He fights Bane, who has set up a base underneath the city. Bane then proceeds to attack the Gotham stock exchange, leaving Wayne and the Batman bankrupt. He then traps all the policemen in Gotham underground, holds the entire city hostage with a bomb, and releases prisoners caught by Harvey Dent to wreak havoc on a policeless city. Batman is then left to save the city of Gotham before the bomb goes off and all is lost. The Dark Knight Rises was a phenomenal film and in my personal opinion deserves a rating of 9 out of 10. However, there were a few minor flaws that I would like to point out. First, the costumes were very poorly made. Batman and Catwoman's outfits almost looked like something that you buy at Party City for twenty dollars. Next, the plot was a little confusing at times. While I said that this movie had a plot line that is comparable to literally any superhero movie (Superman, Spiderman, Ironman, you name it the list goes on), the plot was extremely complex and at times, and very had to follow. This is especially true if you had not seen any of the previous movies. However for some, this is not a negative at all. The sense of time in the movie is confusing at times as well. The audience is left wondering how much time has passed between certain scenes of movies and really, how much time has elapsed in total in the movie. Finally, the ending was a little lackluster. The villain was beaten a little too easily and the audience was left with some questions and cliff hangers. With all that being said, there were numerous more positives to the movie than negatives. First off, like I said before, the plot is the generic superhero plot line that everybody loves, except so perfectly manipulated with plot twists and connections to past films and flashbacks that it is unlike any other superhero movie. The build up that really highlighted how difficult and dark of a life that superheroes can have added a sense of realism that almost every viewer can relate to. This also contributed to a major theme that all of the batman movies have: Nobody lives a perfectly happy life, even the most powerful and influential people in today's society. To further push this message to the audience, director Christopher Nolan selected the perfect actor. There could not be a more perfect actor for Batman than Christian Bale. He perfectly displays how a superhero's life can never be normal because they are conflicted with a dark past and burdened with always feeling the need to save the city. Finally, the final battle scene is everything that a fan of action movies could ever want. The build up led to an all out brawl of good versus bad. The intensity and action packed final battle is so satisfying and cool to watch there are practically no words to describe it. There are so many more positives that you have to see it with your own two eyes to really experience the how great it actually is. All in all, this movie is definitely worth the watch. It is the perfect balance of being a typical superhero movie, while also being so different than others that it almost makes it the perfect movie. In my personal opinion, there should be no varying opinions with this movie. It truly is a movie that "rises" above all others.

9.title: Outstanding Batman Action at the Box Office!!
9.content: The Dark Knight Rises is perhaps the second greatest Batman movie of all-time, only second to Christopher Nolan's The Dark Knight in this reviewer's mind!! This movie has everything in its, the answer to all of the questions that have been building up in Nolan's Batman trilogy, outstanding action, more hero-villain drama and intrigue, and an ending that just makes you feel good!! Picking right up where The Dark Knight left off with the death of Gotham City District Attorney Harvey Dent, Police Commissioner Gordon has to continue to spin to the public that Dent is a good man despite the fact that he went on a bit of a killing spree at the end of the last movie after the death of his fiancée in order to keep convictions in place. Meanwhile, Batman has to contend with a new menace to Gotham society in Bane, played wonderfully by Tom Hardy (Venom) who is on a mission to take over Gotham and hold it hostage under the guise of a neutron bomb!! There are action and fight scenes galore between Batman and Bane that keep you tied to your screen, and Catwoman (Anne Hathaway) is now introduced to the Nolan Batman trilogy!! Hathaway is outstanding as Selina Kyle, charming and smart and tough as nails as you would expect out of Catwoman!! Like with Catwomen before her, she does team up with Batman when it is to her advantage and does fight side by side with the Caped Crusader in memorable scenes that just add to the greatness of this film! Needless to say Christian Bale (Ford vs Ferrari) is outstanding as Batman/Bruce Wayne and Gary Oldman and Michael Caine put in nice performances as Commissioner Gordon and Alfred the butler respectively. There are also new players to the all-star cast of The Dark Knight Rises including Joseph Gordon-Levitt who plays a cop named Blake but actually plays more of a realistic Robin. Turns out, in the end, his legal first name is Robin in the movie!! Also appearing in the film is French actress Marion Cotillard who plays Miranda - a bit of a two sided figure who is more importantly the daughter of Ra's al Ghul!! Last but certainly not least is Morgan Freeman who plays Fox the steady tech support man to Batman throughout Nolan's Batman trilogy. An epic conclusion, outstanding acting, terrific action scenes, outstanding costuming, great soundtrack, a realistic storyline, great writing, and a terrific sense of fun have me giving The Dark Knight Rises my rare 9 out of 10 stars!!
