10.title: The phenomenal completion of a trilogy as close to perfect as we're ever likely to see.
10.content:
He did. It rocks! The Dark Knight Rises is my third ten-star film of the year.

There was a possibility and a fear that after the unique, blistering start to the trilogy and the mind-blowing, Oscar-winning follow-up, the third installment would dip. Not even The Godfather series managed three films of equal importance, impact and quality but in The Dark Knight Rises Christopher Nolan has given us a trinity of near perfection.

This final offering from the team that reinvented superheroes with Batman Begins in 2005 and produced a staggering, thrilling and at times shocking sequel in The Dark Knight in 2008 has closed the book in majestic style and, as the finest directors do, Nolan has left us wanting more. However, we don't always get what we want and in this case, maybe that's a good thing. Why risk devaluing perfection with a shoddy, money-grabbing bolt on? The Dark Knight Rises sees Gotham in a state of confidence amid mumblings that the absent Batman is neither needed nor really missed after eight years of self-imposed exile. Bruce Wayne has isolated himself from the world, his reputation in tatters having taking the blame for Harvey Dent's demise, his empire is close to financial ruin and his costume of choice is a now a silk dressing gown, an unkempt mass of facial hair and a miserable scowl. Then he catches the delectable Selina Kyle burgling his home and all hell breaks lose with the emergence of Bane Nolan is confident enough in his product and team to take his time in setting the scene, building the pace and drawing our emotional involvement. For those who saw the trailer, there is an expectation of mortality, though we hope desperately that he has misled us, and there is little risk of us not being absorbed in the emotional tangle of Wayne's life and the decisions he must make.

The Dark Knight Rises harks back to the first installment but there is never an impression of retreading old ground or rehashing plot lines. This is an entirely new beast and what Nolan unleashes on us is enthralling, engrossing and inventive while remaining comfortably familiar. We care about Wayne and his alter ego because we've travelled with him. Like the reinvented Bond in Casino Royale and The Quantum of Solace, we've felt his pain and understood how his mind works. Why? Because Christian Bale is one of the finest actors of his generation and doesn't merely don a cowl and play a part, he inhabits the man and embraces the yin and yang of altruism and monstrousness that makes him who he is.

It is obvious to focus on Bale because without him Batman, the film and the character, just wouldn't work. But again Nolan has cast his ensemble with perfection. While Bane is not as spectacular as The Joker and Tom Hardy, though superb, will not emulate Heath Ledger and win an Oscar, he is an expansive villain who thrills and chills and who just might come on top. Beyond Hardy it is a delight to watch Marion Cotillard's beautiful, steely Miranda and, of course, the presence of Gary Oldman, Morgan Freeman and Michael Caine reprising their roles is as welcome as it is rewarding. Even at 164 minutes, The Dark Knight Rises feels too brief to explore the lives of Gordon, Fox and Alfred as deeply as we would like, but that is also an asset as we're never allowed to be complacent in the company of the familiar allies.

And then there is the cat.

In Batman Returns, Michelle Pfeiffer stole the show, seized our hearts and adorned our bedroom walls as the oh-so-sensual Catwoman in her stitched-in cat suit. Could Anne Hathaway come close to the impact Pfeiffer had on us? Emphatically, yes! Hathaway gives us a very different Cat and steals both the crown and the hearts of a new generation. Though never actually referred to as 'Catwoman' she leaves us in no doubt as to who she is and how the world should revolve around her. Hathaway exudes sexuality without needing to purr and is feisty, stubborn and naughty enough to step out of the Bat's shadow and for us to clamour for more. And they way we are shown exactly who she is, with the revealing of her ears, is a subtle act of class.

Jonathon and Christopher Nolan have written yet another screenplay that is taut and thrilling without a single wasted or superfluous line. The pace is varied enough to allow us time to enjoy the odd quip and occasional surprise without ever permitting us to wallow and admire the scenery before it whips across to a new scene or snaps in a different direction.

The sets, effects, costumes and machines are darkly dazzling as we've come to expect and time doesn't allow for me to elucidate as expansively as they deserve. Let's just say this is a film where one Batmobile isn't enough.

The Dark Knight Rises is not just a good film; it's an excellent film and it completes a trilogy as close to perfect as we're ever likely to see.

For more reviews from The Squiss subscribe to my blog at www.thesquiss.co.uk

10.title: Nolan shows the scope of his genius.
10.content: Bare with me, this is my first movie review. I figured what better film to get started with than the epic conclusion to the Dark Knight Trilogy, and indeed it is epic. Nolan's elaborate storyline is acted out beautifully by the usual cast, since he doesn't vary his actors often. Christian Bale has appeared in 4 of his films, Cillian Murphy in 4, Michael Caine in 5. Marion Cotillard, Tom Hardy, and Joseph Gordon-Levitt each return for their 2nd go around, while others provide their usual outstanding supporting roles, like Morgan Freeman and Gary Oldman. Acting and script as usual cannot be scrutinized when it comes to Christopher Nolan. However since it is the end of a trilogy, its impossible not to go back and think which of the three is the best? I honestly can't decide, which i suppose with the company we are talking about, can only be a compliment for The Dark Knight Rises, that i am even willing to consider this greater than or equal to the near perfection of The Dark Knight. My gut tells me to say this film is not as good as The Dark Knight, but for me, that would mean calling it a disappointment, which i don't want to imply. In the grand scope of things, what this film shows me is this; that Christopher Nolan, even after all his success is still willing to take risks and try new things. The only complaint i could have for this film is that its....unimaginable, but that isn't Chris Nolan's fault, its mine. Its difficult for us to imagine an entire city held captive by a small army lead by a ruthless juggernaut, with the threat of being blown away at any given moment. The only reason we have trouble imagining this is because, thankfully, such a circumstance has never occurred in the real wold, but that doest make it implausible. When in the climax of the Dark Knight, the threats were much smaller and much more understandable. While also in this film, Nolan isn't afraid to include the army, nuclear weapons, football teams. Such things make the world of batman almost too much like the real world, when up until then, the world of the caped crusader never dared to go beyond the stretches of a made up city called Gotham, no outside influence, no federal government, no nukes, just batman. To my surprise, the extreme realism doesn't hurt the credibility of the movie, which makes me believe Nolan can make just about anything work. Ultimately you come away satisfied, and i suppose thats what counts. It provides excellent closure, even with a subtle hint at another film to come. The Dark Knight Trilogy is finally put to bed and it will rest well. I guess that isn't a typical movie review, so let me close with a few comments that are typical. Ahem, i think Christian Bale is up for an Oscar, and Anne Hathaway is sooooo hot!

10.title: Absolute Batman
10.content:
I had the delightful experience of watching the Batman trilogy at the BFI IMAX cinema in London, on the day of it's UK release. First of all, I'm so glad that Christopher Nolan chose to shoot in IMAX and not 3D. I'm not a '3D' fan and this would have killed the movie. I admire Chris Nolan for doing what he wanted and not just jumping on the bandwagon. IMAX definitely enhanced the films overall. The scenes that were shot with IMAX cameras, totally filled the 26mx20m silver screen and I felt fully immersed in the story. Ultra high definition and true depth of field certainly made this an experience to remember. I doubt I will ever enjoy normal cinemas as much.

I'm a massive Batman fan. I loved the cartoons when I was younger and had all the toys. I still read the comics now and Batman is in fact the only comic I read. The characters are so complex and interesting, that I have no need to read any other comics nor the time. I understand the great depth of each character and it is clear that Christopher Nolan also shares this knowledge.

I was disappointed by the Original Batman Movies and as a fan, I felt let down. In my eyes, the Batman films were forever dead. Memento is one of my favourite films, so when it was announced that Christopher Nolan was making Batman Begins, I started to believe that Batman would finally get the screen time and a decent story that he deserved, although I was still sceptical. Thankfully the first film exceeded expectations and the ending made me very anxious to see the next film. Batman was dark and mysterious, just like he was meant to be.

My favourite Batman character is of course the Joker and the second Christopher Nolan film, The Dark Knight, ticked every single box. Christopher Nolan and Heath Ledger both had a great vision and created the perfect Joker. The character was so complex and was depicted exactly how he was in some of my favourite Batman comics.

After watching The Prestige and Inception, Christopher Nolan soon became my favourite Director of all time. He consistently surpasses my expectations and is such a creative and talented Director. Despite rumours that he wouldn't come back to make a third Batman movie, I believed that he would want to make the perfect ending to the perfect beginning of a famous icon. Thus The Dark Knight Rises was announced.

Despite the opinions and bad reviews the title for this new film received, I personally thought it made sense and fitted well within the Nolan story arc. I saw many rumours of whom was being cast for the new film, including Johnny Depp as the Riddler. This was entertaining to read and exciting. As soon as Tom Hardy was confirmed as Bane, I started researching the Actor as I had only seen him in Inception.

After watching Layer Cake and Rock'n'Rolla again, Bronson, The Take and Warrior, I realised how talented an Actor Tom Hardy is and soon became a big fan of his too. I had every faith that Christopher Nolan had picked the perfect actor to play such a fantastic and iconic Batman villain, despite what others were saying. I spent the following year looking forward to the next and final instalment of Nolan's Batman franchise.

Leading up to the release, everyone had high expectations of this film due to the success from its predecessor. Many believed it would not be as good because Heath Ledger was not in it. I had my own expectations and was anxious but I believed in Christopher Nolan.

I'm happy to say that this final film, was a complete success in my eyes. It successfully connected the dots from the previous films and gave a fantastic ending that was true to Batman, as well as keeping with Nolan's signature story-telling and vision. I totally got what Nolan was trying to achieve and could only wish that I could have the opportunity to work with such a talented person.

The story was interesting throughout and had many references to some of my favourite comics, as did the previous two films. The sound and music was ear-popping and exactly how it should be. Seeing this at the IMAX really helped enhance the experience.

All actors were fantastic and played the characters perfectly. Christian Bale once again portrayed Batman in a way that is true to character. Anne Hathaway went beyond my expectations for her role as Catwoman. Tom Hardy continued to strengthen his talents. His eyes are piercing and demonstrate so much emotion without the need to see his face. Very few great actors can do that. Bane was realistic and certainly on par with Heath Ledger's performance as the Joker. Despite what others think, I believe that the audio for his voice was perfectly clear and understandable. I look forward to seeing Hardy as Mad Max.

As far as the story goes. It lives up to what has already happened in Gotham City and goes beyond this. It has its twists and turns, as well as its puzzles and complexities, like all Nolan films. I understood the ending and have my own interpretation of it, just like Nolan expects. Some people may not like this film and may feel let down because it is not how they expected it to be. At the end of the day, if you think you can do better, good luck to you. As a genuine Batman and Christopher Nolan fan, I am entirely satisfied with this film.

May the people that tragically lost their lives to this film rest in peace now. My thoughts are with their friends and families. I hope that one day, they will be able to watch this film and appreciate it for what it is, without being reminded of the horrible events that occurred.

10.title: From a Trilogy standpoint
10.content:
It has been a month...everything about this film as it is on its own, has been said and reviewed by many. My opinion of it is from a trilogy standpoint.

After watching the trilogy again from Batman Begins, The Dark Knight and now Rises, all in all... it is to me, the greatest trilogy i had ever seen. Never was there a moment in all three films, that i felt bored, that the story wasn't moving along.

Eg. LOTR - The Two Towers, i dreaded the hobbit parts or SW looking at it as a whole episode from 1 to 6, there are many arcs of the story that was uninteresting.

Having said that, my only gripe with The Dark Knight Rises as a trilogy, was with the 3 principal characters of Blake, Serena and Miranda. If these 3 characters were introduced much earlier either during Batman Begins or The Dark Knight, their impact on the overall trilogy would had been much greater. And if only Katie Holmes reprises her role as Rachel in The Dark Knight, or Maggie Gyllenhaal was the one portraying her in Batman Begins, everything would had been perfect.

Either way, the choice of the actors & actresses portraying their respective characters was the perfect cast. They did great. Never was there a time that i watched these characters as their actors & actresses. Each of them made me forget and believed in the characters themselves. I am saddened that it has finally come to a fitting end unfortunately.

With Christopher Nolan's Batman...it is the closest and the best comic book adaptation i had ever seen.

Thank you for making it possible for me (as a fan of the comics) to be able to watch this in my life time.

10.title: Greatest movie of all time!
10.content:
First of all, let's get this clear, The Dark Knight was amazing, by far the best superhero movie and one of the greatest movie's ever. Heath Ledger's Joker performance was amazing and it seemed like Christopher Nolan would not be able to top his magnificent work with the second film.

Then he releases this. The Dark Knight Rises blows the Dark Knight out of the water. I didn't think that would be possible, but Nolan did it! I won't give anything away in this review, I would never want to ruin the movie for anyone.

This is what I will say, I've been reading a lot of reviews and there is far too much knit-picking out there. This movie had no flaws. The flashbacks demonstrated from the previous films added a certain flavor that this movie couldn't do without. The plot was incredible. The storyline continues to build and build as the movie progresses and you get see a brand new Bruce Wayne/Batman, one that is neglected by this city and seen as a thug and a murderer. You get to see the way Jim Gordan deals with "the secret" of knowing that it was Harvey Dent that was the true criminal.

The last hour of the movie will leave you on the edge of your seat and when the movie concludes you will want to buy a ticket to the next showing. This movie touches on every emotion. It's a mixture of action/adventure/drama/thrill/sadness/happiness. The score by Hans Zimmer will give you goosebumps throughout the film, but once again it's the incredible acting that makes this movie complete.

My question is why doesn't Christian Bale get more credit for his acting in these films? His acting is flawless. You forget it's an actor on screen, instead it seems like you are really watching Bruce Wayne/Batman. He totally dives into the character and he is perfect for the role.

Then there's Michael Caine who really outdoes himself in this one. Alfred was great in the first two films, but Caine takes Alred to another level in this one. Then there's Morgan Freeman who is his usual self, Gary Oldman does another fantastic job as Jim Gordon.

The newbies really make this movie great though. Tom Hardy as Bane was right up there with Ledger's Joker. I could understand everything he said perfectly fine and he was a violent and opposing villain. His acting really sets the bar for what a villain should look like and act like in a superhero film. Joseph Gordan Levitt was great as John Blake. He seems like a younger version of Bruce Wayne with his passion for justice. Anne Hathaway is at her very best as Selina Kyle/Catwoman, and by the way, she looks incredible in that cat suit! Overall, this movie has already inked it's place in history. It was fantastic from beginning to end and it's a sad reality knowing we won't get to see these actors laying these roles ever again. It would be great if Nolan decided to do another one, but it seems that won't be happening. Either way, he goes out with a bang and this movie was by far his best. If this movie doesn't get an Oscar Nod for best picture, in fact if it doesn't win the Oscar for best picture, there is something truly wrong with the Academy.

10.title: Absolutely incredible
10.content:
I have never understood the need for escapism as part of cinema, to me it seems like too much of a brilliant format to waste on people who don't have the intelligence to further their outlook on the world. But nonetheless, mind-numbing, multi-million dollar movies are churned out like nobody's business and the majority of the population will happily pay their money to sit through cinematic garbage and learn nothing new about the universe they live in.

When Chris Nolan walked onto the 'superhero movie' scene with 'Batman Begins', I cant say I or anyone else for that matter expected him to do anything out of the ordinary with the franchise. I even expected $150 million of Hollywood vomit to be wiped before my eyes, but what instead happened was a $150 million art-house movie, a film that challenged and made no shortcuts in explaining its multiple engrossing plots (a Chris Nolan strength in general)and it did not insult the audiences intelligence. I loved the dark and frightening twist on the franchise, along with a grade A cast and a superb score, one would have been forgiven in thinking that if and when a sequel were to be made that it would not match it.

And then Nolan did it again, moulding together an even better cast (I much prefer Maggie Gyllenhaal to Katie Holmes) and not to mention the bloody fantastic Heath ledger who puts most screen villains to shame with his extremely sadistic yet darkly humorous joker.

And that was it. 'The Dark Knight'. I certainly didn't think even Chris Nolan could out-do that. Especially after 'Inception' in 2010, it was about time the man did something ordinary and created a bad film to dent his incredible record.

But he couldn't even do that.

I do not want to go into detail about the plot of 'The Dark Knight Rises', so all I will say is this. In my opinion Tom Hardy's 'Bane' is the most frightening screen presence of all time. There is a moment where he gently places the side of his hand on Daggett's shoulder, a fantastically subtle shift in power between the two characters. Christian Bale shifts between Wayne and the Batman in such a way that you feel the weight of the suit and challenges of donning his alter ego, Michael Caine is fantastic, an emotional charge that has been somewhat missing from the other films. Anne Hathaway might have had an excuse to be poor considering the talent she was surrounded by but even she was marvellous. Gary Oldman deserves far more praise than he gets for his involvement in the trilogy and Joseph Gordon Levitt was the perfect choice for his role.

Hans Zimmer shows us why he is the best movie composer of all time and Wally Pfister's photography is an art form in itself.

All in all the most well rounded action movie/superhero comic adaptation of all time, the final part in the Dark Knight trilogy that we were all waiting for and perhaps the most satisfying (yet totally up for debate) ending to a movie ever!

Thankyou Chris Nolan for enjoying what you do, your work in cinema is a relief to those who want to watch films for what they truly are; an art form.

10.title: Holy! Epic! Batman!
10.content:
Billionaire Bruce Wayne once said, "I am moreit's what you do that defines you." The question is: what defines us all? The fire has risen and that fire has been put out, but not yet though. One thing still remains: Is there a future for the billionaire playboy? Enough about playboys, let's chat about how we got here.

In 2005, we were re-introduced to a boy who fell down a well and we saw what frightened him the most – bats. But he overcame that fear and struck fear into the hearts of those that knew the very existence of fear. Fighting against the mob, Batman took down the biggest crime lords of Gotham City – Carmine Falcone and gave the Scarecrow a taste of his own medicine.

But in 2008, the war was not over, not even by a landslide. As Bruce Wayne was having battles of his own, Batman was posed as a threat to the city and plus a mastermind of theatricality, a brain as the size of a laughing matter, brought a new taste in life – SLAUGHTER WAS THE BEST MEDICINE! The Joker (RIP Heath!), portrayed one of the darkest villains of all time as he brought down upon the city and the new DA Harvey Dent and gave the word "light" a new name.

Now we come to 2012, no one expected this to come to a conclusion, we thought we were in it for the long haul. Let's just say it was bittersweet and a whole lot of punches and back breaking. The ultimate villain, Bane, gave violence a new name. A name that was synonymous unlike any other. But Bane was not working alone. An arch-enemy came back to finish a job but through someone else. And the black was faded and billionaire was living his life and moving on. But wait something red approaches, something that will fly red colors – is it a red monster, is it a red wagon, no it is a RED ROBIN.

For 8 years, the mastermind of Christopher Nolan and his brother Jonathon gave Batman a new look and took the story to a whole new level. Thank you for teaching us that it is what we do that defines us. Christian Bale – you gave us an icon to live up to, you taught us to live for ourselves. Thank you. From Cillian Murphy to Tom Wilkinson to the late Heath Ledger to Aaron Eckhart to Tom Hardy to Anne Hathaway to Marion Cotillard – you guys defined evil. Thank you.

Batman will live in our hearts for years to come.

10.title: The PERFECT Conclusion!
10.content:
I read that Christopher Nolan took inspiration from the Lord of the Rings trilogy on this final Dark Knight film, and it showed. It is true there are rarely any superb third films in a saga, but I think this is up there with the top.

The acting was truly spectacular, as usual, with many heartbreaking moments (namely those between Alfred and Bruce.) It is difficult enough for actors to portray potent emotions using words, but sometimes Caine and Bale simply broke my heart using their eyes. Anne Hathaway was amazing and seductive as the Catwoman, taking on a very complex character wonderfully. Also Joseph Gordon-Levitt shone through as he usually does, likable and courageous as Blake. Tom Hardy was simply terrifying at times.

I know there are people who are ranting at this movie for "not meeting the standard set by the Dark Knight" but personally I think they are looking only at the antagonists. Yes, the Joker was a wholeheartedly epic villain, and it will probably be difficult for anyone to match Ledger's outstanding performance of him - but that doesn't mean Bane was in any way not up to scratch. He was very scary and I found myself wide- eyed at certain scenes, especially the first real fight between him and Batman. I don't think it's fair to judge this movie simply on Bane vs Joker, because obviously the Joker will win.

The plot was very ambitious and intense. Even though the runtime was a lengthy two hours and forty five minutes, I almost wanted some time to stop for breath at certain points. I believe it is probably a film which needs to be viewed twice before all of it really is sewn together (also, if you haven't seen Batman Begins and the Dark Knight in a while it is better when you re-watch all.) It was full of heart-racing action and breath-taking emotion. It is most definitely not just a "simple action movie" as it included so many twists and turns in the story. I admit I am usually not a fan of actions just because they often lack intelligent plots - however, the Dark Knight trilogy is right there near the top of my five favourite films. I also liked the introduction of the Bat, just out of pure enjoyment.

There are a couple of downsides I have though, first being Marion Cotillard as Miranda Tate. She was underdeveloped and unlike-able from the beginning and, although this is explained later, I do not understand what Bruce saw in her in the first place. The second little bad point I can't really go into without making a spoiler, but when a certain character dies I wish it had been more significant after all of the trouble it took.

I am glad Nolan didn't go for the 3D option, too. The ending was simply perfect in my opinion, and although I am devastated that it is all over, I am happy I left the cinema fully satisfied rather than disappointed as I am with many endings.

Truly a 10/10 film regardless of the bitter cynics.

10.title: There Are No Words To Describe This Film's Greatness!!!
10.content:
I waited in line for nearly 5 hours to see this film in IMAX on the midnight premiere, and waited another 2 hours sitting in the theatre. And OH MY GOD WAS IT WORTH IT!!!

The thing that I always loved about Nolan's Batman films was the reality basis that they had, and of course the great performances in them, as well as the writing, directing, cinematography, visuals, EVERYTHING!!

This film delivers all of those elements of course, but also has a lot of new great things about it.

The film takes place eight years after the events of The Dark Knight, and both Batman and Bruce Wayne have disappeared from Gotham City. After Batman took the fall for Harvey Dent's crimes and disappeared, Gotham has turned from being a chaotic hell hole, to a peaceful place. And now a new unstoppable force, Bane, has entered Gotham with very aggressive plans, and clearly appears to be the biggest threat Gotham has ever experienced.

The performances in this film were excellent. Christian Bale as always was great as Bruce Wayne and Batman, but this was by far his best performance as both, but particularly as Bruce Wayne. This film does happen to contain more Bruce Wayne story than Batman story. But that's because he has been out of it for so long, that he must rise from the darkness and become Batman again.

Tom Hardy was especially great as the masked terrorist Bane. This was probably my favourite performance in the film. Tom Hardy pulls off everything I think Bane should be. He's intelligent, cunning, and so menacing that it quite terrifying. And thankfully, they enhanced his voice. In the six minute prologue, I found him kind of hard to understand in a few lines, but in this, he is completely understandable. And In my opinion, he is the greatest movie villain since Darth Vader in The Empire Strikes Back. Yes, I liked him more than The Joker.

Anne Hathaway was really great as Catwoman. She really does pull off everything about Catwoman, the sexiness, fighting combat, and even emotion. I was a bit skeptical about Hathaway playing her when I first heard, but now that I've seen the film, she really is a scene stealer.

What I've heard a lot of people say was that they didn't like Bane as much as The Joker, but almost everyone agrees that Bane's plan is more creative than anything The Joker did and more enjoyable to watch as it unfolds.

The climax of this film is spectacular. It's great for all of you idiots who just love action, and even greater for people who love quality films. The climax is not just filled with action either, it is also very emotional and dramatic. The last twenty minutes of this film is the closest i've ever come to crying in a film. I truly wanted to cry. And if you are a fan boy of Christopher Nolan and his Batman films, you will also.

The Dark Knight Rises is an extremely satisfying conclusion to the Batman trilogy, and in my opinion, the best of the trilogy and of Christopher Nolan's films in general. There are honestly no words I can describe this films greatness with. 10/10.

10.content: let me start up with the performances first, the first i would like to talk about is BANE.. let us not compare with the joker, he has given his best shot, and the way his character ended with one boom is disappointing, next ANNA HATHAWAY she has truly done justice to her part and does not get much more to deliver.. and others are cool.. lastly the Christian BALE.. here he has got chance to express the emotions and of him than BATMAN character.. outstanding.. 10.title: I loved it.
10.content:
I feel as if this review is going to evolve into a rant and so I give my readers a fair warning. I love Christopher Nolan as a filmmaker, to me he is the biggest breath of fresh air and creativity working in Hollywood today. His 'Dark Knight' trilogy took Batman and turned it into something that is fresh and daring. His Batman although just as flamboyant and loud as other comic book pictures is built upon real emotion and characters. I can see why these films have become so popular because I dare to say that audiences are seldom if not ever treated to an entertaining comic book picture that respects their intelligence.

I thought this film was a solid finish to a great trilogy. It has flaws to be sure but I really think that as a part of a united whole 'Rises' overcomes it's shortcomings and becomes an integral piece of a brilliant opus. There are excellent performances all around. And most satisfying for me is that the film delves into the greater implications of how the concept of a Batman brought Gotham into a further hell that needed a life or death stake battle to save. The picture is thrilling and never dull.

What interests me even more though is the negative backlash and flaming that has brought around this picture. People are defensive about their love of it and haters are extra loud about their hate. It is unnecessary and stupid.

10.title: First there was Fear, then came the Anarchy and now the Pain: Well Done Mr. Nolan
10.content:
Well, to start with Mr. Nolan is extremely gifted filmmaker there is no doubt about it even in the minds of his most extreme critics.But being gifted and able to deliver consistently are two different things and Nolan has excelled in both.

In 2008 when Dark Knight was released people were pleasantly surprised by the depth of this movie (which is primarily an action movie based on comics ) they expected lots of boom, CGI gimmicks and a bit of humor (a la Avengers, Iron Man etc )instead Nolan takes us deep in to the mind of Joker and perhaps gives us a glimpse of pure evil , an evil which has no interest in Money ,women or power but just pure destruction and corruption.People instantly connected with the film because deep down they know that if they are put on a ship and told that they can only survive if they blow up the other ship which has inmates on it, they will have their conscience tested.After watching the movie , i can bet that all of us must have thought about that for a long time.

Coming to TDKR , first of all i would like to say that this is sheer brilliance , a master piece of a film and if any critic gives it less than 10/10 then he must surely couldn't have understood the movie.

Most of the time filmmakers in their quest for achieving the expectations of the people try so hard ,try so many things and make the film so complicated and bland that it loses its basic premise of holding and continuing the story of its prequel. But in this case what we see is that Nolan takes his vision to a more logical level and delivers it with much more panache. Critics say that Nolan couldn't create a match for joker this time, he created a world too dull and may be too dark but can somebody ask those critics that if Nolan had created a character similar to Joker wouldn't they would have said that TDKR simply follows the moves of its predecessor, wouldn't they say that TDKR has nothing new to show ? Well, I say that if TDK has the Joker who is hell bent on corrupting the Gotham, in TDKR Bane takes that to a new level, he doesn't only want to corrupt them but he wants to humiliate them , literary make them to beg at his mercy and if that is not enough, to kill them all. TDKR is unquestionably better than TDK in terms of production quality, the special effects and in its scope, not to mention the exceptional performance of each actors involved.

I would specially like to mention Michael Cain, he is the emotional powerhouse of this movie and without him, no doubt the film would have lacked in that department.

To conclude, i want to say that since this movie's biggest competitor is its predecessor (any other action/comic/superhero/adventure movie doesn't even come close) , it really surpassed it in every aspect.

10.title: Inspired work
10.content:
Never underestimate the power of an old comic strip to inspire. Hence we are inspired. I was thoroughly entertained by The Dark Knight Rises and did not think it was any less of a movie than The Dark Knight. Maybe better!

Though not possessed with the amazing power of its predecessor's Oscar winning performance it is none the less a compelling movie.

The main character is played with an excellent eye towards the craft by Christian Bale who seems like a different person in the Batman suit. Rather haggard and a little spent. This is what it takes to win an Oscar to be able to project a character's state of mind and spirit.

Now that Mr. Bale has an Oscar you who did not like his Batman can now believe!

It was not lost on me that this villain's pain is hidden and relieved buy his mask and the hero's pain is his mask. They battle it out against the back drop of a city that is living a lie.

Also this movie captures its moment in history before it happened as a villain stepped inside a theatre and while wearing a mask murdered 12 innocent people and injured 58 who went to see this very film.

GOD BE WITH ALL OF YOU!

I saw "The Dark Knight Rises" less than 5 hours after 12:00 PM EDT 7-20-11 when I found out about the senseless attack on that theatre in Colorado.

It didn't stop me.

I planned on seeing this movie on the day and at the hour it opened in Waltham but was delayed by all the news feeds.

Christopher Nolan was inspired and has made an excellent film.

10.title: Christopher Nolan Shows That Batman is a True Hero
10.content:
The Dark Knight Rises is a really epic movie. You can tell when you watch it. There are a ton of people in it, has really amazing special effects, and great action scenes. But a movie isn't good just because of these things (even though it really helps). This movie has a lot more to offer than just a typical Hollywood action film. Most of us have learned to love Christopher Nolan's batman films, and this one does not disappoint. The performance by the actors is absolutely stunning. Tom Hardy played an excellent Bane while only using his eyes, body language, and voice. We couldn't see his whole face, which helps us see emotion. But with Hardy's great performance, we get to see and feel the emotions without seeing his whole face. He is a very creepy villain, and one of the best I have seen. Anne Hathaway also does a great job portraying Selina Kyle (Catwoman). Like most, I was afraid that she wouldn't do so well, but then I realized that Nolan always knows what he's doing, and always chooses the right actors. And he really does know what he's doing. Anne pulled it off! She played an amazing Catwoman, and was pretty darn sexy in that outfit! Great addition to the movie. And Bale as Batman was freaking cool as always. But he really shines in this film because of all the things the character had to go through and overcome. Best performance by Bale in my opinion. He really showed us that Bruce Wayne is as heroic as his alter ego, the Batman. Which brings me to my next point.

Aside from all the cool special effects and amazing acting, this movie has an amazing story. Christopher Nolan is really good at getting those emotions out there for us to feel. Also, he knows how to make a character heroic. While watching the movie, I kept rooting for Bruce, and Batman, and when he failed, I was devastated. But when Batman rose to show his true strength, and his true colors, I cheered. I was happy and excited for Batman/Bruce. I actually cheered a lot in this film. Bruce is shown more in the movie than Batman. And it's Bruce as himself that has to overcome everything before he can show the world how good Batman really is. We actually see more Bruce than Batman in this film. This made Batman seem even more human than before, and made me connect more to the film. I loved Batman, because he's human. And we got to see that. We also get to see how heroic and amazing this character is in this film as he overcomes everything to try to save Gotham and its people. The amazing emotions are also helped by Hans and his amazing score for The Dark Knight Rises. One of the best soundtracks I have ever listened to. Heavier than the past Batman films, and much more heroic at times. Not to mention super epic.

So all in all, because of the amazing special effects, with amazing acting, great story that lets us feel (and think), which is also helped by the amazing soundtrack, this film has got to be one of the most brilliant films I have ever seen. Also the most epic, and the most amazing film I have yet seen. Christopher Nolan shows us again that he can create an action film with heart, spirit, and brains (which is much needed in Hollywood these days). It is also the smartest, and heroic comic book movie I have ever seen. And the addition of special characters from the comic book also makes things even more exciting. This movie had the perfect ending for a Batman series, and one of the best and most satisfying endings I have ever seen in a movie, and in a trilogy. I am grateful to Nolan for creating this masterpiece, and I suggest that everyone sees this movie. It really is a must see. It's more than just a comic book movie. It's a film for everyone, not just for comic book fans. Shows us the worst and the best of humanity. And leaves you in aw. Why do we fall? So we can learn to pick ourselves up. And you'll really see a hero rise.

10.title: Magnificent!
10.content:
I've heard quite a few people doubting this movie would be anywhere near as good as either of its predecessors. But in my opinion they were wrong.

Similarly to The Dark Knight, there actually several scenes excluding Batman, but unlike TDK, The Dark Knight Rises is actually about Batman. Christian Bale is awesome yet again as are Michael Caine (who has much more emotion in this one), Gary Oldman and Morgan Freeman in their respective roles. There'll always be people disappointed by any movie. But I find The Dark Knight Rises to be a brilliant ending to an epic masterpiece of a trilogy.

And if you don't applaud at the climax of The Dark Knight Rises, remember, you are one in a million.

10.title: The Dark Rises...against OWS
10.content:
"Dark Knight Rises" is a relentless, conceptually terrifying, soul-crushing but ultimately vindicating and hopeful social commentary.

In operatic terms, "Avengers" would be Mozart's "Magic Flute" while "DKR" is Wagner's "Das Rheingold" turned up to 11.

One doesn't exactly sit watching idly. Seems more like Christopher Nolan beats the spit out of you with "DKR." Even those familiar with the various comic book source materials will find themselves surprised, pleasantly.

There's also an edgy "anything can happen" vibe rare in genre films. The sequence of events provides an incredible smokescreen of misdirection that keeps one guessing but also FEARING what might occur.

"Can Nolan go there?" you might ask as the plot unfolds and you're assuming what's next. He does. Amazingly, he finds ways.

Just as amazing is Nolan's track record with this incredible cinematic hat trick trilogy. "Batman Begins" was a compelling, clever film that didn't disappoint and even improved upon the legendary source material. "Dark Knight" upped the ante and even commented upon the war on terror. Now, with "DKR," Nolan not only swings for the fences but doesn't whiff, as is traditional with every other threequel. Far from it.

The "DKR" villains aren't the brilliantly flip Heath Ledger, they're something else entirely -- totally menacing, self-righteously delusional and murderously uncompromising. Ledger's Joker embodied chaos, while Bane and the League Of Shadows represented the dead-end false promises of far-left demagogues preaching class warfare, and, of course, "fairness." Sound familiar?

Experiencing "DKR" is nothing if not overwhelming, in a thought-provoking and resonating manner. The shiny veneer of certain political promises and assertions might peel away even further while Hans Zimmer's music buzzes in your head during the days following.

I'd label Nolan a genius...but, he really can't take credit for this motion picture. "He didn't do it himself." Other disenfranchised people are entitled to the praise. Right, Bane?

10.title: Outstanding and the best movie of 2012!!!
10.content:
This review is for those film lovers who watch films for the experience, and boy, does this film blows one away or what!!this was undoubtedly the best movie so far of 2012 and this one is definitely in the best top 10 movies i have ever seen.

One cant imagine anyone other than Christian Bale to fill the shoes of Batman.He gives a great performance in this film.Personally i liked the performance of the Joker better in The Dark Knight but in this one nobody doesn't even stand a chance against Bale.He delivers the goods so perfectly that one cant help but applaud.The way in which the story unfolds is also superb.Hats off to the director for creating nothing short of a masterpiece.The story seems to have a life of its own and keeps you guessing and at the edge of the seat at all times wondering what is going to happen next.Selina Kyle played by Anne Hathaway and Tom Hardy as Blane also nails it.Its Tom Hardy's best performance after Warrior i would say.

Some minor glitches which i would like to point out is the way in which the character Robin was developed and also the prison scenes could have been better.I guess it was left to the imagination of the audience how a badly bruised and mentally broken Batman regains his physical and mental strength within 3 months.The character Blake played by Joseph Gordon-Levitt appeared to be a bit flimsy when compared to the otherwise total dark and gripping film.

10.title: The Legend Ends Or Rather Continues??
10.content:

Wow...my best movie experience ever..and the deafening cheering in the movie-hall complimenting it! 10.title: Just loved it
10.content:
It is fair to say that this movie had a lot to live up to. The Dark Knight blew not only comic book movies, but action movies out of the water. It raised expectations for this type of film. It was smart, thoughtful and to be honest just pure brilliance, well in my opinion anyway. So the question was always can the Dark Knight Rises match it? Personally, I think the answer is yes.

The Dark Knight Rises doesn't have the madness and darkness of the Joker. It doesn't have Batman show as much emotion and vulnerability. This movie doesn't try to beat The Dark Knight. Instead, it tries to be different. The threat in this movie is bigger and we see Batman stood with others beside him not alone. And for the first time we see the 'legacy' Batman has left on Gotham. This movie is not about a war between two men in masks, it is about something much more than that. Aesthetically this movie is pleasing. Christopher Nolan knows this world well. The effects, action sequences, camera work are all stunning. The music is epic and used well. He proves yet again that he is a talented and smart director.

The performances are top notch. The returning characters are all great. Bale's Batman is as brooding and suffering as always. Caine's Alfred is full of more heart than I know what to do with, and Freeman and Oldman are just brilliant as they always are.

It is the new members of the cast that have to shoulder the weight of this movie, most notably with Tom Hardy's Bane. It is hard not to compare his performance with Heath Ledger's Joker but to do so is not really fair. I am not sure if we will ever see such an outstandingly dark and manic performance again. Bane, as a character, has maybe a little more heart and there are moments where it shows. His motivation to harm is not the same as The Joker; in fact it could not be more different. I have not seen Hardy like this before, the performance was restrained but it worked and I enjoyed his character a lot.

Anne Hathaway's cold and calculating Catwoman is also impressive. To be honest I was not expecting much from her but she delivered and she ended up being one of my favourite parts of the movie.

Of all the new characters it is Joseph Gordon Levitt's good cop John Blake that really stood out for me. There is something about this guy that just works on screen, he is effortless in the role and I cared for his character more than any other.

The Dark Knight Rises is not just good action and acting. There are also moments of humour, of light-heartedness. There are amazing gadgets, a great ending and quite a few twists and turns.

This movie is genius, it fits perfectly with the rest of the series and I loved it.

As a whole the Batman trilogy is something that will never be beaten and I hope no one ever tries. As far as batman movies go (in my opinion), they start here and they should end here to. I am sad to see the back of Christian Bale's Batman but glad that it ended on a high.

10.title: The Dark Knight Rises is MONUMENTAL work by Nolan!
10.content:
Here are my thoughts- Watched the movie -2 straight viewings.The movie is MESMERIZING .Can't get myself out of the Bat universe of Nolan. TDKR is a monumental achievement by Great director C.Nolan.Before saying anything we have to agree on one point that while making this movie he had faced the toughest challenge of living up to the standard of the preceding masterpiece -TDK and ending the most anticipated trilogy on a sound note. I have nothing but superlatives to describe what I just witnessed. Honestly I'm still shocked at how it far exceeded anything I had hoped for. The ending is perfect! Absolute resolution! I'm still soaking it in. yeah, this movie has everything I wanted in a Nolan Batman movie and then some...

ABSORBING.Yes,the movie is engaging to a great extent despite having a long run time of roughly 3 hours.After initial 15 minutes you get sucked into the Gotham universe.This is not a popcorn movie where you can afford munching on popcorn to kill boredom.One of the Very few movies that I have seen with such long playtime but still not becoming dull at a single moment.(Unless you have ADHD)

2.Casting Hardy as Bane is quite intimidating,ruthless.You must appreciate the actor's dedication to his work. He has molded his body physique in a terrific hunk character.You get to see his face briefly for one scene only.With mask on for most of the rest of time,he has given a commendable performance Bane.You can appreciate the furious eyes,the twitching of muscles and the horrifying voice-they have modded the voice definitely since he was a bit inaudible in the prologue(but in the movie-Bane is audible for each and every sentence)He is a classy villain, whose motivations are understandable, and frightening.This is, in my opinion, his best work aside from Warrior. Christian Bale-What a spectacular performance!He has proved his acting mettle too many times and he gives full justice to Bruce's role yet again!He was phenomenal in emotional scenes with Caine.Age just doesn't show up on the actors' face.Best Bruce Wayne in the history of Batman movies!Period.

Freeman,Caine,Gary Oldman are just amazing actors,you can simply expect a seminal performance from them.There was no doubt they were going to do their best! Anne Hathaway -Surprisingly steals the show.She is the best Catwoman I have ever seen!Her character is gifted with many crisp ,humorous,sarcastic dialogs.She has immersed herself in that role fully. M.Cotillard-What a shocking twist!She had perfectly portrayed seductive ,yet negative role of MAL in Inception,and she succeeds in justifying her casting in this film.It's impressive how actor's with very few dialogs in the movie can impact the general outcome! 3.Action: This is the mother of all superhero action movies.The last hour or so is just EPIC.At one stage the city of Gotham is almost torn apart by Bane.The CGI are perfect.The last 15 minutes are full of "edge-of the seat" moments.The Cinematography is breathtakingly beautiful. Many scenes have been shot with an IMAX camera and that extra effort has helped make the film all the more amazing. I can safely say this is the best piece of cinematography I have seen till now!!In last 30 minutes,all the chaos breaks loose and you get the feeling of a new world-war. Bane proves to be a far enormous master of anarchy than the Joker.The destruction he causes is unimaginable.

4.Direction "The dark knight rises" isn't the perfect film but it is definitely the most emotional of all three. You can feel the pressure on Nolan while making this enormously anticipated movie.He has lived up to expectations.He has once again shown he is the BEST film maker of this generation.This man continues to amaze me as a FINISHER.Look at any board maximum people are discussing the END of the movie.Yes!He succeeds yet again in satisfying both classes-the hardcore Batman fans(Who can take a little bit of fantasy into consideration)and the prudent not-so-fan type of viewers. TDKR is much beyond the final ending scenes.This is what most people ain't getting in their heads.

The emotional scenes are directed skilfully.Noaln has always been blamed for lacking emotional content,being too cerebral etc..In this movie he will shut the mouth of such critics.In fact it is "Not-so-typical of-Nolan" type movie,which begins slow,but seeps deep inside your heart.

Yes,there are few flaws.

5.Music- Composer Hans Zimmer has done an excellent job again creating a haunting and beautiful soundtrack to accompany this film. There are not many places where you can appreciate the OST since the movie thrives heavily on the dialogs,still you get goose-bumps when "Imagine the fire" plays at the end.What a soundtrack it is! "Rise" plays at grim moments of the movie.It is Perfectly fitting to the situations of the movie. IMHO,they under-utilized Bane's chant "Dey she Bah-SA-rah". I Would have loved to hear that score at many places.

6.Conclusion&Reception It is a great film which would have been considered amazing had it not been for the impossibly high standards set by it's predecessors. The end leaves you awestruck and speechless, feeling satisfied and knowing that you have just seen the ending to what is possibly the best trilogy of all time. You just don't want to get out of the Nolan Universe of Batman even after the credits stop rolling down the screen. The reception was awesome in the theater.There was huge cheer for the Batman when he appears for the first time in the movie.Huge applause followed the end,when name of the director flashes on the screen for one final time as far as Batman movies are concerned. Thanks to C.Nolan for reviving a dead comic series,a series which was awfully pictured by so many directors till now.You happen to be the best and deserve great acclaim for making The Dark Knight Rises", - "a fantastic spectacle, groundbreaking and masterfully incredible".

Rating - 9.5/10

10.title: Nolan's finale knocks it out of the park
10.content: I Can easily say when i saw Dark Knight Rises, my expectations were that it would be good but it wouldn't come come close to Dark Knight. boy, was I wrong. if anything, This is even better than the Dark Knight. The plot is a good Batman story with lots of twists.It was kind of a combination of the story lines Knightfal and No man's land. i'm not going to give anything away but one of the twists involves Ra's Al ghul and his legacy. 10.title: An excellent conclusion to a terrific trilogy!
10.content:
I have never written any kind of review in my life (not counting facebook ranting!), but after hearing people (a clear minority, but still too many!) give negative opinions of this movie, I felt obligated to write my own review. I need to start off by saying that I had never been this excited for a film. Ever! This is the first film that I've seen on the day of its release and I had been hyping it up like you would not believe to anyone that would listen. Well, even to people who wouldn't listen too! Despite going in with the expectation that this would be one of the best movies I've ever seen, I can safely say that I was not let down. Not one bit!

The Dark Knight Rises is an even mix of Batman Begins and The Dark Knight. Batman Begins has its slow moments (especially in the first half of the movie), whereas The Dark Knight is able to just continue straight on from the foundations that the previous movie built, and is pretty much non-stop epic action from start to finish. The Dark Knight Rises also has slower moments, but where the story continues on from The Dark Knight, it's a bit inevitable. There was not a single moment though, where I thought to myself "man, this is a bit boring". Because of some of the "less exciting" scenes, I may not be able to re-watch The Dark Knight Rises as many times as I have seen The Dark Knight though. That doesn't make it an inferior film at all (especially going by first viewings). The plans that the bad guys have in store for Gotham City in Batman Begins could well and truly mean the destruction of the city. However, while it feels, and is an epic movie, the truth is that nothing that the Joker does in The Dark Knight poses much of a threat to your average citizen, let alone the whole of Gotham City. In The Dark Knight Rises however, what Bane achieves certainly does affect and also seriously threaten the WHOLE of Gotham City, and the conclusion (as it should, being the end of the trilogy) blows the ending of The Dark Knight out of the water, and then some.

Complaints about Bane not being as good a villain as the Joker are a bit ridiculous in my opinion. Sure, Heath Ledger as the Joker was a once in a lifetime performance, but you can't judge Bane against that. Tom Hardy does an incredible job as Bane. While the Joker was crazy... Bane is a psycho! If I were to come across either of these two in a street by themselves (unarmed), sure I'd be running like crazy from either of them... but I'd be running a lot harder and a lot faster from Bane, guaranteed! If Christopher Nolan had the option of returning to the Joker for the final film (well, if he could, maybe it might not have been his final film, who knows?), then chances are we would have just been given The Dark Knight V2.0. Not that there would have been anything wrong with that at all! But it might have gotten a little bit stale/repetitive. The unfortunate passing of Heath Ledger forced Nolan to go in a new direction, and it's an absolute credit to the story/screen writing team of himself, his brother Jonathon and David S. Goyer.

Overall the actors were very good. Christian Bale was excellent as Bruce Wayne, struggling with wanting/needing to be Batman. Michael Caine finally gets a chance to show his acting ability (in this trilogy!) and is very emotional in his scenes. Joseph Gordon-Levitt was very good as newcomer cop John Blake. Anne Hathaway did a good job as Catwoman (a word never said in the movie, which I think is a good thing!). I don't know why anyone thought she would do a bad job. Tom Hardy as Bane was exactly what you wanted him to be, terrifying, brutal, yet strangely composed. There was a line here or there from Bane that I missed completely, but nothing that left me confused about anything going on in the story. The scenes where he had extended dialogue, for example the NFL stadium speeches, I could understand every word. With second, third, fourth viewings etc, I'm sure I will pick up on the little bits that I missed. Even if I still miss them again, it's nothing that a subtitled DVD won't fix eventually!

I don't want to go on all day, so I won't go on about the other aspects too much. The cinematography and score are exactly what we've come to expect from Nolan's previous epic films. Either you like them or you don't. I certainly do! From the moment I first heard it in a preview, I have loved Bane's chant.

I had more written out, but I'll cut it short. I'll just say this, I think that anyone who gives The Dark Knight Rises less than a 7 out of 10 is being a bit ridiculous. It is a very exciting and entertaining movie, well written, with a lot of high quality action scenes. A lot of time and effort has clearly gone into every aspect of making The Dark Knight Rises (as it does with every one of Christopher Nolan's films), and if you can't at least appreciate and respect that, then you probably shouldn't be watching movies at all! I'll finish off by saying that it was an absolute tragedy what happened at the midnight screening at Aurora. How disgusting is it that anyone should be put through something like that? But people who are at the movies, clearly excited (since they're the first in the country to see it!) to watch a good movie, it's a disgrace. There's so many screwed up people in the world, all you can do is try your best to avoid them!

10.title: Best Trilogy ever. Satisfying ending to the franchise. Will Greatly be missed by all the fans. Epic epic of epicness.
10.content:
The Dark Knight Rises stars, Christian Bale, Michael Caine, Gary Oldman, and Morgan Freeman return for the third installment of Christopher Nolan's Batman franchise. New stars join the franchise to conclude the series with a bang, such as Anne Hathaway, Tom Hardy, with Joseph Gordon-Levitt, and Marion Coltillard. Written and Directed by Christopher Nolan, The Dark Knight Rises is the final chapter with the Bruce Wayne/ Batman trilogy that Christopher Nolan has directed and I would have to say this movie had some shoes to fill with the previous installment. Going into the theater expecting the most out of Christopher Nolan and now that the saga has concluded and the Film is over, Christopher Nolan surpassed my expectations in every form. This is an Epic ,epic with epic proportions and Nolan has outdone himself once again. Nolan has concluded the series with a satisfying third installment and will leave fans satisfied and gave them their money's worth, and also four years worth.

The premise of ''The Dark Knight Rises'' is a compelling story about redemption and rising and hope for Bruce Wayne/Batman and the city of Gotham. It's been 8 years since the previous film, and Batman has taken the blame for Harvey Dent/ Two-face's death and goes into hiding. Gotham city living without the caped crusader is need of faith and hope. A mercenary named Bane comes to Gotham city to destroy it to ashes, it's all part of Bane's plans. Batman is needed to rise in order to save Gotham city from Destruction. Batman then gets the help of Commissioner Gordon( Gary Oldman) John Blake (Joseph Gordon- Levitt) and also Selina Kyle/Catwoman (Anne Hathaway). Also reprising their roles as mentors and helpers of Bruce Wayne is Lucius Fox (Morgan Freeman) and also Alfred Pennyworth ( Michael Caine).

The Dark Knight Rises in my opinion is the best movie of 2012, and will have you on the edge of your seat the whole movie. The plot is very well written and the film executes the plot without barely any flaw. The acting by most actors is beyond good, especially the few with minor roles. Christian Bale's performance was flawless and his best of the series, delivering a character that we really care about and care about what happens to Batman, and even Bruce Wayne. He delivers both aspects flawlessly and does it in such a way that its one of his best. Anne Hathaway was almost a show stealer and embraced the character of Selina Kyle and made it her own and also made it fit into the tone of Nolan's universe. Then we have the menacing, terrifying and another show stealer by Tom Hardy's performance as Bane. My was he a great villain. From the moment you first hear him talk, it sounds almost like a Darth Vader tone to it. You're terrified of his character throughout the whole movie and I wouldn't have thought of anyone better to play Bane, after seeing his performance in Warrior, he was physically ready to play the Part and he executed it perfectly. He had some shoes to fill with Heath Ledger's ''Joker'' and he almost did, a near second I would say. Last but not least, Joseph Gordon-Levitt's performance was phenomenal and one of his best performances as the detective John Blake. His character has a big heart and is basically the voice of the citizens of Gotham City. He has faith and Hope in Batman and plays a big role towards the climax of the movie. The script and the dialogue was fitting to the films settings and situations and also there are some lines that make the tone of the film, less dark and gritty and lighten the mood of the film which is needed for a 2 hour and 40 minute film. Settings were phenomenal and also the special effects and props for Batman and Catwoman. For example ''The Bat'' which is Batman's fighter Jet. The direction and cinematography by Christopher Nolan and Wally Pfister is just wonderful to look at and just breathe taking. The editing in this film is more than good and I think should be nominated from the Academy, also one that should in my opinion win an Oscar would be the Musical composure of Hans Zimmer. This piece of work is truly amazing and will give you chills when watching the film, and suit the film perfectly giving each and every scene an added element of suspense or an element of hope and intertwines with the theme of the film which is redemption and finding hope. This movie is truly a perfect conclusion to Nolan's Batman trilogy and is beyond spectacular. It is the movie you can watch over and over again and is Amazing! I praise Christopher Nolan for making the best trilogy ever and I thank him with all my heart for these three films. Please watch this film, you won't be disappointed.

10.title: I didn't think anything could top The Dark Knight... I was wrong!
10.content: I wrote a review of The Dark Knight four years ago which, as you can see, said that it was simply the greatest comic movie ever made and also one of the best films ever (http://www.imdb.com/title/tt0468569/reviews-2622). Well today I write a review of The Dark Knight Rises with a completely different opinion- The Dark Knight of 2008 is now second to this movie. People may say it is quite long at 164mins but let me tell you, I have seen this in theatres twice already this week and this movie is so compelling and absorbing that it doesn't feel anything close to being long, as the script is constantly moving and developing and taking you on a thrill-ride you wont have have experienced in a long time. It is set in 2016, and Bruce Wayne, (with Christian Bale now hitting a career best Batman performance), leading a reclusive life in Wayne Manor and Batman retired after taking the blame for Harvey Dent's evil doing at the end of the previous movie. Well he is retired, that is, until a maid at his mansion turns out to be a 'cat burglar' named Selina Kyle who steals his beloved mother's pearl necklace, so he dons the cowl and cape again to track her down. After eight years of inactivity, Wayne isn't the same man he was, nursing injuries and a broken heart, and doesn't realise the size of his latest challenge. As it turns out, Selina has a debt with corrupt politicians who have hired a mysterious masked mercenary called Bane (an excellent Tom Hardy) to seemingly help them run Wayne Enterprises. Bane has other ideas though. He wants to destroy Gotham and sends his message through a brutal fight with the caped crusader. He doesn't care about money or power. He is on a mission. With Bruce Wayne at rock bottom, physically and mentally, can he find the courage to rise up and defeat his deadliest enemy? You will enjoy every minute of this to find out. He cant do it alone. With the help of Commissioner Gordon and a moralistic young street cop named John Blake, Batman has to rid the streets of Gotham's evil reckoning and save his own soul. You will be blown away by the sheer size and brilliance of the trilogy ending Dark Knight Rises- one of the greatest movies ever made. After you have seen this you will realise why this was the most anticipated movie of its time. Batman goes out in a blaze of glory... or does he?

10.title: the cinema viewing at its best
10.content: what a movie.........a clear example for how a movie should be..the tension build up and reaches the crescendo at the climax.....i m new preview but i cant put the thoughts and experience i had when i m watching here.... The at-the-same-time stylish and brutal visuals of the dark knight are replaced by a grittier, more hands on approach to the subject.As a result we get a much greater feeling of the environment in which the characters exist, and so it is perhaps easier to empathize, and/or sympathize with them.Also on hand is a colorful palette of characters. we see a multidimensional, pulsating, alive community that seems in need of a strong, sustained outside push to finally stop chasing its own tail and get out of this destructive cycle. this s a fine piece of art and an absolute filmmaking.i have never seen a movie completely with top performers and they all giving their best.this movie is better viewed in IMAX but i didn't get the chance of watching it there.but i loved every second of this movie.finally....TDKR is essential viewing, and is cinema at its most brilliant.In short, this is a superb achievement, and is easily one of the best films of the year, and of the decade so far .

10.title: The Dark Knight Rises
10.content:
"The Dark Knight Rises" certainly lived up to all the expectations. Christopher Nolan, once again proved why is the greatest director in Hollywood. At 165 minutes long, it never gets boring. It is full of great action, great dialogue, great acting and an amazing story.

"The Dark Knight Rises" is by far my favorite movie of what I've seen, and I really do not see any movie passing it for a while.

10/10

10.title: A suitable finish for an epic series
10.content: The Dark Knight Rises -- Not the usual superhero movie....Christopher Nolan ends his batman franchise spectacularly. An action packed, thoughtful, ambitious film which misses the high standards set by its predecessor by a scratch. FRESH-- Not the usual same old same old...The fact that the director managed to pack the huge storyline into a good package which entertains the audience is amazing. Though Nolan's series comes to a halt, the legacy of batman continues and one can hope to see another take on batman sometime soon. A must watch definitely. The movie makes one to search for reality within the virtuality. The storyline is huge and therefore you are not going to get out of your seat anytime soon, but believe me you would get more than what you would pay. All the characters play their roles admirably and executes them in style. The music is awesome as always, thanks to Zimmer. The score is amazing for the full length of the movie. A deserving finale to an epic story. I Don't want to leak any spoilers over here so i will stop here :)

10.title: Another Perfect Epic Batman Tale from Chris Nolan
10.content: Everything that was excellent about the Dark Knight can also be said about "Rises". The Dark Knight Trilogy is what super hero tales are supposed to be. Everyone in the movie is terrific. Bane is as terrifying and menacing as any movie villain in cinematic history. It's bizarre how a film can run well over two hours and it's just not long enough, or it just seems to end too soon. This work of art really follows the Hollywood rule of leaving your audience wanting more. I can't wait until the entire trilogy is packaged and released on Blu-Ray. Or better yet, I really hope Nolan, Bale and company reconsider, and get together for yet another chapter in the heroically tragic life of Batman and his alter ego Bruce Wayne.

10.title: An epic end to an epic trilogy!
10.content:
Right, first of all, to all of you haters out there who have labelled this film with such poor reviews....you must have watched the first two, so why on earth did you waste your time with this one just to give it such a rough time reviewing it! You knew what you were in for!

OK, the review.....this was indeed a fitting end to a fantastic trilogy. Trilogy's over the years are normally boring you to tears by the time the 3rd film comes along and there hasn't been a decent trilogy from first film to third since LOTR. But there is no doubt this is trilogy of the decade!! The acting from all concerned was superb. Bale, what a fantastic Bruce Wayne he has been! In this we see how trying his best to save gotham has taken its physically and mental toll on Wayne and the batman. He is bruised, battered and tired and you can feel that there is going to be an end to this batman and he is willing to make the ultimate sacrifice! Bale, the perfect choice to play the caped crusader!

Caine, what a performance! His portrayal of Alfred throughout has been brilliant but in this we see how much Wayne means to him and Caine squeezes out every ounce of emotion as he tries to convince Wayne not to take on Bane for fear of losing him! An excellent performance and a pleasure to watch!

Hardy, playing the ultimate villain. Nowhere near as crazed or manic as the joker and in no way unpredictable but Hardy played Bane brilliantly. You can't tell me that you would not fear this man?!?! Bane had strength, speed, an army, and intelligence! The only enemy of the Bat to beat him. The two fights they do have you feel every punch, kick and strike each of them throw at each other. Batmans fury as he tries his damnedest to beat Bane in the sewer fight was awesome!

Hathaway, she did indeed surpass herself in this with the best catwoman to date! Just perfect! Oldman, Freeman and Lewitt were all equally as fantastic!

What Nolan has done with this comic book hero, is move him away from the cheesy, far fetched stuff and made him believable. This is certainly what us comic book geeks have been waiting for and it has indeed been worth the wait!! I wish I could write more but I feel I would not have enough time to review this film as much as I would like. All I will say to you is, watch this film and it will blow you away! Well done to all concerned with making this film! The true fans salute you!!!

10.title: Dark Knight Has Risen
10.content:
Take a deep breath , bow your head & in awe you kneel down for you have witnessed one of the greatest movie in the history. This is movie making at its best. Chris Nolan has done it (yet) again. By the time end credit start to roll you would have been swept by a wave of emotional tsunami. Normally superhero movies are mindless action flicks,Dark Knight broke this myth in 2008 and now in 2012 the scale is bigger ,wider and better. Each and every aspect of the film is simply mind blowing. I am a great fan of 'Editing' in Nolans movies (Who can forget 'Prestige' and 'Memento'). Frankly speaking BatMan was never my favorite superhero but the faith Nolan has show in this superhero and the treatment which has been given to the character is simply amazing. Nolan has adopted Batman and turned him into a real hero. Unlike other superhero you don't want to see Batman perform just stunts for he is much more than a mere action figure. He is human and prone to failures. During the length of movie you are made to experience BatMan's pain, his fear & his failures.

TDKR belongs to Christian bail no doubts about that but Nolan has given sufficient room to other characters to shine through and CatWoman does shine. Shes a surprise package in the movie. Michael Caine can always be expected to give a strong performance and does he deliver? yes with a bang. Other strong performance comes from Joseph Gordon Lewitt. Looks like Nolan trust him a great deal.

About the story, since the screenplay is written by Nolan himself ( along with his brother) its fantastic as usual. Story is fast paced and runs along pretty well, there's a lot of stuff which has been carried over from part-1 and 2 so if you haven't seen those 2 movies (highly unlikely) then my suggestion is that you go and see those first. Action and special effects are top notch.I only have one problem with the movie, just because its running at a brisk pace few portions of the movie looks rushed into or may be that's only because I was enjoying the movie so much that I wanted more of it.

Nolan has confirmed that this is the end of Batman and after seeing the end you are pretty much convinced that BatMan has ended. To quote Nolan "Every story deserves a great ending and this is our attempt to give BatMan an ending he deserves".

We will definitely see the batman once again on big screen sometime in future ( may be after 3-4 years) in a reboot of the franchisee , created by some other team but will the batman ever be made to look so interesting and 'Human'? Slim chance ..I really doubt it.

10.title: He seems like a pretty cool guy
10.content: Through the third installment Batman finishes his legacy by fighting the bad guys and showing that he doesn't afraid of anything. There is more to this movie than an action film, it engulfs you into the characters emotions and the overwhelming circumstances. Bane is the most horrifying of all the villains, although his character isn't as fun as the Joker. We see Batman's limits and his efforts to surpass them. The plot is immersing and full of twists. Anne Hathaway's performance surprised me, but all others were out shined by Hardy and Caine. The fight scenes were suspenseful and satisfying although they were limited by the films PG-13 rating. The movie was shot almost flawlessly and the score was perfect. The scope of the movie is larger and is still able to pull it off.In comparison to the previous two but it is a completely new experience compared to TDK.

10.title: Excellent! Tom Hardy & Bane are incredible!
10.content:
If you haven't seen it yet then you are wasting precious time. The movie is excellent. Of course you have the action but it is more than that. This final movie of the trilogy really pushes the Batman character. He is tested physically and psychologically. The events develop in the same time as the character. If you are expecting just dumb action, this is not the movie for you. The cast is excellent and they did their up-most to transmit the pain and anguish the characters are experiencing. Tom Hardy is excellent in the role of Bane. He takes back the reality of the character: he is a general, a strategist and a torturer both physically and psychologically for Batman. He is the ultimate enemy and the biggest surprise ... you will understand at the end.

Tom Hardy had to work with his voice and eyes for this movie and he did an excellent job. At the end when Talia tells Batman the story about Bane, the prison and the excommunication from the league of shadows... the look on his face when she says that he loved her was incredible. His total expression changed. Considering he had a mask on the face and still be able to see the difference says a lot about the actors performance.

You are in for a few surprises that I will not divulge. Let's just say, the isolated Gotham is a sight to behold. It is beautiful and mind-blowing.

I think this is my favourite Batman movie and I am so happy it was not filmed in 3D. Very good choice from Christopher Nolan.

This is my favourite of the three. No offence to Heath Ledger, he was great it The Dark Knight. But for me Bane and Tom Hardy were even greater. Great lines, great tension and great performance.

10.title: An absolute stunning beautiful Masterpiece
10.content: The reason why this movie is my favorite of all time is the ending. I loved how it showed the ultimate sacrifice from a man. He cared so much about this city he would give everything. As Batman states to Selina Kyle "not everything, not yet". He gave them everything in the end. As always the movie was supported by great and emotional performances by Freeman and Caine. The major standouts were Anne Hathaway, Tom Hardy, and Marion Cotillard. The few twists along the way will please comic book fans like myself. When I walked out of the midnight release I had goose bumps up and down my body. I couldn't think of a better way to end the perfect trilogy. As this Nolan universe is ending I don't know how any director is going to step into the batman franchise and top what was done in these 3 movies. Everywhere from Hans Zimmer's score to the iconic performances from Bale,Oldman,Neeson,Ledger,Hardy, Hathaway, Caine and Freeman these movies will forever be my heart as the greatest trilogy of all time. I'm so grateful that I grew up when I did. Sad to see it go, but these movies are timeless and will always be in my play list. Thank you Nolan, Bale, and Zimmer for simply creating my favorite movies of all time.

10.title: First review because the movie is so worth it.

10.title: The Legend Ends with an Epic Experience
