From then on began the age of plot holes and Bollywood drama, I would just highlight some of the things that scarred me permanently, "how could you do this Nolan, how!!"

1) Batman whining in the prison was the biggest disgrace ever to the dark knight, world's best detective not only is tricked by Catwoman, beaten to a pulp by Bane, is forced to watch Gotham's destruction via TV. And all Bale manages to do is some epic melodrama!! Pathetic!

2) Anyways through means of numerous plot holes the dark knight arrives in time to save gotham(!!), only to waste precious time making a huge bat-logo on the bridge!!! "it's not the time for dramatics master wayne", wish alfred was there to talk some sense unto him!!

3) *Bollywood drama prevails* with minutes remaining before the nuclear bomb goes off, our dark (who at this point of the film was in no way dark, but for the suit may be) knight takes his time kissing catwoman goodbye, i couldn't bear anymore at this point, but taking ki from the dark knight i went on to finish the film.

* Honorary mention: the whole , i mean the WHOLE damn police force of gotham went underground!! these little things brought tears to my eyes! Oh! and the super redundant sidekick who recognizes batman at first sight, is the only police left over ground, finds the batcave all by himself. Bravo mr.blake, bravo!

In a nutshell, TDKR let me down big-time. Assuming it was not a nolan film, i haven't watched its predecessors and there was no hype to attached to it, i might have given it a 7. But that's not the case, as someone said, TDKR had more plot holes than a mosquito net!

5.title: booorrrrriiiing
5.content:
Too long. If you cannot tell the story in under two hours and make it interesting, its not worth telling.

I had no real empathy for any of the characters, including "Batman." I think Levitt could have made quite a good "Joker", if brought back, never a "Robin" though.

Anne Hathaway, passable but not as engaging as say,Moretz from "Kick-Ass?"

Hardy was quite good as "Bane" but not a patch on Ledger. His Sean Connery speaking through a blender was most amusing.

I think Caine was wasted, and his crying old man act, we only need to see this once per film Michael.

The film has become almost a blur in my memory and at an estimated $25000000 dollars, that really shouldn't be the case.

5.title: Meh! Its alright
5.content:
Since I don't get a hard-on from comic book movies and neither did I stand in line on opening night, I don't need to find a justification to give this movie a higher score. The introduction to this movie was pleasant, actually coming off rather well and establishing the villain (Bane) fast and why there is no Batman at the time. Also this was not shot in 3D, so the ticket prices were normal. That's was all I can actually say I liked about this movie overall.

Like the other Batman movies, Christian Bale sounds like he has something stuck in his throat (even more so in The Dark Knight Rises). He continues to do this even when people who he is talking to knows that he is Bruce Wayne. Tom Hardy does do a great job playing a guy in a mask, because it is hard to show any expression with your face when its covered. Also I think it is horrible how a cop figures out who Batman is (as a child) by looking at his eyes. Seems like a weak link in the story.

Also what is the motivation behind Bane and Talia al Ghul (Ra al Ghul's daughter). Its like saying "You killed my father who I hated, now I am going to kill everyone (including myself)." So much planning for revenge against a city that has no real connection to the League of Assassin's. Please remember I am writing this from the previous film's stand point, not the comics. And for you comic book fans out there, you had to be disappointed with the Robin reference at the end and not Jean-Paul Valley.

Now I did love this movie for the fact that Batman was not in much of the last half of the movie. I like Christian Bale, but I seriously cannot stand his Batman voice. I know I mentioned this before. Also to me some of the top billet actors did a sub-par job in this movie. I know Christian Bale does better work, look at American Psycho. I do forgive Joseph Gordon-Levitt, just because he doesn't shine with actors like Morgan Freeman and Micheal Caine in the same movie. I felt like the actors really didn't give it their all.

Can't really tell you how overall disappointed I was with this film. Honestly I say wait for Redbox, unless you need something to talk about at work. Also I would recommend watching this movie in theaters if you have insecure friends who need someone to back them up on how awesome they thought this movie was because they waiting through the long lines and stayed up till 3a.m. on opening night.

Overall this movie will definitely be overshadowed by its predecessor, The Dark Knight, just because of the outstanding acting in that film alone. So save your money, wait for Redbox and rent the Dark Knight at the same time to get a glimmer of satisfaction.

5.title: Why So Serious Nolan?
5.content:
I don't get the praise director Nolan gets; does he mix eye candy and brain food that well? No. Does he direct action scenes supremely? Surely not. Does he inject vital finesses of irony and charm? No. Does he pace and edit his films well? No. Does he get the best out of his actors? No. Most importantly, does he tell a good story? Not by a mile. Does he treat his audience with intellectual respect? Not a chance. The story of the entire Batman trilogy started out good enough, got mixed up and messy during the second installment, and as it goes in "The Dark Knight Rises" you're lucky if you understand half the things going on: Characters shift motivations in the blink of an eye, there's loads of shallow and unnecessary ideas, the need to use flashbacks in every other scene both over-explains and confuses, every single scene has something "incredibly" important to say as the plot chameleons through different stages and what happened to the word "COMIC" in comic books film? It's all gone. Nolan paints it black and takes us down to the depths of darkness, here we're given muscleman Bane to incarnate this evil and violence - forgive me, but his character snaps peoples' necks in an indifferent way, he talks too much and too articulate, and he's having a tough time outmaneuvering everyone's favorite villain from "The Dark Knight", The Joker (Heath Ledger). And the way Bane's utter importance disappears in the final third of the movie, as Marion Cotillard's (wow, that's a miscast!) character enters as the true villain, is laughable. Everything we've experienced throughout the 165 minutes with Bane as the numero uno bad-guy goes out the window as Cotillard's Miranda Tate, a member of the Wayne Enterprises and a flirting flick that blinks at Bruce Wayne, shows her true colors with a knife and strained explanations. She might be the worst character Nolan's added to the Batman universe. She enters in the final film with so much history, so much pizazz and trickery, and as a viewer I never felt her presence as neither a business executive, a romance interest for Wayne, or as a new, relevant member of the big Gotham family. Now she makes for one half of the film's female ground - the other is Anne Hathaway as Selina Kyle, also she a miscast. Her character is irritating and too important. She never really fails, she never really gets in any real trouble, she never involves herself especially in anything or anyone, she SUDDENLY becomes flirty with Wayne/Batman and co-operates with him, she has some feigned, badly worded jokes, and she's completely stupid looking in that catsuit. Now, in being too important I mean she takes way too much screen time, she's all too important for Batman to defeat the villains at the end, and she's very self-important though does anyone really mind her presence at all? Talking of too much importance, Joseph Gordon-Levitt as John Blake. This guy knows everything that's going on and he never makes a mistake, and he has some of the worst scenes in the film - when he explains to Wayne that "he saw it in his eyes", you really don't forgive Nolan and the screenwriters for getting away with murder as bad writing goes. The importance of this character is so overdone, so out of proportions that he almost outshines Jim Gordon (Gary Oldman) himself during the finale. Why is it Blake that stands on the bridge at the end watching the explosion and not Gordon? That would have had a significance, an emotional impact - but Blake standing there, no way. Or maybe it was a way to push Blake into becoming Batman's successor, a way of understanding the heritage of the hero - during the end we're revealed that Blake's original name is Robin. I really don't want to see Gordon-Levitt playing Robin in a fourth Gotham film, jumping around in Gotham without Batman.

The music by Hans Zimmer is unrelenting and monotone. The cinematography is fine, all dark, drained and grainy. The acting performances by Christian Bale enhances the movie's quality, he is a great actor and he has some very good scenes, including some dialog with Alfred (also a very good Michael Caine), the scenes in the "Hell on Earth" prison, the scenes in which he's crippled and depressed. Sadly his Bruce Wayne character takes a bad turn where he during the despairing emotions concerning Rachel's death and love for Harvey Dent suddenly takes a swing at Miranda. Sure, he's a lonesome wolf, but that doesn't help as he utterly shows no interest for anything or anyone earlier in the film (when Alfred states during the party that there was a pretty woman, he says he doesn't care. Or when Alfred jokes around that he's returning home alone without female company, we know what Wayne's been up to talking law and order with Selina inside the party). Morgan Freeman's character is downplayed some, luckily we get several good bits with Gary Oldman as Jim Gordon, one of the major assets of the entire Batman trilogy.

Much of the atmosphere and spark that was created in "Batman Begins", and that blossomed and spellbound in "The Dark Knight", fades away in "The Dark Knight Rises", and we're left with half the heart, and that half is not very good. Though it still is fairly entertaining and there are several things to mildly enjoy, it doesn't hold a candle against great superhero films as "X2" and "Spider-Man 2". With all this said, the film's biggest failure is it's running time, stretching towards three hours, it becomes an ordeal to sit through towards the end.

5.title: A half-hearted effort hastily done to close the series.
5.content:
I felt this movie was a half-hearted effort, made only to provide a hasty closure and to appear as a trilogy. The movie had a decent story (as expected of a Nolan movie) but there were several plot holes throughout and none of the characters were explored thoroughly. Joseph Gordon-Lewitt does the job of Commissioner Gordon who sleeps through most of the movie. I felt that Gary Oldman spoke like his character "George Smiley" in several places.

We hardly get to see Lucius Fox and any of the "Batman" gadgets namely the bat-claw, grapple guns, or the glider with his cape. Tom Hardy has good body language but at times it becomes difficult to understand what he is saying. The soundtrack was rather loud and interfered with the speech at several instances.

Christian Bale has performed really well as Bruce Wayne but his Batman voice was probably the worst in the series. It almost looked like Bale was spoofing the character himself, especially towards the end, lol. You can't help but feel that he has a throat problem and needs some sort of cough syrup.The Catwoman suddenly has a change of heart and decides to help? Her character does not have any specific motivations throughout the movie.

The plot twist towards the end was decent but it could have used some good acting on the main antagonist's part. I found myself laughing at the dialogues. It fell way below my expectations, considering the first two movies. This deserves not more than 5 out of 10.

5.title: Why is all this happening?
5.content:
First of all, this movie was decent entertainment and I did not feel cheated for my money. it has a great cast. The special effects never looked too much like computer graphics, which was refreshing. The overall look is not too stylish and posing is kept to a minimum. I was thankful for that.

There are however flaws. I am only picking upon the two that distracted me the most. The fist and most important issue is the motivation of the villains. They are basically suicide bombers with a timer attached to the bomb. The longest timer ever. If their goals is to eventually blow up everything, why wait for months? Is it to give someone the chance to stop them? Is this an awkward cry for help? If not, it must be to torture Batman, which on this scale is hilarious. Is Batman the navel of the universe? And then again, why perish together with all the captives? Self-punishment?

The second problem is that the past event are never brought back in more than a few words. For instance, I could not remember why Bruce Wayne is a broken and solitary man in the beginning of the movie. Was that explained by the last movie? Probably I should have bought and watched it before going to see this latest release. Or they should have made it a memorable experience and not the mess I remember it to be.

5.title: A Lot of Rise and Not much Batman
5.content:
There's enough reviews on here about The Dark Knight Rises for me to skip the details and tell you simply...

The Dark Knight Rises isn't as good as "The Dark Knight." Nowhere Near as good. All fans of the Nolan franchise can agree on that.

Batman isn't given enough screen time. All BATMAN fans can agree on that.

The villain 'Bane' didn't have the depth of 'Ra's Al Ghul' (Batman Begins) or menace of 'the Joker' (The Dark Knight) and was used mainly as a smoke screen for a sub plot of which there are many. Which brings me to ..

..The plot. No spoilers but there's a lot going on. Too much. Which took screen time away from the films main character...Batman!

I left the cinema feeling entertained yes, but cheated at the same time.

Some people (clearly by the amount of 10s handed this film loved it)

But I say if Nolan had changed the villain(s), shortened the film and added more action then The Dark Knight Rises would have been a more entertaining and engaging film. Instead we got Too much Rise and not enough Batman. 5/10

5.title: I thought bats were supposed to sleep during daytime...
5.content:
It is possible, that my expectations were just too high, but this was nowhere near The Dark Night. It didn't even surpass Batman Begins.

I think Nolan had some trouble figuring out a suitable ending to the trilogy, but seriously...

*SPOILERS AHEAD*

The whole movie was shot in sunlight. It would be okay for a Superman, or Captain America movie, but this is just ridiculous. The Dark Knight was truly amazing, because it reflected perfectly the chaos which was in Gotham City, but this was just like any other action movie. It had nothing to do with the original comics, except for some parts.

The whole idea to returning to the Ra's al Ghul theme was also a bit boring. I mean seriously... couldn't Nolan come up with something new? Bane himself could have been the perfect villain for this movie, i think the only possible explanation of bringing back Ra's Al Ghul was to fill the remaining one hour of the movie.

Some positive thoughts: The characters were quite amazing, especially Bane and Catwoman. We really should have seen more of them. The ending was also very confusing, but I actually like these kind of endings, when it's up to the viewer to decide what had happened.

Anyway, everyone who saw the first two episodes, has to watch this one too, but don't expect anything even close to the Dark Knight.

5.title: A disappointingly underwhelming conclusion to an otherwise overwhelmingly stunning trilogy
5.content:
Granted, it's not easy to generate a sequel that lives up to an epic prequel, particularly a prequel like The Dark Knight. Francis Ford Coppola did it once, the sequel to the Godfather was, according to many, even better. Satyajit Ray did it twice, with Aparajito and Apur Sansar setting the bars higher consecutively. Sadly, not only does Nolan not reproduce such heights, he falls several notches short.

Set as an aftermath to The Dark Knight, with an epic character of Joker portrayed to frightening perfection by the late Heath Ledger, Bane was always going to be pitted against him. None of Batman's enemies match the charisma of Joker, so it was fair to surmise that Bane will be as sinister as Joker, minus the dark charisma, perhaps. But the character was to be, in effect, THE essence of the movie, the character the movie would revolve around, the character that would frighten, if not quite mesmerize, us. Such a character, however, requires a solid backdrop, a potent script. Unfortunately, the movie has neither. A has-been superhero, who has gone into self-recluse for 7 years, severing all connections with everybody concerned, would need ample reason to resurge. However, what we find here is that all it requires is a heist job in a bank by a semi-masked man, and some 'Storm is coming' kind of soothsaying by a semi-masked woman to jerk him into action. Such heist jobs occur in untold numbers every day, everywhere, so were it the reason, he wouldn't have been a recluse even for a day, let alone 7 years. Alfred Pennyworth displays a wide range of emotions throughout the movie, but it is never quite clear what he actually wants, whether Batman should stay put, or come out of his shell and fight the evil, or whatever. A torrid one-night stand with Cottilard hardly adds any value, except may be disgracing the fond memories the audience has of the duo of Batman and Rachel. Cillian Murphy appears out of nowhere, and pronounces judgement on people, in what capacity, God only knows. Robin spends a substantial amount of the second half in just shoving a bunch of people into the bus and shoving them again after they come out. Gordon, a pivotal character in the earlier movies, spends the majority of the movie either in hospital bed, or just running around. Each and every character in the earlier movies were meticulously planned, their purposes clearly defined, most characters in this movie lack substance and look more like fillers than characters. An unbiased judgement would tell us that the CatWoman character was totally redundant, her only role was to create an illusion of two-facedness, that, alas, turns out to be disarmingly straight-forward. Even the 'twist' in the later part of the movie fails to leave an impression, and is a fundamental cheat, the twists in The Prestige, or The Sixth Sense, all leave trails for the audience to do some guess work, that's what which makes the twist so endearing, here it looks like a twist for a twist's sake, and adds another layer of superficial-ness to the movie.

And of course, none of the flaws are as disappointing as Bane. Even when not pitted against Joker, he fails to impress at any level at all, be it visceral or psychological. A movie is as good as its villain is bad - since when a thug and mercenary has become synonymous with bad? A character without any resolution (in fact even his death is poorly scripted, as if the director did not know how to finish him off), he is no different than a thug who leads a pack of weaker thugs who naturally gravitate towards someone who can show them newer levels of badness. He wears a mask that ruins half the effect, and the other half is ruined when he opens his mouth, it is difficult to figure out whether he is reciting passages from Macbeth or delivering supposedly evil lines, each and every line he utters, is grossly dramatic in both its substance and delivery, and one cannot but remember the crisp, terrifying and thought-provoking lines from Joker. He goes all out to destroy Gotham with an atom bomb, and after seeing thousands of movies relishing on this idea, one can't but say "Been there, seen that". Again, this reminds us of the brilliant social experiment Joker perpetrates towards the end of The Dark Knight.

Most ordinary movies provide at least a couple of interesting moments, moments one can later recall and marvel at, or laugh oneself silly, or ponder over. Unfortunately, while The Dark Knight provides a surfeit of those, its sequel hardly provides any. Not a single line, or scene stands out, and it has nothing to recommend a re-watch. A disappointing conclusion to an epic saga, thankfully it won't be able to undo what the previous two movies have done, and when we fondly recall the saga later, it will always be the charisma of The Joker, the menace of Ras-Al-Ghoul or the steel of Batman.

5.title: seriously....who is giving this movie a 9 or 10?
5.content: okay, so i see a great deal of you loved this movie....enough for you to rate 9's and 10's. are you people under 25 and haven't seen a real good batman movie before so consequently you had nothing to compare this film to other than "batman begins" and "dark knight"? please people, before rating this film, just go see the original batman movies directed by tim burton (batman-1989, batman returns-1992) and even batman forever-1995 directed by joel schumacher....then come back and give your HONEST opinion on this film. i bet a great deal of you "fanatics" will have a change of heart....and those 9's and 10's will be converted to 5's and 6's!! nothing compares to the original....so far!

5.title: Did I watch the same film?
5.content:
As a long-time Batfan, and having thoroughly enjoyed the other two parts of the trilogy, I was willing to meet this more than 90% of the way. Don't get me wrong, I enjoyed it at the time, but seriously, there are so many holes in the plot it's almost insulting. Bruce Wayne fine without leg brace; no consequences to his knife wound; Bane's cronies witnessing their first fight knowing also that Bruce Wayne is Batman (to reveal at any later point); Batman encouraging Gordon to light a flare on the dangerously thin ice upon which they stand; the child at the orphanage fondly drawing a bat sign at a point when Batman is still considered to be a homicidal maniac... the list goes on.

Plenty of scenes also come across as half-baked. Batman taking a few moments to ambiguously explain his identity to Gordon while the clock ticks on a nuclear device; Liam Neeson embarrassingly thrown in; the TV in the prison designed to torment Bruce Wayne easily broken by a lobbed projectile. And then there's Bane abruptly getting shot by 'Catwoman' on the bike; even the cast looked a bit taken aback after that. As soon as Bane ceased to be the baddie, the film had to deliver something exceptional to conclude, and it simply didn't.

Then there's John Blake's deduction that Bruce Wayne is Batman due to the look in his eyes?! I'd simply assumed that I'd heard this wrong in the cinema until discussing with someone else. It's difficult to understand how this dreadful and bone-idle explanation could have found its way into the film. Undermining the story's credibility so carelessly earns another star lost from my rating.

This is in my opinion a bit of a selfish film on the part of the director. The conclusion is the beginning; all Nolan wanted to do was to pack the punch of the 'death' of Bruce Wayne. Which I'm up for. Just do it in a more coherent and competent fashion.

5.title: Do not watch this if you aren't an avid Batman fan
5.content:
I am not exaggerating when I say that this is one of the most boring films that I have had the displeasure of watching this year. I am very glad I sneaked into the cinema to watch this, otherwise I would be writing an angry letter to the writers to ask for my $18 back.

It was nearly 3 hours of boredom. I literally had to stop myself from falling asleep about an hour in. I struggled through, expecting something spectacular towards the end, but to no avail. The fight scenes were shockingly bad and although well choreographed, lacked any realism (e.g. I didn't see one drop of blood on anyone after they had been shot multiple times). Also every single scene where Bane speaks you have to listen very hard to understand what the **** he is saying.

I am not just writing this review because I don't like Batman. I loved the 1997 film, Batman and Robin and I could watch that again and thoroughly enjoy it.

5.title: Long and Kind of Boring
5.content: I loved the trilogy, specially first two movies were revolutionary. Which I can't say about the this part. Movie itself was so long and i felt like it was boring sometimes. Batman was just so week, basically as a suited up regular human. Cast was great as in all movies.

5.title: Nolan's weakest
5.content:
What a disappointment! A structural mess of a movie, short of anything memorable. Clunky, poorly executed action set-pieces devoid of the scope and elegance I've come to expect from Nolan, plot holes, nonsensical story developments and a villain that triggers no emotion whatsoever. Also, for a director whom I have come to appreciate for his originality, this is a blandly unoriginal effort that at times reminded me of Pierce Brosnan Bond days.

Sure, it makes you cringe at times, laugh at others, holds a couple of surprises and it is entertaining, don't get me wrong. But even with all that and its forced epic scope, this is still Nolan's worst film to date.

5.title: Pretentious
5.content:
I'll be brief: the characters have zero, well, character, the movie is full of plot holes, the twists are not mind-blowing but mind-numbing and irritating, and to top it all off, the fight scenes are poorly shot.

It's pretentious and it fails: it has multiple plot lines of great potential, but none of them go full circle, leaving so much hanging in the air. If 2.5 hours is not enough, you might consider changing your plan.

I have to have at least 10 lines for the review to be accepted, but this film really does not merit so much text or thought. Nolan's Batman magic is gone and this movie is completely unnecessary - from an artistic point of view, of course. From the money perspective, it makes perfect sense. Too bad it won't be a flop.

5.title: Huge disappointment
5.content:
What a let down.

I have no idea how this film has gotten such high ratings.

I would have given this a 6 but I was just waiting for it to end about halfway through and that's never a good sign. It wasn't very entertaining. Someone has already mentioned on the message boards that the film was really shallow with bad acting and nonsense scenes. Well, I can't say that there was anything wrong with the acting but the story was a mess, most of it didn't make sense or wasn't clear enough.

A lot from the previous films in the franchise was re-done here like repeated one-liners, actors and past events which made it feel less original.

There was no character development and the film was nowhere near as funny as the other films. I didn't laugh once, I didn't care about this film at all and it was all just very unoriginal and uninspired.

The fight scenes were boring and poorly choreographed.

It took itself far too seriously and I hope they make one more which mirrors how fantastic the first one was with a clearer villain and storyline, funny moments and cooler fight scenes, maybe Bourne-style!

But this one was just a mess and extremely boring.

I did like the introduction of two "Batman" characters and I hope this is developed more in the next film, if there is one.

5/10

5.title: Dark Hype Rises
5.content:
Nolan and the team shot themselves on the foot trying to over-hype the film. I mean from guerrilla advertising to every annoying little details such as "get your t-shirt" or "action figure" on Facebook pages, by the time the film aired on big screen there was nothing more left for an intelligent fan to look forward to. Yes, it's a superhero film and plot-holes need to be overlooked, but so was The Dark Knight, which in retrospect seems to be a masterpiece only because of genius of Heath Ledger and not because of Nolan. I became huge fan of Nolan after TDK but after disappointment from Deception and now this film, it is pretty evident Nolan cares for big budget grossing and nothing more.

Sometimes much is left unsaid or unviewed. But just as I mentioned Nolan et al, gave away pretty much the entirety of the film in the trailer from start to finish without leaving viewers begging for more. Although the opening was brilliant and just like villains that make up the Batman series, I enjoyed Bane's performance but it was NO WHERE character driven as TDK's Joker.

My only reaction during the movie was when is this thing gonna end. Really? Three hours? I do not go to movies to watch self-patting director/producer for grandeur and magnitude that is supposed to represent "art". Other than comic con nerds - who by the way WILL NOT acquiesce to the fact of being deluding themselves (after all they waited lifetime for this movie setting aside countless dates and they would rather go with bandwagon instead of face the truth about negativity) - and fan boys, people DO NOT want to be drained by the movie where one knows - either through trailer or umm...common sense- that Batman will save the day.

For all the tl;dr's here's a summary why after Deception, Nolan lost the plot with TDKR:

too long of a movie making it a chore to watch - no character driven storyline - no interesting catchphrase - over-hyped by guerrilla advertising - just plain visuals, eye candy and CGI instead of subtleties - trailer gave away everything - movie makers were most concerned with money making instead of creating art


So there. Like Shymalan, now I will gladly avoid anything with Nolan tag to it and yes, I can see miles ahead that Superman one would be a major flop too.

5.title: Not as good as previous series.
5.content:
I felt the movie moved to fast at key locations and other non key locations sort of drooled on.

My biggest complaint of this movie and a host of other new movies is, music is played over top of lines being said by actors. Therefore washing out what the actors actually said. If it wasn't for closed caption one would never really know what was said. It is a shame that music is even in a action movie. Doesn't lend to the artistic capabilities of the movie. I believe this concept was bore from the silent movies and actually was creative. But into days movies it is a distraction and annoyance because the tone or beat is so out of step with what is actually happening.

5.title: Killings for nothing!
5.content: I remember hearing about 12 kills and 38 wounded for this movie. I expected something spectacular! I only saw Batman got his ass beat so bad than ever before!!! Moreover he ends up to a miserable underground prison, he eats this shitty food and like a miracle he finds his old strength out of nothing! No special moves, no action (except of *some* basic punches and kicks) at all. The basic evil character and our hero were fighting like girls! I don't remember not once Batman flying with his cape (a classic scene)... The girl (like cat-woman?) makes more special moves than our hero. I think this was a bad decision that the director made. Another drawback is that the main hero-characters Batman and Commissioner James Gordon, where wounded so bad for at least half of the movie. This spoiled all the action. I wanted to see actions from these characters, not the side ones (Selina Kyle and Blake). Lucius Fox seems like an old guy who even can't climb a small ladder-see scene. The worst Batman movie (even the one with A. Schwarzenegger)... Big disappointment.

5.title: Not so great.
5.content: First off I have to say that I'm not a huge comic fan, but I can enjoy a good movie of any genre. I thought Batman Begins was okay, and I liked how Christopher Nolan took it in a different direction. Then came The Dark Knight, which I thought was nothing special. I could be wrong, but I think the death of Heath Ledger is really the catalyst for The Dark Knight being so overrated. Sure, he had an awesome look and was eccentric, but there is just something shallow about him and the movie. Perhaps it could be I can't identify with the characters. After seeing The Dark Knight Rises, I just can't see what all the hype is about. The plot is boring and I just don't care what happens to the characters. After reading some of the negative reviews for this movie I can't understand how people could love the other two movies and not like this one. It's basically constructed in the same manner. On a side note I watched the Blu Bay version of this movie and the sound mix is just awful. The music and voice volumes are so off from one another that you have to turn the volume down when an action scene occurs so the music isn't overwhelming, but then you have to turn it back up to hear what anyone is saying. This isn't a terrible movie but it shouldn't be getting the rating it has. I would say at best this movie is a 6.5 period.

5.title: "Batman" Good Plot, but Technically Poor and Very Violent
5.content:
I saw "Batman: The Dark Knight Rises" after the incident in Colorado. I talk a lot about that in my opinion piece, which you can read in all the usual places, including AmericanEntertainmentReport.com

The point I made in that column is that is impossible for most people, including me, to not think about this movie in the same way as those who saw if before the tragedy did.

I didn't care for this movie that much. Most of my reasons have to do with poor production values and with the acting. Technically, I didn't think it was very good. I noticed several bad edits, out of sync audio, and one fight scene between Batman and the bad guy where you can tell the film was sped up. This was a "keystone cops" quality effect not worthy of the amount of money spent on this film. At almost three hours, this movie was WAY too long. It drags in spots where it should be moving along. I also was disappointed that there was no bat mobile and it lacked the gadgets we want to see coming out of the caped crusader's utility belt.

The cast list has Christian Bale back as Batman/Bruce Wayne , Gary Oldman as Commissioner Gordon, and Morgan Freeman back as Fox. Quite frankly, these three usually fine actors appeared to be there more for a pay check than to do a good job.

Tom Hardy is the new villain, "Bane." While convincing, the silly mask he wears makes him hard to understand at times.

The stand-outs here are Joseph Gordon-Levitt as the young police detective who "gets it," Anne Hathaway as Selina (aka "Catwoman"), and Michael Caine, who is again marvelous as Alfred the butler.

Here is the place where I am not sure what to say. I found this movie one of the most violent I have ever seen. It disturbed me. So I must ask myself: "Would I have thought the same thing if I had seen this movie before knowing about what happened in Colorado?" The answer is: I will never know.

The movie has a good plot, but the ending is a little predictable, so the best I can give it is 2 out of Fordyce. Since I don't want to spoil anything for those of you who may wait a while to see this film, I will just say we are left with the possibilities of much more from Batman in the future and a strong hint of who will be dressed in the famous cape and cowl next.

Should you stay or should you go?

Credit Check:

Nothing happens after the credits roll.

5.title: Disappointed
5.content:
This isn't really i review but more of a rant but before i start i didn't hate it but i was left unsatisfied. As a big fan of the first two i was hoping Nolan would build on what has gone before and give the audiences what they were hoping for. Instead what we got was nearly three hours of unfulfilled potential and a terrible story.

heres a list of what I felt was wrong with this movie. 1)Bane is ONCE AGAIN relegated to being a henchman! 2)'Breaking the bats back'. What we got was a poor fight scene shot in close up ending with a back breaker with all the power of a WWE rookie. This leads to.. 3)The prison scenes. Completely tacked on scenes about Bruces recovery. The back breaking story arc is reduced to a slipped disk and 5 months recovery doing press ups. Also during the climbing scenes, if bruce fell that distance with a loose rope tied around him he probably would have broke his back again on each attempt. These whole scenes felt tacked on to me, they didn't reveal anything or drive the plot, their only purpose was to drop massive hints about what the 'plot twist' at the end. I feel that Bruces recovery could have been better explained if he used a variation on the device that he used on his knees to help him walk again. 4)Why on earth did we have to be treated to another story about Ra's al Goul. Couldn't we have a story with Bane having his own agenda. This felt lack of imagination on behalf of the writers. i understand they probably felt they were bringing things full circle but for me it just felt like a cop out. 5)'The autopilot debate' all through the movies they have talked about batman being a symbol and can be anyone. So Mr. Nolan why didn't you have the courage to kill off Bruce when you have set up the means to do so through out the film. Blake could have took the role of Batman during bruces recovery for example. Also Batman says he hasn't given his all, surely sacrificing himself to save Gotham is doing just that! Batman doesn't get to have a happy ending..

I could go on with other issues with this movie but i wont. There were some things i liked, Catwoman was handled better than i thought it would be. The special effects and the cinematography was superb as usual and Gotham has never looked better, especially as we got to see it during the day. Nolans Batman movies have always had great performances from its cast and this was no exception and Micheal Caine was the real heart of the piece, giving a strong but short performance. I understand i am in the minority in my views but they are just that. I wrote this little piece for my own benefit really, just to get my thoughts down as i was so frustrated. The Avengers/Amazing Spiderman had me smiling as i left the cinema, TDKR left we sad inside.

Thanks for reading and take care!

5.title: The Dark Knight Rises - Another Millennial Marvel Movie
5.content: Remember the old days of movies, when they were rated R or X because of adult content? Well, after the year 2000, films should now be rated the same way, but with M - Millennial Content, as a red flag for adults. This rating system would accomplish two things; it would tell Millennials that here is another big hit for you, and would prevent adults from wasting their hard-earned money on films that are better left to comic books and animated films. This is one of those films; another in a long line of meaningless imitations of what the real 1930s Batman comics really intended; a dark, atmospheric city, where crime was around every corner, and where decent people had to struggle to get by. This film conveys very little of that atmosphere. Try again.

5.title: Enjoyable but underwhelmed
5.content:
Dark Knight took my breath away for many reasons but unfortunately the same was not true for The Dark Knight Rises. I shall cover the negative points first so we can get it out the way.

The adverts for the film over recent weeks showed some incredible scenes which I thought were just a sample of what the film would deliver. Turns out that those scenes were mostly all the film had to offer. The amount of characters taking focus in the film made it quite confusing, jumping from one character to the next. Understanding Bane was a challenge in itself which detracted further from the story. Finally, 2 3/4 hours was quite long and could have easily been shortened but still captivate the audience (definitely has to receive such a great review by many though).

Now for some good points. Its Batman and he is awesome as is Cat Women (naturally). Story is quite enjoyable despite jumping around such a great deal. Some spectacular moments visually but a little underwhelming in comparison to Dark Knight.

In conclusion, I respect Mr Nolan and his work, I am just not sure it was presented as well as it could have been.

5.title: Over Hyped Action-Movie
5.content:
The Dark Knight (2008) is probably one of my favourite movies of all time. IMDb gave this new batman film, The Dark Knight Rises a 9, placing it in the top four greatest movies of all time. This was more disappointing than Prometheus and I was close to playing a game of solitaire on my phone for the last hour of the movie.

I think what plays an important role in determining the quality of batman films, and other super-hero films, is the villain. The Joker (Heath Ledger) was terrifying because he really had no motives for his actions, he just enjoyed putting people in situations with impossible decisions. He also had personality and wasn't physically superior so he had to turn to alternative methods to create terror and chaos. This meant that you didn't have your stock-standard fist fight every batman scene.

Bane (Tom Hardy) is a very menacing looking guy and appeared to look like a very good villain. However, upon watching the movie, I discovered that his actions really had no motives. I found it extremely difficult to follow what he was trying to accomplish. At first he was a mercenary, then he turned into some sort of martyr for freedom and liberty but controlled the city through means of a dictatorship.The twist at the end with Miranda (Marion Cotillard) where it was revealed she was the child that escaped the prison was cringeful and silly, because neither me or the audience really cared about this character.

On to the prison, where is it exactly? And this League of Shadows? Perhaps it's some contextual thing from the comics but should be explained. Bane justifies his actions by saying he's returning power to the people. He does this by releasing a thousand criminals and arming them with automatic rifles. So no one in Gotham decides to take action against this guy? Seemed like the residents weren't having a great time under this new regime.

A nuclear bomb? Wow that's incredibly original stuff from the Nolan brothersAlso the police of Gotham use their tactical skills to run into a hundred or so guys armed with guns. Luckily for them though, this tactic paid off because Bane's private army decided to have a punch-up instead. Hopefully this movie doesn't inspire people to raid the stock exchange, it seemed all too easy to bankrupt a huge company.

Some positives

Catwoman (Anne Hathaway) was a welcome surprise and wasn't just Batman's apprentice, she actually had her own agendas. Batmans new fly mobile was cool and the special effects all round were good. The soundtrack was quality and fit the action sequences well.

Overall I think this movie deserves a 5/10 pretty much because of all the weird stuff the come on screen. The final battle went on for too long and this prison thing was just plain random. I can't see why people would think this was one of the greatest batman or even eclipses the quality of The Dark Knight (2008).

5.title: Disappointing!

Marion Cotillard's character was half-baked and she made it worse with her pedestrian acting. To make matters worse, in a movie that is about 2 hrs 45 minutes long, there is only about 20 minutes of Batman...its a finale of the Batman series...am I expecting too much here. The only highlights are the last 10 minutes of the movie, some scenes here and there, Bale, and always wonderful Freeman and Caine. Overall, the movie is just a pale shadow of the previous installations of the trilogy.

5.title: Disappointed
5.content:
As a big Batman fan and collector, I saw this movie in the summer when it came out and have just seen it again after having purchased it, but must say I am disappointed.

There are epic scenes, the actors are consistently excellent and the themes of heroism, sacrifice and family match well with the first two chapters of Nolan's trilogy. Unfortunately, the basic story is a mess.

Just cup your hands in front of your mouth and repeat Bane's speeches and see how ridiculous they sound. The Braveheart battle between the police ( who have spent 3 months locked in tunnels, but have fresh clean uniforms) and the mercenaries should have included 'Pow', "Bam' and 'Wam' flashes like the 60's series. The last battle scene even has a major mistake, where Talia is alternately shown as being alone and with a driver that ultimately disappears from the cab of the truck carrying the nuclear device.

Like I said, I am a big fan of Batman and have loved all of Nolan's previous work, but the movie let me down for the above and many more reasons. Would recommend only to Batman fanatics like me.

5.title: Fan Boys Will Hate Me. Sorry.
5.content:
I don't know if Michael Caine and Anne Hathaway's excellent acting could even redeem this dime-a-dozen special effects extravaganza.

Many of the fight scenes appeared poorly choreographed, badly filmed, and were often devoid of appropriate sound effects. Seemingly unpopulated bridges being blown-up in too-distant shots made me feel like I should call a civil engineer out instead of Batman. And while the lack of copious amounts of actual blood flowing should have been refreshing, it seemed a little weird to see dead police officers sprawled-out but no blood pooling around them.

Now on to the acting: I can't decide which death scene wins the gold for worst acting ever: Sofia Coppola in Godfather 3 or Marion Cotillard's in this movie. As for Bane, each time this character's overly-loud and difficult-to-understand voice emerged, all I could think of was Albert Finney's role as Churchill. Additionally, didn't anyone think that more body and/or facial gestures would be an appropriate acting necessity for a man whose entire mouth and nose were covered??? Perhaps a little more eye grimacing, eyebrow-raising, neck movement, or arm flailing, anyone?

Aside from the aforementioned performances of Mr. Caine and Ms. Hathaway, the story itself failed to engage any aspect of human emotion - being utterly anemic and lacking in its ability to pull the heart- strings of the audience. How do you write, film, and produce a "hero" film without anybody giving a crap emotionally about the hero? Or to have a villain in a film without evoking any element of fear? Furthermore, I don't know how they succeeded in showing an imprisoned mother being attacked and killed before her child's eyes without me giving a hoot about it, but they did. There were very few times in this whole movie where I felt like anyone was in significant danger (or even cared)despite the fact that guns were being shot, things were being blown up left and right, and a flippin' nuclear bomb was poised to blow up the entire city. Was the "drag the little orphans out on the bridge" scene supposed to get my pulse up? Because it didn't, and as we see towards the end of the movie, most of Gotham's citizens were all holed- up safely in their little homes anyway.

This is all compounded by the fact that Christian Bale's performance in this movie is mind-numbingly dull; sure, he can recite lines and groan a little when his vertebrae are supposedly being shoved back in his body, but other than that I'd struggle to give his mediocre performance a "C" in a community college theater course. The movie would get a "B" for effort.

5.title: Fascism versus anarchy
5.content: A few thoughts on Christopher Nolan's film 'The Dark Knight Rises'. Firstly, a positive: I'm a sucker for films which play on the audience's sense of vertigo, I thought the window ledge scene was by far the best thing of the three 'Matrix' films put together, and there's also one scene in this film that's genuinely heart-in-mouth. The others are less positive. One, the standard elements of the blockbuster genre appear to have been done to death - 'Watchmen' also featured a plot based on the misappropriation of a source of potential power, while Cat-woman here has a moment that is pure Han Solo. Two, Nolan goes to great length with his use of computer graphics to depict Gotham City, yet still chooses to demonstrate the existence of its population in the form of a single bus-load of schoolchildren. Thirdly, whatever made anyone think that Bat-man, in any form, was a story worth spending nearly three hours telling? Comic books have their place but it's not that of the epic. Fourthly, as in Nolan's first Bat-man film, there's a storyline based on a pseudo-Eastern Jedi-esque world that feels as if it's from a parallel universe to the urban world of Gotham. Finally, the message of the storyline could be summarised as, when faced with a choice between fascism and anarchy, the former is to be preferred every time. I don't think Nolan is a fascist - but that he can make a film so long and yet so simplistic is in some ways indicative of what is wrong with so many mainstream movies. And yet this is by no means the worst film of it's kind. But views that it represents some kind of masterpiece are symptoms of expectations lowered by a sea of inanity elsewhere.

5.title: Decent Plot, Lackluster Direction
5.content:
I never saw TDKR at the theatres because I'd heard it was all about terrorism and Occupy Wall Street nonsense, so I was pleasantly surprised to see that the movie has much more of a French Revolution plot to it. In fact,I really liked Bane's plan: turn the city over to "the people" after stoking up the class-warfare thing, and then sitting back and laughing as The People destroy society through mindless chaos and violence.

I wish more of the movie had been about the trials they started conducting (with the Scarecrow as Judge). You know, it would have been the corrupt rich on trial first, then "regular" rich people, then upper middle class workers, then the middle class. The crowds would have gotten bigger and more bloodthirsty until finally people started to realize that they'd run out of "villains" and were just killing their neighbors at random. Would there be food riots in the streets? Would private militias form? How would petty crimes be handled by the residents? What a great concept for a Batman movie! Unfortunately, we spent too much time with Bruce Wayne and his personal problems and all this other extraneous stuff with a degrading nuclear bomb, and villains in love, and old friends breaking up/reuniting, etc.

Plus, the movie seemed to be plodding along much of the time. Direction was poor and on the level of a TV show. Place the camera, have a bunch of extras play-fight, and call "Cut". Very little suspense was ever built up, as characters showed up in a scene, hit their marks, and moved on. Fights between Bane and Batman were poor.

Why hire a good actor to play Bane if you're going to cover up his face the whole time? Was that his real voice? What was he saying the entire movie? I never could tell. As far as I knew, Bane was just a big bald guy with a weird mask.

I think any episode of "24" was probably more suspenseful, had better dialog, and was better directed than TDKR.

Also, how would the NFL classify that football game? Did the touchdown count?

I thought Bane was an excellent Baddie, ruthless, strong, intelligent. The Plot was fine - the other characters sufficient - the devil for me was in the detail.

Gotham was in lock-down for how long? The cops were trapped underground for - months was it? Weeks anyway. They came out of there hole looking shiny and new. Nolan - go and stand in the corner with Lucas and Cameron - Damn it! Another £15 wasted.

5.title: Read more at schneid-remarks.blogspot.com.au
5.content:
I'm going to just rip the band-aid off quickly before it becomes too excruciating. The Dark Knight Rises isn't very good. There, I said it. Before I devour all the faults of the film, I want to make it very clear that it's not awful. It's an okay movie, and had it been the first film in the series (even if that would have made absolutely no sense) I would have been a little less harsh on it. But the simple fact of the matter is that I couldn't walk into this movie with an objective point of view because I've seen the first two Batman movies and I love them to bits. It is humanly impossible for me to detach those two movies from my mind while viewing this one, and I don't see any reason why I should. A precedent was set, and said precedent was not lived up to. I would also like to clarify that precedent is different to hype. I actually wasn't very excited for The Dark Knight Rises. I tried very hard not to think about it and let it creep up on me. I remember talking with a friend of mine and saying "when we see The Dark Knight Rises" and subsequently realising we were going to see it the following week! I was more hyped for The Dark Knight than for The Dark Knight Rises, and I was far more satisfied with it than I was with this. Here is why.

One of the major problems I had was with the pacing. God, it was all over the place! The first act lasted all of about 5 seconds (that may be a slight understatement), jumping from scene to scene introducing characters and plot points far too quickly for them to feel anything but artificial. Right after that, we were treated to a horribly stretched- out second act where nothing of much significance happened for the first half at all. The third act was a little better, but still not nearly as tight as what we'd ordinarily expect from a Christopher Nolan movie. The epilogue could also have gone on for far longer than it did. This is the end of an epic trilogy! It's fine if they spend some time finishing everything up (also, real quick, the ending was half good).

As well as the bad pacing, there were some plot points that I really wasn't very happy with. There's one really big thing that I found completely ridiculous (you'll know it when you see it) which brought down the movie by a large portion in my eyes. Additionally, the film opens with an eight year timeskip that feels totally unnatural. Batman has disappeared, Bruce Wayne is a hermit, and none of the actors look like they've aged a day. The film then proceeds to spend the entire first act telling us how Batman and Bruce Wayne coming back (or rising, I suppose) is a big deal and everyone's been wondering where they've been, but it doesn't work at all because we don't feel the same way about any of it as the characters in the film do because we never experienced the absence of Batman or Bruce Wayne.

On a more positive note, the acting wasn't too bad. But that's about it, really. Some of the returning characters felt a little underwhelming, but that was mainly due to a lower quality in writing than anything else (Batman's badass retort to Bane: "No, I came to stop you"). Tom Hardy did a great job as Bane, especially with his severe limitations. The distortions on his voice are by no means intimidating, which I really appreciated. I was dreading hearing his voice because I thought they would make him sound like a Transformer just because he's supposed to be so huge and overpowering. I was mega wrong, and I love everyone involved in that decision because it's one of the best things about the movie. On top of the voice, we don't ever see his facial expressions, so his performance essentially relies entirely on body language, which must be incomprehensively difficult. Anne Hathaway as Catwoman was nothing special. She did a good job, but there was nothing special about her. That's sort of the case with the entire cast, really. Except Bane.

There was also absolutely no reason for Catwoman to be in this movie other than for fan-service. Were she to be taken out of it, it would have made almost no different to the plot at all. She really only does two or three things in the entire film, and none of them are character- specific in any way. Batman also blindly trusts her for no reason at all. There was no point where she proved herself to be anything other than a villain, yet Batman doesn't even seem to consider this.

One thing I admired about The Dark Knight is how little CG it used. This is primarily the case here too, but there are a few noticeable uses of it. And I mean NOTICEABLE. You'd think that with a $250000000 budget they could get some good CG. Seriously.

I know that I'm dwelling on the negatives here, but none of the positives are all that remarkable, to be quite honest. The movie was okay, but it was plagued by countless problems that neither Batman Begins or The Dark Knight suffered from. There were a few sections that feel like they were changed at the last minute, and the whole package just didn't feel nearly as refined and perfected as The Dark Knight or Batman Begins.

Well, now that we have this generation's Star Wars trilogy, bring on the reboots!

5.title: If you like the Dark Knight, and if you like Batman Comic Books, this is not the Batman film you should see.
5.content:
I was so hyped up for this film. I've spent most of my life reading Batman comics, watching Batman movies and TV shows, and just being a huge fan of Batman.

When Batman Begins came out, I went and saw it in theaters, and left a little less than impressed. This was not the Gotham City I grew up on. But after reading different graphic novels depicting Batman's growth as a hero, I began to gain an appreciation for the film. I gave it a 7/10.

Leading up to the Dark Knight, I kept up closely with the viral campaign, the set photos being released of Ledger as the Joker, etc. I was actually excited for this one. I had grown to love Nolan's Batman, and couldn't wait to see the next film. Seeing it for the first time, it was like watching the perfect film. 10/10.

After I started a podcast with my friend Zac (zacandchuck.com, buzzsprout.com/3269) we started to cover everything that came out about the Dark Knight Rises. Bane photos (I defended Hardy), speculation over John Blake (I speculated he would be Azrael), the awaited return of Ra's Al Ghul (Huge letdown. Nolan had the body disappear, foreshadowing... NOTHING.) and the question as to who Miranda Tate was.

I predicted that Miranda Tate would be Talia Al Ghul (correctly), and that R'as would return to Gotham to destroy it, using Bane as a pawn. Batman would be injured and would enlist in someone to fight the good fight for him. Seeing Azrael fail, Bruce built up his strength, and went back out to take on the League of Shadows. This is what I thought was going to happen. What did happen, was a messy, long, poorly explained film involving Batman characters doing the opposite of what Batman characters do. Batman had given up. Alfred would go on to abandon him. Bruce retires the fight that is his and only his, and passes it on to someone who isn't trained, and has no business wearing the Batsuit.

This film was terrible. The only redeeming factors were Anne Hathaway's performance as Catwoman (I thought she would suck, and she blew me AWAY). and Tom Hardy as the chilling Bane. If you want to see Batman give up, retire, come back, save the day, and give up on avenging his parents death? This is the movie for you. But that is not my Batman.

5.title: Over-hyped. Nolan disappoints this time.
5.content:
I love what Nolan did with the Batman story. Batman Begins was great, The Dark Knight was simply a brilliant masterpiece; so I went into the cinema full of expectation for this third and final installment.

I was a bit let down. It was a good stand alone movie, but with a poor story even if it had not been the final of the trilogy. Again it had a great cast that did their job well, though their characters this time around were quite flat and two-dimensional.

It was definitely not, as great as The Dark Knight and I especially did not appreciate how Nolan carelessly destroyed what he had Batman and Gordon build with their sacrifices at the end of the second movie, as if it was a bad mistake. Surely, he could have exonerated Batman in a different way without turning his hard work and sacrifice into nothing, by bringing out the truth about Dent.

Overall, the story felt as if it was put together in a hurry, and the movie did not feel very solid as a whole. Maybe it will look better the second time around, though I highly doubt it. The mistakes in editing didn't help much either, but will not insert spoilers here.

Again, an OK movie though a disappointing end to the trilogy; it could and should have been better.

5.title: Batman...The Messiah
5.content:
He took others sin upon himself to protect his world (read Gotham). He was persecuted for it. But he still loved his people. And finally gave the ultimate sacrifice so that the world would be saved. Sound familiar?

Everything Nolan did with the first two movies made Batman very plausible. This movie is some where between the comic book world and theology and just doesn't seem to be sure what it is. For me its a huge let down from the predecessors. In fact, I'm not even sure if this is a "Batman" movie...Batman barely even made it to the screen, probably had the same amount of time as Catwoman. So Batman was a supporting character in this movie.

Rock solid performances by the whole cast but completely let down by an overambitious script trying hard to be bigger in scale than its predecessor. Catwoman was the only 'human' and 'plausible' part of the movie. The only smart piece of the script in my opinion. And kudos to Anne Hathaway for delivering on it.

I must admit, the first thought that ran through my mind after Avengers was how soon can I get to watch it again. No such feelings here; in fact far from it. I'm debating if I'd want this Blu-ray when it comes out. :(

5.title: Batman, Champion of Wall Street.
5.content:
The Dark Knight Rises was an interesting movie with a very interesting message, but so far as entertainment value goes I can't help but feel it missed the mark. While it had a strong start, the first half entirely enjoyable, the movie breaks down in the wake of Bane's initial triumph and seems to plod on about an hour too long from there. While I'm a big fan of the actor who plays Bane, thinking his work in the movie Bronson was tremendous, the character is too one-dimensional to be an effective follow-up to the Joker, and can only provide some enjoyable fight-scenes.

What I'm wondering is this: how many of you out there picked up on the message of this film? It's not exactly subtle. While in the first movie Gotham was clearly a fantasy-city full of weird monorails and towering, Gothic skyscrapers, it became an every-city in the second movie, largely indistinguishable from any other. In this movie however, it's entirely clear what Gotham resembles and represents: New York City. From the Islands to the bridges, it looks just like it all of a sudden. What they've done here with this film is produce a thinly veiled criticism of the Occupy movement, and similar sentiments that are against rampant capitalism. Think about it. When Batman saves the innocent hostages from Bane's evil clutches, who are they? Stock brokers, from Gotham's Wall Street. When Bane gives his 'we the people' speeches, who does he sound like, talking about rising up against financial oppressors and retaking the streets from corruption? A lot like occupy. The one character in the movie who criticizes wealth itself? Evil betrayer. Alternative and green energy solutions? Turns out they're evil too, and terribly dangerous. If you understand the applications of film as propaganda, this is a pretty blatant example... and, like most superhero movies these days (Avengers, Man of Steel, etc.), it insists on conjuring up images of 9/11, with clouds of dust filling streets and chasing fleeing citizens. The habit of using that image to try and get people emotionally attached to an action sequence is to me an example of Hollywood at it's most crass.

5.title: Considerably less "NOLANISH" than the previous Batman Movies
5.content:
Yes, even though the critic has been really good, in my opinion this movie hasn't been so good. Before arguing why I think this, I just have to say that this was a very, VERY awaited movie, and that could prompt a more careful critic than with other films. Its just that if we have received Masterpieces from Nolan, we just want another Masterpiece as simple as that!. Now, why do I think this was a slightly bad film?. Well, the reason is simply because Nolan didn't respect the style he previously developed, and what's that style?... The Realistic/Dark Superhero Style. What traits does this Great Style include?: 1. Profoundity of the main characters. 2. Great Acting, that complements perfectly the complexity of the characters (and a great sense of realism in the behavior, ideas and gestures of the characters) 3. Realistic weapons, effects, combat strategy, and also influential economical and political situations 4. The sense of surprise given by the fact that, Anything can happen! (because being realistic, you don't become attached to a happy ending.

So, we'll just have a review of how did the movie failed in maintaining this style. Here it goes a series of facts in the movie that... are no good:

First, there is a considerable problem with the plot: If Bane and Miranda wanted to destroy western civilization, how would they do that if they only destroy one city? (and they die in the act!!). I mean, they, in the name of the "the league of shadows" (and by this mean they were the only active members of "the league") want to change the course of things in the hole planet, and what they are going to do is exploit NY. Well, that's not enough!, because that certainly would be a massive killing, but with no after Master Plan!. Maybe, an alternative way of managing the plot would have been Bane is got to destroy the city while Miranda continues the plan in the long term.

An important fact of a main Character (like Bane), is that when I hear that, Bane was born in the worst prison in the hole World, I imagine something like the worst prisons of Venezuela. Yeah, it's a shame for me to admit that there is such an Awful Management of the prisons. But the point is, in this prisons there are gangs, weapons, fire combat, raping, slaughter, total corruption, and a complete chaos because there is NO LAW. So, don't tell me, that the Whorst prison in the world is no more than a bunch of old Uzbekistan dudes exhorting others to get out of the prison, like saying "Yeah dude!!, you can do it!". Also an important fact of the character of Bane. If he was born in the worst prison, or we could say, one of the Pits of terror in this Earth he just couldn't have a heart; he surely would be a Hard Psychopath. Even as a way of surviving... But no, now, because we like Soap operas, it seems he Has a heart and well writes Poetry like Neruda inspired by Miranda! (when did this became "the beauty and the beast??).

Another super Unrealistic fact is that, if the cops were trapped underground for like... more than three months!!, they surely would have died or would have committed cannibalism!!.

The war/combat scene, with the cop's running forward like in the Lord of the Rings come on!!, how would the fight like that!!! (I mean, the enemies have guns!, and so did them!). In fact, if you are playing "realistic", you should have thought in a complicated warfare, that surely end when Batman gets the bomb out of the Island! (because the US army would enter an take control over the hole situation)

The acting of Marion Cotillard wasn't very good. Didn't got my attention in the hole movie, (maybe because the film it's not too centered on her), BUT, the dying was so F**ing badly acted!! My god!, the dying of the frogish father in law of Shreck was more touching!!.

Finally, an over-elaborated and cliché happy ending. First, what's the thing with a Kiss in the end?, I mean, I thought this was a movie that would consider realistic situations: So, if there is a Freaking H bomb that is going to exploit, and Im gonna take it out of the island, I better DO IT FAST!!. And if we consider that the character with the decision is a Righteous Bruce Wayne who wouldn't waste time, it doesn't make sense. Second, if they showed Batman in the "Batcopter", and the H bomb exploits, then Batman simply should have died, and don't tell me he could have ejected, an atomic explosion is so freakingly destructive, that affect miles and miles. So the hole "Batman is still Alive to bang Catwoman", is nice, but, then again, against the striking Nolan Style. Like all the other facts.

My final observation is that, there is a fact: the Nolan films are realistic mind blowing "craftworks", and because of that, are very laborious. But, in my opinion, he should have avoided the idealistic- cliché style, and work more on a modest but mind blowing ending for this fantastic Batman trilogy.

5.title: Review of The Dark Knight Rises.
5.content: We all know what a suicide note means, but have you ever heard of suicide review? 5.title: Too Much Nolan, Not Enough Batman - The title should have been- The Dark Knight Goes Flaccid
