4.title: Weakest link in the series
4.content:
This movie just didn't do anything for the series.

The writing was lazy and you needed to take great leaps of logic to allow the story line to become acceptable.

The characters really were treated poorly. No real depth was given, and they often seemed force into a certain role rather than look as if they naturally belonged to it.

The end is guaranteed to annoy you. Normally after a Batman movie the audience is buzzing when it leave the theater. There was quite a subdued feel after this one. Nobody seemed terribly excited about the event.

You will have to be a major Batman fan to get anything out of this one.

All in all a rather boring,predictable, and disappointing film.

4.title: Dark Knight Rises - not for me
4.content:
This is the weakest of the trilogy. After the first two being superb, I came away feeling let down. Don't get me wrong, it's an OK movie, but could have been so much better. Some scenes just look too fake. And, I miss the magical, supernatural feel of the first two movies. In this movie, you don't have the feeling that there is anything special about Bruce, that he's very weak and just another human, that without ingenuity, would be slaughtered. It's also too long, with periods that lose your attention and could have easily been edited. Liked the ending. But, the story was all over the place and the music is too loud - frequently running over the conversations, making it difficult to hear the dialog. Saw it in IMAX and it was painfully loud, which also distracted from the movie itself. Will see it one more time in a theater with better volume control, but I don't expect to walk away feeling much different about the production or storyline.

Update: Saw the movie again at another theater, which was better than IMAX for noise level during the first 3/4 of the movie, but most scenes towards the end of the movie are still too loud; especially when Bane is talking and all the fight scenes. Most often you can't even understand what Bane is saying.

As far as the movie itself, it's still just OK. Don't like the character Bane at all and storyline is weak. There are too many main or potentially main characters with only bit parts, which makes the movie too long, for one, and gives it a feeling of incompletion and confusion. There are also parts of the movie that are not just unbelievable, but impossible.

My hubs will, of course, purchase a copy for his collection (in the future, when it's much cheaper), but I have no plans to watch it again.

4.title: Doctorate level concept + 6th grade level execution = FAIL
4.content:
Abandon hope, all ye that fear SPOILERS! SPOILERS BELOW!!! YE HAVE BEEN WARNED! AAaarrggg.....

Bottom line up front: I found this movie to be EXTREMELY stupid and, frankly, insulting to the intelligence of ANY audience above the age of say....12.

Right off the bat, the film insults the audience by asking us to believe that:

1) Super high speed CIA operatives handle the conduct of covert prisoner exchange and transportation the same way they would a flubbed fast food order in a drive through.

"Dude....I didn't order onion rings, did you? No? Oh well, we're good, let's roll."

2) Criminal "masterminds" are stupid enough to try capturing AN AIRCRAFT IN FLIGHT using another AIRCRAFT IN FLIGHT by lowering hijackers on ropes/cable from AN AIRCRAFT IN FLIGHT.

Seriously? Come on man! That was a RIDICULOUS premise, and the effect LOOKED as stupid as the idea! Writer: "O.K., and then they'll lower themselves down to the plane WHILE IT'S IN FLIGHT...yea! That's it! That's believable!" No. It's not. It's a stupid idea, and it LOOKED stupid in the film.

ALL THAT STUPID before the movie even gets started....

But the stupid never stops. It just keeps going, and gets WORSE.

The Batman gets into a fight and sustains a debilitating back injury that can only be corrected through....prisoner medicine, ropes, push ups and sit ups!!!????? - An ENTIRE POLICE FORCE is stupid enough to be trapped in a sewer system. ALL of them.... WTF? - An ENTIRE POLICE FORCE is stupid enough to use civil war tactics, ie charge as a mob, against an entrenched force using automatic weapons.


A federal government is willing to just write off a large metropolitan city.


People can't manage to get into, or out of, a city undetected. Right.


There's just too much stupid to list in this film.

We are ALL willing to suspend our disbelief in a film, and that's one of the reasons we go to films. However, the film maker has to put some effort into it to make it look plausible, otherwise, it just looks stupid, and becomes irritating rather than enjoyable. This film seems to have taken a bunch of shortcuts that turned what could have been a good movie, into an irritating farce.

If a 6th grader was told to write a superhero script, I would imagine it would be very similar to this movie.

4 of 10 stars.

4.title: The Dark Knight Flop
4.content:
I've never been a huge fan of these new Batman movies like everyone else seems to be, but I recognized as an avid movie-goer how well constructed the first two were in the series, and therefore how enjoyable they were to watch for the characters, story, and cinematography.

That being said, nothing in this film works.

First of all, why write in an 8-year span in the canon between TDK and TDKR if you're not ever going to fill in that back story, at least with even a little bit of fluff? That was the first thing that put me off. Along with that bit of poor writing, you have the "too many bad guys" effect; Bane is built as the main bad guy for the entire movie, then is undercut in the most horrible way, and then the "overarching" bad guy comes in and gets taken out within 10-20 minutes of revealing themselves. And then there's the threat of a nuke. Ugh.

My second quarrel is with the characters. You're introduced to three or four new characters right from the beginning of the movie and only one of them gets a developed back story. Now I know this isn't LotR where the story is essential, but seriously? Catwoman acts with zero moral ramifications, but by the end of the movie she's suddenly a good guy? (And I won't go on about how horrible Anne Hathaway was) Batman is hardly ever on screen and when he is it's mostly to get his ass kicked by Bane. Now I liked Gordon-Levitt's character because it added a normality to an otherwise frequently unrealistic (and here I'll mention the doctor in the Pit) sequence of events, but I didn't feel any depth to his character. Bane was... disappointing. You can't understand him half the time and he is no where near as terrifying as the Joker. He's supposed to be cruel and calculating and downright evil, and the biggest threat he asserts is a nuclear device... lame. And then Miranda/Talia: well, let's just say I was unhappy with her character as a whole.

The action is so stylized that you can almost see the gap between the character's punches and reactions; it's so cheesy. The gadgets are something we've seen before, other than the Bat (but that gets blown up in the nuke and hardly ever does anything anyway). The fight between the mercenaries and the police was corny, unrealistic, and stupid. I mean, they're firing pistols and AKs and there's no gunshot wounds. Seriously? Then there's the end. Oh God, what did they do with the ending? I honestly felt like the ending was written by M. Night Shyamalan. It was THAT terrible. It left gaping holes in the plot, showed a lack of interest in the direction of the movie, and was just ludicrous.

So in summary, not a terrible movie by today's standards, but I thoroughly disliked every bit of it.

4.title: The more time passes, the less I like this movie
4.content: To be frank, I absolutely HATE the Bane character. Right from the moment I read that Bane would be the main villain in this film, I was wary of it. That didn't stop me seeing it multiple times and buying the Blu-ray, but the more I reflect on it, the more I realise that despite its overall coherence and impressive action sequences, the narrative is riddled with stupid plot contrivances and the plot itself is driven by incredibly stupid actions by the characters. First, the idiot CIA man who takes three prisoners on board his aircraft during a covert extraction without checking either their identities or their cuffs (or shooting them on the spot or even running them off at gunpoint, which maybe he should have done). Bane himself takes a huge and probably unnecessary risk in delivering himself into the stupid CIA man's hands too, in that he already has the professor as a prisoner. Next, Bruce Wayne being basically disabled and far less intelligent than in 'Begins' or TDK at the start of the film, a stupid contrivance that is the basis of monumentally stupid actions by him later on. Next, Bane breaks into the Gotham Stock Exchange in full view of the public and executes a computer program that bankrupts Bruce Wayne (and affects no other wealthy Gothamite, as far as we see in the movie); however Bruce is too stupid to simply demand that an investigation take place, since it's obvious (and he has evidence on the flash drive he takes from Bane's hacker) that some form of ridiculously overt fraud has just been perpetrated by Bane. Bruce then reveals the location of the clean energy device to Miranda Tate, a woman whom I'm fairly certain from my viewing of the movie that he's only ever met once, despite her investment in his controlled fusion project. His background check on her is also revealed to be useless, as he only finds out she wasn't always wealthy when she tells him herself. Next, the ultimate stupidity in the movie, how someone as intelligent as Bruce Wayne, having been only recently told by his doctor that he's basically disabled, decides to put on his old Batman suit (he could have even had Lucius rustle up that stupid 'iron bat' suit from the 'Knightfall' saga to support his wrecked skeletal system) and go toe to toe with someone who is clearly itching to break him in half, without at least trying gassing him, tranquilising him (which we see him do to other thugs later), tasering him or even throwing a few concussion grenades at him, resulting in him having his back broken and then dumped in an underground hellhole while his nemesis converts a fusion reactor into a bomb with a countdown of six months. Those who insist that despite the damage to his skeleton, Bruce is still as strong as he was before clearly don't understand infirmity and just to make sure no one misses the point, Bane actually taunts Bruce's weakness as they fight. Clearly, Bane wasn't made cleverer than Batman, Batman was made stupid to serve the plot. This however is no more stupid than the original 'Knightfall' storyline; Nolan simply should not have adapted it for his third film. Then consider the stupidity of the GCPD in allowing themselves to be trapped underground with no reserves to even direct the traffic (and if you don't hold sufficient personnel back to function as an effective force, you haven't maintained a reserve). Next, Bruce Wayne's broken spine is miraculously healed by a punch in the back and a few sit-ups, one of the most stupid plot contrivances ever, but worse, his other physical disabilities are cured by him simply getting his push-ups program back on track. While heroes making spectacular recoveries from life threatening injuries is a cliché of just about every movie genre, this 'recovery' actually insults the audiences' intelligence (I note here that Batman was cured of his spinal injuries by magic in the 'Knightfall' saga too, another reason why Nolan shouldn't have used it as the basis for this movie). Those who argue that Bruce's back injury wasn't so severe as to paralyse him may have a point, but putting myself in Bane's shoes here, I'd make damn sure that if I'd captured BATMAN, that he wouldn't be walking ANYWHERE until well after I'd executed my masterplan, if ever. Then, having been rescued by the miraculously rejuvenated Batman, the GCPD then executes a frontal assault against Bane's forces; fortunately for them Bane's forces stupidly decide to give up the massive advantage favoured by the defender (particularly in an urban environment such as Gotham) by obligingly rushing into the attack themselves and almost everyone seems to forget that the battle scene that ensues belongs in a movie like 'Kingdom of Heaven' or 'Lord of the Rings', because they're all carrying 20th century guns rather than medieval weapons. Then, knowing that Bane has the clean energy device, Batman gives Miranda Tate a gun and turns his back on her, even though he should have least suspected she might not be trustworthy. While there are a few other plot contrivances that just laughable rather than dumb, mainly in the handing over the role of Batman to John Blake, who will no doubt be killed on his first patrol in the armour, having not even had Bruce Wayne's ninja/league of shadows training (while I'm on the subject of Robin John Blake, does anyone actually believe that Joseph Gordon-Levitt could kick Christopher Judge's ass? Presumably that's why it took place off camera), the out and out stupidities I've listed above make me wonder how the director of the sublime 'The Dark Knight', the incredible 'Inception' and the excellent 'Batman Begins', a director renowned for the intelligence of his movies, could be responsible for this stupidity-dependant travesty of a Batman film.

4.title: and it could have been so good...

4.title: #Not a Hiptser
4.content:
I should say that I did not give this movie a relatively low score because I was "trying to be different" or whatnot, in fact most of the time I agree, and am glad that I agree (makes me feel more sane/normal) with the rest of the population. I love the dark knight series, Nolan movies, and I like to think that I generally have good taste in movies...

now, it is also possible that my expectations where simply so high that they were unattainable; part of me expected a similar jump in quality like the one from "batman begins" to "the dark knight," and this no doubt also contributed my disappointment to the end of the trilogy. But let's get on with the first main problem.

I rather liked the non-conventional ending message of "The Dark Knight"- where most movies tell us that saying the truth is the most important thing no matter what, but tdk recognized that there are situations in which "the truth isn't good enough" and that a people sometimes deserved better. A great way to end a film.

And then the dark knight rises comes along and almost seems takes it all back by saying, "Oh no, we made mistake, you need to always tell the truth, and never lie" making the film appear much more conventional and in a way diminishing the ending of tdk.

This point is more personal opinion, but I think the joker was the best villain in the trilogy, Bane didn't have any flaws (aside from his voice), but I personally felt the jokers chaotic and unpredictable character (and actions) made him a more memorable villain.

I know this has probably already been mentioned, but some of the (main) plot point elements were just a little too unrealistic (in the realm of super hero movies) for my taste, the whole sending of the ENTIRE police force down the tunnels to find bane was simply not logical, any militia would instead block the exits, set up guards and possibly send in a small scout team.

The part were bane defeated batman for the first time was pretty cool, it was during batman's "recovery" where I had a problem. Normally the hero has to learn something, or learn to do something, that is then used in order to have a different outcome in the second confrontation. Here the "thing" batman had to do was (imo) very underwhelming

Basically all batman had had to do was jump a ledge. When he made the jump I couldn't hep but think "well that was fast, are you sure you're ready to take on Bane again? Will this newfangled jumping ability really help you take down a enemy twice your size?"

Another personal opinion, but I feel that the whole "nuke" thing has already been overdone. The ending of tdk was very good, particularly the part in which each boat had the other boats detonator, or the part where Harvey Dent Turned- the ending of tdkr on the other hand, had no such moment (at least not for me). In fact several scenes gave me a negative emotion

1. The charging scene. This scene really broke my immersion with the film because it was just so unrealistic; no modern police force that uses firearms is going CHARGE in another similarly armed force, it just doesn't work anymore since weapons no longer take more than a minute to reload. This scene also bothered me because I felt that the more realistic alternative would've actually worked better (normally would consider excusing such a thing if it helped with the films emotional impact).

Having the cops take positions over any available cover and slowly struggling (with sacrifices) to take more ground, doesn't sound too bad, or hard to do.

2. Banes Defeat. As you can probably guess by now, I didn't like how Batman beat Bane in a fistfight. This is not supposed to happen. Batman is simply not stronger than bane, what batman IS, is that he is smarter than bane, an ending where batman outsmarted or/and used his gadgets to defeat bane would have been much preferred.

in the end Tdkr was not a terrible film, it had some good moments (the intro scene with the planes was terrific) but I certainly don't think its one of the best films of all times.

4.title: not a real Batman movie
4.content:
This is a rather boring movie mainly consisting of shoot outs, explosions and other CGIs. It is NOT a real Batman movie. Jack Nicholson as the Joker, Danny Devito as the Penguin, Michele Pheiffer as Cat Woman, Heath Ledger as the Joker, Tommy Lee Jones.These were all great actors playing great villains and they made these movies. In this movie there are no interesting villains so it cannot be a real Batman movie. So who do we have in this movie as villains.

4.title: Does not rise enough
4.content:
While I thought "Batman Begins" was good, I consider 2008's "The Dark Knight" to be not just the greatest superhero film ever made, but one of the greatest movies in general. I'd been wondering if this would be another example of the 'second film is best' syndrome. Superman II, Wrath of Khan, Empire Strikes Back, etc.

It took me a while to get to "The Dark Knight Rises" but I finally can confirm that it's the weakest of the three. Which is not to say it's horribly bad. It's not; however, I'm afraid the bar had been set too high from #2 for me to not feel the anguish of weak villains, cynically inept characters, moments of badly acting and dialog, and an overall plot that I just could not fully accept. Alas, I couldn't recommend this film.

4.title: dreary scripting and too much cutting scenes
4.content:
I waited to see this film yesterday... rather excited.. rather thrilled to be finally seeing this highly rated film. But as the film started it soon became abrupt it was yet again another American action film fail. with too much action, dreary scripting and too much cutting scenes, making it very irritating to watch. I don't feel this way because I dislike the genre of film... I dislike it because it lacks the basic principles of a good film. yes, I am a huge fan of action/super hero films, but ones that are actually well developed and well presented (such as the likes of the matrix, inception, even x men) but this film not only lacked development, it seems that Hollywood has yet gain made the classic mistake of a too much action and not enough sole.

A few reasons that I shall mention to why I disliked this in this 'film,' is simply how unbelievable it was. The scene in the desert, in which bat man ends up getting imprisoned in a tomb where he has a chance to... 'climb out' to freedom..and when he does so he all so casually walks out the well with no one outside to stop him (even though there is a town right near it) and unforgivably this was not only which made this scene diabolically ludicrous- batman ends up back in gothem in a few days... - when it is meant to be on lock down.. not forgetting that he no longer has any of his precious bat devises.

I also believe there was no good characters...due to the quick cutting of scenes and lack of developed insight into each character it left no emotion...even batman became some what irritating. Bane was such a poor bad guy...with the bad guy in the dark night making a 'joker' out of him - he just mumbles all the way through the film and just keeps talking.. The fight scenes, terribly acted and poorly choreographed.who ever scripted this film needs to seriously get his act together...or even better... the actors need to lean to act. very poor lines.... one example is between dane and the bat creature... dane proclaims 'have you come here to die batman'- the bat creature replays 'no I have come here to kill you'. erm seriously? a 4 year old could right better quotes then that...and I know a few these actors could learn a lesson from. just poor.

And no mr Hollywood, attempting to add a cleaver twist into your dull film did not give you any higher ratings from the likes of me. It was so bad it saddens me to dwell into it, *sighs*

I shall now add a little sentence into why this film managed to gain a generous 4 out of 10.. 1 for CGI.. 1 for the cat womens fighting and 2 for Mark Webbs hair.

4.title: The dark knight rises as a Power Rangers and falls (screen)
4.content:
When i was a kid, there were those Japanese shows with costumed heroes who were fighting very seriously villains in real cities. With this choice of putting Batman in the same vision, i reached the same conclusion: it's unbelievable and funny. This Batman seems totally tiny in a huge Gotham, all the more than he does now his job in plain daylight instead of being a force in darkness.

As a batfan, i don't really find my character as well: putting away the hood as his beloved dies is OK but living as an old hermit isn't true to this icon: as Miller felt, the old Bruce is a man who is driven mad by his strong drive to put the hood back. The Batman is bigger than Bruce Wayne: it's an urge, a need that seems totally forgotten here. On the other hand, i haven't read "Knightfall" or "No man's land" but those plots were interesting to adapt: The scenes of having the elites assaulted and being put on trial were the more dynamic of the movie but they would have been more impact if this rebellion has a more charismatic leader with a vision (as in "the cult").

Beyond this, the movie doesn't leave the actual trend of blockbusters movies: it's a sequel for followers only because contrary to TV shows, there isn't a few seconds for "previouly last movies". The dialogs worth nothing and it's always the far-west in a democracy where it's about fighting opponents with guns and violence. If there's a good cast (Bale, Cain), there's a lot of transparent participation (Hathaway, Cotillard,...).

In conclusion, there's nothing Dark in this knight and the movie is totally overrated for its anticipation and Oscar run.

4.title: A disappointing follow up to an amazing film.
4.content:
-May contain spoilers.- I don't even know where to begin with my criticism of this film. What I can start off by saying is that after the sheer amazing storytelling performed in The Dark Knight, this movie failed utterly to follow it up. I think the main reason was because in The Dark Knight it was not Christian Bale as The Batman you found yourself relating to, or even rooting for, but Heath Ledger as The Joker.

Once more we find a film where the bad guy seems more human than the supposed hero. I found that I could relate more to Bane than I could Batman. Though not as good as The Joker, Tom Hardy does a decent job of playing his role as Bane, the once-imprisoned mercenary whose only sin was losing his humanity for the love of a child. His frank honesty and seemingly heartfelt desire to liberate the common man really struck a chord with me and I spent the entire film hoping he would pull it off.

Once again Christian Bale delivers a wooden, unbelievable role as The Batman. Poor acting and the pure goofiness of how he changes his voice once he dons the costume lose it for me. Unlike the first one where a large portion of the movie is spent with The Joker, Bane's appearances are far and in-between so you get to spend more time with Bale as Batman on screen and this killed it for me. One scene in particular towards the end where he is beating on Bane, asking about the detonator had me cracking up at how campy Bale's "angry voice" is and how stupid his mouth looked as even it moved over-dramatically with his spoken words.

Sadly, even Michael Caine's performance as Alfred was cheesy and his supposedly emotional scenes were unbelievable and just plain dumb. Though I have to say that Anne Hathaway provided some form of relief with her performance as Catwoman, though she looked the part more so than any previous attempt at Selina Kyle, she could not put a "scratch" on the surface of Pfeiffer's 1992 performance as the same.

As I like to make my reviews unbiased, I can honestly say that even from the standpoint of someone who enjoyed the comics, this movie took one too many liberties. Where the original Robin was the child of circus performers, this movie tries to introduce him as an orphaned police officer.

I only give this movie four stars because of Hardy's redeeming performance as Bane. Otherwise, this film did not come close to touching even the worst of films in the Batman series.

4.title: Another overrated Nolan flick
4.content: Nolan is one lucky filmmaker, always enjoying big box office and critical acclaim while most of his movies/stories are -for the sake of intellectuality- overly structured, making them dry, unsubtle and artificial. As an audience, you end up watching it as a series of moving pictures (literally.) Thus you're emotionally distant... So far Nolan as a filmmaker has the same effect on my face as a decent amount of Botox injection would have. Whereas movies are and should be about making you feel some sort of emotion. They should make you care about the characters. I'm not gonna get into his technical side as a filmmaker. And I definitely don't think that's where he lacks. His problem is much more simpler yet a fundamental one. The screenplay. To have a moving script, you really need to let it go at some point. If you intellectualize it too much, in other words, if you over do it, you'll end up with poor dialogues where characters will just say what you want them to say, not what they would say naturally. When I was watching the movie I could almost picture Nolan and his brother arguing about what the cat woman SHOULD say etc. That's usually not a good sign. It means it lacks credibility in my eyes and from that point on I don't care what happens to the "hero." It just breaks my heart to see films like this and the Avengers have much higher ratings than, say, All About Eve.

4.title: Somebody forgot the whole idea of Batman
4.content:
If Batman walks up to the bad guys and starts beating up people in broad daylight, it only shows that somebody forgot the point of this mysterious vigilante.

Spoiling the main character is enough to make a movie just dull experience with a predictable chain of events and action sequences that finally leads to taking out the bad guys.

This one felt like 4 hours to me as I really enjoyed the last 2 movies.

Production level was great as it was expected from a big and ambitious series of Batman origin stories. This final movie just lost it's attraction when characters are thin shadows from the original comic heroes/villains and everything meaningful (like character development, dialogue and emotion) was replaced with over dramatic action and suspense towards to the final showdown.

4.title: I was really disappointed by The Dark Knight Rises
4.content:
I was disappointed by The Dark Knight Rises. Honestly, I thought it was very amateur. And I thought the initial idea behind it was pretty flimsy.

First of all, I think Bane is a very poor choice of villain. Not that Bane isn't a good character. I don't think he was right for this movie. I'll admit, I prefer it when Bane is more bestial and animalistic, and completely hyped up on army drugs. But, that's just a Batman fan nit-picking. Even if I set aside my pet peeves and personal preferences, I can name at least five Gotham villains better-suited to top off this trilogy then Bane (I'm quite partial to Harley Quinn or Deathstroke.) I just don't think Bane was right for it. He just doesn't have zazz. He's got no flare, he's not that menacing, and he didn't have what it takes to end this trilogy with a bang. Not to mention, in the last few seconds of the film he was demoted from boss to henchman. He was a poor choice. Especially as a follow-up for Heath Ledger's Joker. Granted, Ledger isn't the best Joker out there, but he was the only thing holding The Dark Knight together, and put on a very good performance. He was going to be a tough villain to show-up. And Bane was not the villain to do it.

And then there was Catwoman. I was so disappointed about Catwoman. But it wasn't Anne Hathaway's fault. She did justice to Selina Kyle. I was sad she didn't get more screen time. But the limited screen time isn't my beef with Nolan (that's another bone to pick altogether), it was how Catwoman was written. The animal-loving, over-the-top environmentalist aspect of Catwoman's character was virtually non-existent, although that's basically been erased over the years. But even through the bad writing, Anne Hathaway managed to deliver a satisfactory performance (although I wasn't too fond of her costume.) But what annoyed me was the role Catwoman had. She was reduced to little but a no-name half-assed love interest with no major impact on the plot. The only thing that made her memorable was her actor and the fact that she's CATWOMAN. Had it been some randomly-generated love interest, it would've made no difference. The Catwoman aspect just wasn't there. She didn't swoop in and rescue Batman. She watched from the sidelines, occasionally decided to interfere here and there, but did basically nothing. There was no Catwoman in this movie.

There were so many unnecessary plot twists in this movie. I was vividly reminded of Steven Moffat's take on Doctor Who because of them. That's no compliment. Poor characterisation, cramped dialogue, too-fast plot, and most notably, inexplicable, unnecessary, ridiculous plot twists that leave your head wheeling. I think a good plot twist is one that clicks. One that makes you go, 'Oooh! So that's why this happened and that's why he acted this way!'. A good plot twist needs hints leading up to it and shouldn't leave your viewer feeling like they need a moment or two to figure out what's going on. Well, I needed a whole half hour and second viewing to finally make sense of Nolan's film. That's not a good plot twist.

The Miranda Tate plot twist—pointless, unneeded, headache-invoking. It's only real impact is the devaluing of Bane as a villain. Seeing as his character barely stands as it is, this definitely did not play to Nolan's favour. The Alfred leaving plot twist—not as bad, still unneeded, corny, but all the strings were in the right place. I liked the feeling that everything about Bruce Wayne was falling apart. I didn't like the sap-filled dialogue and dream sequence. Although it acts as an emotional trigger, it wasn't that relevant. There was no aftermath of Alfred's departure apart from an errant comment here or there, and a few sap-pumped scenes from Alfred's perspective. Although not a plot twist, Bruce Wayne making the leap—rife with plot holes, although the set-up was nice. Although we all knew that Bruce was going to make that jump, my fingernails were digging into my palms as he scaled the wall. But it's the events directly after and leading up to that scene that bugs me. Nolan is so often praised for how realistic his version of Batman is, that I found nothing but irony in the fact that Bruce was able to recover from a misplaced vertebrae by damaging his body further, and the fact that he was able to magically teleport from a prison in the middle of nowhere to Gotham City, just as it's about to be blown to smithereens. Nice realism, Nolan.

And then there was the story line. Two words. Batman Begins. This entire film was déjà vu. It's just Batman Begins revamped. Usually I could forgive that but—wait, they're part of the same trilogy and made by the same person? Not only was it Batman Begins .02, the plot progression was predictable and see-through. But plot predictability isn't always a bad thing. But I feel like Nolan tried to make up for this transparency by tossing in those terrible plot twists I mentioned before, giving us all a tumour in the process.

All in all, I was merely disappointed by this film. I don't hate it. But I was excepting so much more. And Nolan failed to meet expectations. As a comic book adaptation, this movie was no good. As a standalone film, this movie was no good. As a political movie, this movie was no good. To polish off a trilogy, this film is acceptable, but not ideal. All in all, as a movie, this is no good. As a wrap up? A thorough meh. Nothing more than eye-candy and a sleeping pill in one. But as a movie? No good. On an off note, I liked Bane's voice. Oddly enough that was a point of irritation for others as pessimistic as I was about this movie.

4.title: A good action film but it disappoints in a big way.
4.content:
A good action film but it disappoints in a big way.

So what's there in this that's better than the other Chris Nolan films, is style and the magnanimous production design where now, we have exceptional aerial shots and many of them hovering over the fictional city of Gotham. But what's missing is the soul of Nolan, the screenplay. The music by Hans Zimmers is OK OK and more melodramatic than action packed. The editing is too very bad coz too many details that lead to nothing are presented in this 2 hours 25 minute saga that could have been done in 2 hours, only if the extra characters of the board members and others were cut down and those many aerial shots were cut down too. The dialogues are way too bland for Bane (Tom Hardy). Bane is not anywhere close to be menacing but at the end he turns out to be doing, what Miranda Tate (Marion Cotillard) says. No, great villain either. And coming to our batman, he fails in a fight and he has to redeem his freedom, he takes an ordeal of doing a climb that takes more than 10 minutes of screen space. Was so much necessary is what I ask now. Also, there are identities revealed only at the end like that of Robin or Talia, ah too much suspense being held till the end is not a good thing, we don't need oil when the food has been cooked up.

The saddest part turns out that Alfred who has protected Wayne for such a long time, cries for he has failed Bruce Wayne. The much sad part is Bruce Wayne has to now live in exile as he is presumably dead just to be shown in a frame to reveal that Batman cannot end. OK, yes so he used autopilot too but that's so impertinent at the end coz we would have been exhausted by dialogue after dialogue for a large part of the film which take away the sheen. The dialogue I must say, is very clichéd and even amateurish from a man who has written Dark Knight and Inception.

Now, remember this is a sequel for Dark Knight so we do expect a big ride, so nothing like that anywhere, this is rather a slow paced dramatic and less action packed turmoil that takes us through the torture of being a superhero. The blessing in disguise, although is Catwoman (Anne Hathaway) oh, she comes up with some good acting skills and is in fact our hero, coz she killed the villain. Yeah, we know that 'he who kills a villain is hero'.

So, it has got good things but they are far away from each other. It's an okie dokie kinda ride and a 2/5 would be apt as per me. But if you have high expectations coz it's NOLAN you are a welcome aboard member to a disappointment group.

4.title: Not a great movie
4.content: Truly speaking the acting has let the movie down. The story line was Good but the action and camera work was very average. I had big expectations from this movie specially following it up with the Joker's Dark night. Marion Cotillard who played Miranda in the movie was definitely the weakest performer. The scene at the end where she died was very blunt and seemed so fake. The Catwoman (Selina ) hardly had any substantial role of catwoman the way it should be according to the DC comics storyline. I guess Anne Hathaway had the looks of being The catwoman but somehow her personality didn't click in that role. I Could picture Angelina Jolie performing better characterization of Selina. Overall I was disappointed with the movie and hope the next one will be a better action movie.

4.title: Not a perfect Ending..Not a Brave one
4.content:
I was expecting a brave ending from Nolan I thought probably he would end BATMAN and the TRILOGY with this movie. I will explain later why the ending is not a brave one..

Here is my review in short. My review contains some spoilers be careful.

BANE -- Yes i will compare him with Joker. Whats the point in having another sequel if this villain doesn't outperform Joker. Sadly Tom Hardy was wasted in this movie with his entire face covered with mask.The character is way too theatrical hey Wait is that Sean Connery's accent ?? Nah some Irish boxer's accent (Someone we all can relate to !!! ). Bane is depicted as Mastermind terrorist, extremist but wait he is also the voice of Occupy Wall-street movement.

BATMAN/BRUCE WAYNE --- The entire movie is based on batman. And if entire movie was bad, Bale hasn't done justice to his character. Come on. He easily forgives Catwoman for helping Bane break his backbone.

CATWOMAN --- Yep she is the REAL surprise of this movie NOT the TWIST at the end but Anne Hathaway's performance. She plays smart vulnerable sensitive yet dangerous character. You wouldn't wanna bull**t with her.

ALFRED --- There is a scene between Bruce and Alfred that leaves you with a lump in your throat. Apart from that he is wasted. He appears in the beginning and the end.

MIRANDA TATE --- The twist at the end reveals her secret identity then she dies within five minutes with some confusing dialogs. Come on Nolan...

JOHN BLAKE --- Nolan takes the artistic license and twist with a few characters. He is one of them.

First 1/3 of the movie was Brilliant and Perfect !!! It met my expectations. Rest of the two third was inconsistent and choppy. There are some scenes which look silly. Like the Bruce Wayne's Jailbreak ?? Few falls( i can count them on my fingers ... 3!!) and he made it. i don't remember him thanking anyone who helped him recover and supported him during JailBreak. All that happens in 6 months but it appears as though it happened in few days like two weeks. Entire story telling and twist at the end is silly. It seems like Studio forced Nolan to take that stance.

What makes this movie interesting is the fact that it deals with real issues like terrorism and Occupy Wall Street movement.

It is NOT a Perfect Conclusion. Specially not a Brave one. Why ??? How would studios make Justice League ?? How would studios go on blowing sequels after sequel.

If there would be a Justice League movie in near future, i can imagine this movie being inconsistent in story telling. Bale wont be in it neither Nolan(unless of course there is financial crunch) so where would they take characters. Justice League just for the heck of it.

Nolan didn't raise the bar for Reboots.

He is just ANOTHER EXAMPLE of a DIRECTOR who was burdened up with a lot of expectations and ended up ruining the conclusion.

All in all this movie has an ENDING, NOT THE ONE IT DESERVES BUT THE ONE IT NEEDS. Watch this movie enjoy this movie..but don't expect brilliance

4.title: Non-sensical explosion fest
4.content: The predecessor, The Dark Knight, is imo a great super-hero film. I am a huge Batman fan, and really wanted to enjoy this. However, I just found it impossible. A lot of the action scenes are fantastic, but the plot and editing are truly shocking in their attempt to take on far more material than could be handled in 2 hours. To all those who are writing raving and enthusiastic reviews, and who will probably hate me for this one: I heartfeltedly ask you to write a detailed summary of the plot as you recall it, and then re-read what you wrote. If any of it makes any sense to you, then you have my sympathy. Of course, this is a super-hero flick, and a certain suspension of doubt is part of enjoying it. But when you get the feeling that the over-hyped movie is mainly addressing spectators who prefer explosions over storyline and character depth, it's difficult to feel much respect for it. In TDK, Harvey Dent and Joker were undoubtedly far more profoundly portrayed than Selina "one-liner" Kyle - who actually managed to make me miss Michelle Pfeiffer - , "subtitles, please" Bane and above all "nuclear-bomb builder, prison escapee, Wayne industries stockholder, one-night-stand, ridiculous plot twist revealer, couldn't care less who the hell she is, get rid of her in truck accident asap" Talia. A movie that felt to me like an amusement park House of Horrors. Some thrills and fun moments. Then the ride ends, you look back. "What was that all about?" "Oh, nevermind, next ride".

4.title: Nothing like the first two...
4.content:
Visually stunning at times, (considering they had to make a Gotham City with out using the real thing)otherwise, slow, lumbering, lethargic, probably pre-diabetic and in need of exercise, this bloated mess is a sad end to a franchise that has seen better days. At least the first two times around it was fun....(and I mean the Batman of '67 and '89 respectively) This version sent me scurrying to the computer to see if my thoughts of "terrible movie" were valid.

But I suppose like anything you could find people on both sides.

It's only the ones that say 'it's crap' are the ones I'm paying attention to.

4.title: Don't bother
4.content: I just don't get it? How can people give this movie a 10? I am a big fan of the last 2 Batman movies, but this one was a let down. For a start Batman is in it for about 15 mins. You can still not understand what it is he is saying? And as for Bane. I could make out one in every three words that he said. The story is very very slow to get going and when it does its slow even then. There is not a lot about this movie that i can give a thumbs up to? Ummmm Catwomen was quite good. But at the end of the day she was just a filler to pad out a very dull film. Lets hope then thay re-boot this again, (come one thay will)thay don't mess it up. All in all i would go see this film if you have three hours to kill and Spiderman is not on.

4.title: so...disappointing
4.content: By far the worst movie Christopher Nolan has ever done. cliché, drawn out, predictable and just boring. i love Memento and Inception...the Prestige was great, the Dark Knight was awesome...i wanted to like it. i even watched it again in the theater to make sure i wasn't just in a bad mood or something the first time. nope, it just sucks. didn't care about the characters, didn't like the acting, found nothing interesting about it. the parallels that people seem to cling to weren't groundbreaking or poignant. easily the worst batman of the new trilogy and probably the most overrated movie on IMDb. i wanted to give it a 1 to even out all the ridiculously high ratings...but to be honest i gave it a 4

4.title: At times good but lots of plot holes and has the potential to be a good movie
4.content:
Lets start with the GOOD BITS-

Very good use of drama for effect, when Bane blows up the playing field and all you can hear is the soft voice of the boy singing.

Good special effects when it is present.

Awesome bat cars/planes/bikes

BAD BITS-

Almost everything

Batman would surely have died from that nuclear bomb and everyone in Gotham would have died of radiation.

Why would all the police officers in Gotham go underground when they know that Bane has lots of explosives to trap them(which were used to cut off every way into Gotham).

When Bruce's back is broken it would have paralyzed him or even killed him but miraculously is cured by a kick to the back. And even if this were possible it would take months to recover but Bruce is back up on his feet within days.

Robin finally turns up (not in costume) at the end of the trilogy when there's no more left!!

VERY LONG AND SLOW AND GETS QUITE BORING AFTER THE FIRST HOUR OR TWO!!

VERDICT: I was quite hoping for it to be "the ultimate ending to a brilliant trilogy" but I felt as though it was very slow and didn't even compare to the first 2 (batman begins and the dark knight).

Bane, although a very good character is not explained as well as he could of and you cant understand what he is saying through most of the film. This is also the same for Catwoman.

You only get to see batman in costume for no longer than 20 minutes in the whole two and three quarter long film which is quite disappointing.

I suppose its better than watching paint dry but not by much and its an okay movie that does kinda finish the trilogy but if you haven't got much time to spare, don't waste your time watching this as its a complete waste of 3 hours unless your the ultimate Batman fan.

4.title: the lowest from the trilogy
4.content:
First , like most of the reviewers, I'm a Batman fan too . The film I saw it at midnight preview and I have big indulgence even for Schumacher's Batman films

pros for this film are couples :

1. Action scene are overwhelming - except the ending 2. Supporting actors raise the stake pretty high 3. Action scenes can be used for few more films - producers can save some money

cons are several :

1. Hurry up screenplay ( money greed?) 2. Inconsistency in editing/finishing the film (scenes are not connected most of the time ) 3. The Batman's major actions are in close combat 4. No chemistry between the good characters - max. guilty feelings 5. The script is not using any batman themas - except the batman light signal 6. The film is rough but not in a violent way more as a general impression

like usual - big trailers/advertising - low quality

4.title: I will only applaud the amazing soundtrack and action scenes
4.content:
With that said I must say as a life long fan of Batman and DC Comics this movie did nothing to make me like it. Bane was surprisingly flat in character, didn't live up to my expectations that I have from the comics and TV series and animated movies.

Catwoman was horrible. The cast for her was horrid as I had foreseen it would be. Anne Hathaway got nothing on Michelle Pfeiffer as Catwoman. Where was the sexual tension that has always been there between Batman and Catwoman I ask? It was all wasted on hidden identity Talia Al Ghul, who I might add was a horrible written character.

Sure Talia and Bruce had a short lived romance flick but it was over just like that. And what is the thing about Talia 'controlling' the whole action against Gotham and Batman? Moving on...

Alfred Pennyworth was ruined in this movie. The Alfred Pennyworth DC Comics has made and everyone loves as the most loyal butler and friend to Wayne ups and leaves because his feelings are hurt, because Bruce doesn't want to have a family and live on as if nothing ever happened in his life? What the hell? I love the cast of Alfred however but the script ruined the most likable character in Batman's universe.

Do not get me started on John Blake appearing to be the new Robin. That is so wrong on many levels. All DC fans knows it was Dick Grayson, Jason Todd and then Tim Drake who carried the mantle of Robin, Batman's sidekick. I know Bale didn't want to be in a movie with Robin in it but that was a lazy way to bring in a Robin and then not using one of the original Robins.

And last but not least... Bruce giving up the mantle as Batman to have a life with Selina??????! There's no words how wrong that is on so many levels. All DC fans knows that Bruce would never, ever give up being Batman until he was damned sure Gotham was free of lunatics and the harsh crime roaming there. The ending was half done and it seems like Nolan just wanted his Batman project to be over and done with because he absolutely failed on so many levels on showing what the Batman is all about.

With all the negative things said I loved the action scenes. The few scenes with Batman was lame, but otherwise okay. As always the soundtrack was a great hit. We get the tension building and chaos raging. The music itself told a better story than the movie itself.

4.title: Batman Review
4.content:
Batman was always my favorite childhood superhero, but when you've grown a little it's not the same anymore. The cape and mask are ugly and how does Wayne's voice suddenly change when he's the bat beats me? They should do something real to Batman's costume, maybe his voice sounds different because the mask suffocates the poor guy.Speaking of masks why on Earth does Bane wear a mask? For people to take him seriously he claims. All he had to do was frighten some stockbrokers and free them within seconds, the act of a dumb villain no doubt.You won't make up a single word Bane says- irritating.

You can't help, but miss the bad o' villains from previous releases given the lack of enthusiasm displayed by Bane and company.False characters are plenty here for example, a cop amazingly makes detective simply because he knows Batman's identity wow! what would we do without him? 3000 cops are effortlessly lured into a tunnel. Bane's incredible strength is unknown his sister claims that it's because he can suppress pain and agony, you learn something new everyday. I can on and on but I'd spoil it for you.

4.title: The Dark Kni - ho-hum! yawn. excuse me - ight Rises
4.content:
The Dark Knight - it looked good. The music score was great. It had mood - lots and lots of mood. The antagonist stole the show every time he walked on screen. Bane looked and sounded good. Every time I was stuck watching someone else, I wished Bane would return just so I can listen to him talk (and yeah, you had to focus, at times, to understand him).

They did a great job letting us know who was "in on it." One can easily see - and is often reminded, with great repetition - who knows Batman, who likes him, who distrusts him, etc.

By my lord, what a boring movie. I just didn't care one bit about anything on the screen. I was rather begging for it to end. This one I should have saved for a $1 rental. But to be honest, if I watched this from my sofa, I would never, never stay away two and a half hours through this.

My thoughts are with the families in Aurora, Colorado. I love the movies - particularly big-bang movies on the big screen. And I went to see The Dark Knight Rises partly out of sympathy and support for both the victims of that awful event, and also for the love of my summer pastime, movies on the big silver screen. So, you see where my heart is. I really wanted to like TDKR. But sorry, this movie was just plain boring.

4.title: Mediocre movie
4.content: This is just a review from an average movie watcher, I don't claim to be a Batman expert or anything of the like. I just want to start by saying I love Christian Bale as Batman. However, this movie was not up to par. It was way too boring in the beginning and felt like a 5 hour movie! I was disappointed in the ending and quite honestly, I really could gone without seeing the movie. (Spoiler if you don't read celeb news or if you haven't seen the movie...) I probably won't watch any more of these movies after hearing that Christian Bale is hanging up the cape. The dude from 3rd Rock might make a good Robin, but not a Batman. Just my opinion, of course.

4.title: Bloated Shallow Rubbish
4.content: This film is expensive bloated nonsense. Watch out for a gut churning funny performance from Michael Caine - he kills (as in ruins) every scene he's in, his lines are terrible and his delivery just risible, and why use these actors who've had that surgery that keeps their eyes open and makes them look so conspicuously Hollywood rather than anything like the type of character they're trying to portray? The story swivels on a conceit revealed far too late in the day for it resonate, it just leaves you feeling cheated, and it is silly anyway, and the whole thing is just overblown and for low IQ boys, silly fights, silly toys, not genre defining but clichéd and hackneyed. Just a franchise and director going through the motions using pyrotechnics to obscure the shallow truth.

4.title: Tired formula needs a mercy killing
4.content:
Strip away the visuals and the cinematography, and this movie screams self-parody. There's nothing new to say in this franchise that hasn't been beaten over your head in previous movies. It's no Batman Begins or the Dark Knight, which were solid movies. But this time the franchise jumped the shark.

The formula broke under the weight of its own hyperbole. So tired and overwrought, I completely lost interest. Self-important high drama, big bad city terrorism, evil trying to outdo itself with every sequel, fabricated family drama we've seen many flavors of before. Even the surprises were no longer surprises.

I felt nothing watching this flick. Well, with the exception that I just wanted everybody to die in a fiery ball of neutron bomb death to end the franchise as a mercy killing.

Please make it stop, Nolan.

4.title: Just bearable
4.content:
It was hard for this movie to follow the very good film that was The dark knight but it could have been better than this nonetheless.It was too long and as a result of that it was boring at times.Too many things were going on that weren't interesting at all.

A lot of the characters weren't very likeable,to me at least but they were annoying instead.I never liked Oldman as James Gordon and Freeman as Fox.They were kind of lame characters and I believe in future Batman films there will be better portrayals of these characters.On the contrary I liked Tom Hardy as Bane.I didn't have a problem with his voice.He wasn't as multi dimensional as the Joker and Twoface from TDK but he had a strong presence in this movie despite his weak ending.As far as Batman is concerned I will agree that he was underused in this movie.To be honest I never cared much about Bale's Batman in this trilogy, he didn't carry any of the three films and he wasn't one of the strongest parts of these movies.As you can understand I definitely don't think Bale is the best Batman, but he was an ok Bruce Wayne.Last and least there's Hathaway as Selina Kyle.I'm almost certain that either Nolan or the studio put her in the flm because they wanted a female as the love interest of the protagonist.Her character didn't fit in the story and was by far worse than Michelle Pfeiffer.Her presence was a waste of screen time.The movie without her would have been shorter and better.

The story was weak.The writing wasn't very polished either.The fight scenes were ordinary but I liked Bane's fighting style.The score was a strong part of the movie even though it was also used in TDK.The last two scenes were nicely done especially the scene with Wayne and Alfred.

All in all this movie was just good.It is highly overrated but what can you do.I expected it.TDK is easily the best of the three,the first and this one are mediocre.Nolan has done so many great films and I was let down a little bit by this one which is his worst next to Batman Begins.

4.title: Crap

4.title: Weird.

Bale throws a rock at the TV when he's in that one jail scene kinda ridiculous in general and why have people even stayed in Gotham? and how isn't everyone running away from the city in any way possible like the second anything happens

4.title: Sleepy script, music stuck on repeat, empty story
4.content:
This site has zero integrity left when multiple reviews can be posted so easily by same person. They all repeat same line about "wonderful trilogy" or some nonsense, saturating the ratings with perfect 10 scores. Batman nerds or bored trolls, who knows. Maybe a legion of reviewers with bad taste in movies.

I wanted to like it, but it has no heart. Very sloppy and clumsy fight scenes. The constant music tries to sustain suspense, but ends up being a wall of irritation.

Bad guy Bane was fun, but that's about where the good stuff ends. Everything else was labored and generic. People go on about Nolan, but this movie came out of a vending machine, it's trash.

4.title: Ordinary...nothing exceptional or worth praising
4.content: TDKR is an ordinary sequel to an extraordinary film. I was expecting much more from the sequel after the standards the first film had set. The worst part is the story. Its just another typical superhero plot, where the city is in danger and the hero rescue it. We have seen this 100 times before. There was nothing unique or new in the film. The climax was ordinary as well. In summary I am really disappointed by Nolan's work after some masterpieces he has given to the world like TDK,Inception, Prestige etc. Common Nolan you are a unique film maker and we have seen that. 4.title: Bane's voice ruins it
4.content:
Bane's voice sounds like it was dubbed over the entire film. It's like it's coming from a loudspeaker behind you but you still can't understand half of what he says because of the muffled sound and ridiculous accent.

They were under duress to modify the script after the tragic death of Heath Ledger. But Bane was a poor choice to fill that void. The plot is empty. It's an hour too long and still goes nowhere.

4.title: Does a lot of injustice to the batman personalities involved
4.content:
I went into this movie expecting another Nolan masterpiece. Before I write my review however I need to make it perfectly clear that Nolan makes good movies and i tend to enjoy his movies for what they are.

No matter how much I try though I find his third installment to be the weakest batman of the 3.

We start the story 8 years after the dark knight "killed" Harvey dent. But thanks to the Dent law crime in Gotham is almost all gone (how a law could do that i do not know). But the impression is given that the law is almost considered a form of oppression.

We find Bruce Wayne to have a bad knee and to be living as a recluse wondering openly what his live with Rachel would have been like. However with the coming of bane we suddenly need our hero needs to come out of retirement because of the actions of Selina Kyle (who is NEVER called catwoman!).

My biggest problem with this movie is that it used bits and pieces of different batman comics to make a story. The famous bane breaking batman scene is in the movie. But it loses much of its impact. Knightfall was about bane knowing who batman was and wanting to break his soul AND body. Only when batman was mentally and physically drained from all his hardships did bane decide to fight batman purely to destroy him and who he was.

There was no such thing here, bane just managed to get him into a room with batman and he kicked the snot out of him. However the powerful scene where batman gets his back "dislocated" is immediately destroyed by the fact some random guy can just punch Batman's back straight like it is some bend piece of iron that needs to smashed straight.

We then get a basic rockyish theme where batman is training while bane takes over the city. But sadly where I felt bane was not the bane I know and while I do agree that Nolan needs creative freedom the way he handled the obvious spoiler of Talia al Ghul is detestable.

We are introducted to a raving lunatic who wants nothing more than Bruce to die and Gotham to burn.

My entire problem with this premise is that it does zero justice to the persona we known from the DC comics Talia was always conflicted because she was in Love with Bruce Wayne and was loyal to the goals of her father which meant she always had to take a side. This one on the other hand was just angry and had no soul she was there because of the sake of being there.

The way bane was portrayed is good but Ifelt they really ignored his venom addiction which makes him so strong. Now he was just a body builder with pain suppressants. And Just like Batman's knee (which apparently happened during Batman's fall in 2 at the end) why on earth where people mutilating bane in one cut scene it would have been nice to get a deeper glimpse in the persona bane rather than the few peeks.

Another perfect example of where Nolan just dropped the ball is with Alfred. He just told Bruce Wayne that he burned Rachel her letter and he was hone the next part for almost the entire movie i really felt the Rachel scene and the repercussions it had on Bruce AND Alfred should have been highlighted more. We had 3 hours but most of it was spend on excellent photography and set pieces but sadly the plot suffered for it.

If you do not know the batman persona's I listed here I am certain you will enjoy this movie for what it is. If you expect a dark knight x2 your going to sadly be disappointed.

4.title: My least favorite in the trilogy but would still definitely get a reccomendation

This film is a satisfying conclusion to a really solid trilogy. Bane is a good villain though his voice is kind of ridiculous. Seriously why does he sound like a muppet. You know a classic chekhovs gun moment.

8/10.

4.title: Good actors - Doesn't have substance
4.content:
There is a lot going on in this movie don't get me wrong...the actors are wonderful at what they are doing...it's just missing something.

SPOILERS (Kind of / not really)

4.content:
I liked Batman Begins (8/10), and loved The Dark Knight (9/10). Bought Imax tickets for TDKR (nearest Imax was 3.5 hours away...) and the disappointment I experienced was similar to after watching Batman Forever. *Love Nolan - Interstellar (10/10) is one of my favourites.

4.title: Fails To Rise Above Suspect Politics and Muddle
4.content:
An impossibly high bar was set. "The Dark Knight" featured, in Heath Ledger, one of the top film performances since Edison started cranking. "Batman Begins" boldly penetrated the psyche of a frightened boy and followed his progress to Gotham's enigmatic crime fighter.

Promised to be the final Nolan Dark Knight film, the stone covering "The Dark Knight Rises" tomb will soon miraculously be moved as resurrection with Robin is assured, though perhaps not with Nolan.

Given the stellar first two installments, there's bound to be quibbling, both major and minor, among the Batman fetishists who threaten Critics with death over the award of less than stellar reviews whether "The Dark Knight Rises" filled their tummies. The best that can be said is it was the end of an arc. And, risking death, to this palate it was more a Rice Krispie treat than sumptuous Last Supper.

"The Dark Knight Rises" lacks conviction. When Bane, the disfigured, masked bad-guy from a shithole prison in an unnamed (Afghanistan, Iraq) country, takes over Gotham he takes everything from the 1 percenters and gives it to the 99%. (Bruce Wayne loses everything, including electricity in the mansion due to non-payment). This hardened criminal Robin Hood then isolates Gotham and lights a five month long fuse on a nuclear bomb ticking down to the big "Fire." These disparate plot elements – Che Guevera meets Bin Laden – mix like 10w40 and water. This leaves the viewer to swim in the resulting oily mess.

William Goldman wrote a self-critique of his script for "Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid" by stating there were too many reversals. Mr. Goldman, those reversals added charm and surprise and lifted the story. The same can not be said for the over length "The Dark Knight Rises": Mr. Wayne is quickly dispatched by Bane and spends much of the rest of the film getting his ass kicked and re-training; in their ultimate battle, Nolan uses a cheap deus ex machina when Bane is dispatched not by the Knight, but by the Batcycle riding Catwoman (the luscious Anne Hathaway who struggles to find meat on the script bone and just wisecracks); a teary Alfred leaves Bruce; Gordon is hospitalized for a long stretch; all of Gotham's finest are buried alive for three months; ad nauseum.

There is always a problem in unduly complex films because they require so much expository dialogue. (And there is lots of it here.) Conversely, there are elements from the previous films paraded across the screen without explanation, i.e. Liam Neeson taunting Wayne in a ghostly cameo as the life-everlasting Ra's al Ghul. There certainly is no requirement to experience the first two films, but it sure helps.

What's lacking in "The Dark Knight Rises" is the chaos and frenetic energy paired with a walk along the fine line between Wayne's madness and his foe's insanity. That balance made the first films extraordinary. Draining it from "The Dark Knight Rises" is a major disappointment. This Bruce Wayne also needs a 'scrip for Viagra.

While the cast is generally fine, Joseph Gordon-Levitt as Officer Blake (and the soon to be Robin) is a most unfortunate casting mistake. He's flat, and in way over his head. Thomas Hardy as Bane is an actor's nightmare – masked throughout nearly the entire film, voice filtered. That leaves just his eyes which conveyed little about the character.

The tech credits are top notch, and 2D served this gritty film well (one of the only smart moves Nolan made).

"The Dark Knight Rises" is overripe. Its politics are confused and suspect – at once Far Left, then Far Right (though parts should be extracted as a recruiting tool for the Occupy Wall Street movement). It serves as a fair Actioner, but it fails to cut to the chase and deliver a knockout punch.

4.title: so so

4.title: How did this happen, again...
4.content:
If you like Transformers 3, Rise of the Planet of the Apes, Gran Torino, The Hunger Games, Taken, Alice in Wonderland, Transporter 3, Snow White and the Huntsman, and so many others like these titles, then stop here. Stop, here. This review is not for those who don't ask questions or find plot holes, or even care for accuracy or realism at all for that matter. No offense to you, but these words will be of no use to you, and likely offend your opinions.

First, I will comment on what I respect about the film. I do acknowledge some of the visual effects, and I do enjoy the soundtrack.

I'd like to start by commenting on the cast. I thought I made the mistake of not reading reviews before watching this film, but then found out that I would have made a bigger mistake by doing so before hand. Several people claim in their reviews that this cast was genius and perfect. I will not review other reviews, but really, common. There are literally 5 characters from Inception in this film, or maybe 4, I honestly lost count. I respect each one of them differently as actors, but this was ridiculous to bag and tag them all in this film. Nolan just got lazy and figured his old pals could handle the roles with no questions asked. I really don't think anyone questions scripts sometimes because of films like this.

Bane, Bane, Bane. The first time I heard his voice I actually threw up some popcorn. I was unaware that Sean Connery was part of the cast, but I did grow to accept it. Although his voice was annoyingly loud and exceptionally silly. The whole time. That is only the verbal problem I have with Bane. Physically, he looks like an old steroid abusing wrestler from the 80s. Really, no one else caught this? His voice, his build (most characters are as tall as him), and then that mask. That mask looks like a piece of SCUBA equipment. But we find out later that it, well, we never actually find out what it does. Or did we? Someone in that hole prison made this for him? He survived the beating from the other prisoners? He was beaten for helping a little boy, or girl, from escaping a prison? He was in love with a little girl, who was a princess? He was how old when he helped her? Easily 30, and yet somehow 30 years later he still looked 30? His scars from the small scene with his face in bandages were all healed? His mask can withstand quite literally every blow, up until the end of the movie? No one thought to shoot this guy in the head? Moving on. Although, there is more.

Now Catwoman, where to begin with her. Hathaway is a pretty face, and nothing more. I have seen enough of her films to know her style of acting, and action is not and never, EVER will be in her qualifications. Catwoman steals from the rich and gives to the poor, a true Robin Hood mimic. Why does she steal so much? She claims that she has to eat. She claims that, or something similar, for the whole film. Where did she get these skills? Who was her lesbian tag along friend? Why was she able to get out of jail/prison/wherever so many times when her record was as big as the bible? What was her back story? Why did she dress like a cat when she had no pictures of cats or have any interest in the movie at all about cats? Oh, because she was a cat burglar? Shocking. Again, plenty more, but running out of words.

Every single character in this film tried so hard to be philosophical. They all gave each other their own perception of life, and all clearly knew each other since each of them were born. Alfred couldn't stop crying, nor could most of the other characters. Really, pay attention to how many different characters tear up how many different times. It is crazy overkill, and unnecessary. Apparently all of these little street rats, that all somehow formed an unknown underground army were all ex-military personnel. They quickly knew how to build/drive the Batmobiles. They were all "trained killers" as I think Batman himself claimed at one point. But they lived, in sewers. In sewers? In sewers. Where would training like this come from? Why/how would trained people live in sewers? How was Bane so popular in the entire world and warmly welcomed into the sewer gang? Why did he choose Gothem? Oh yea. Why was he so faithful to this little girl, or boy? How did that little girl, or boy, make a jump that so many other grown men couldn't? Oh yea, hope, or something. Bane claimed he was born in the shadows, but we found out later that Bane was not the little girl, or boy, that we thought. So where did Bane come from? How was Bane able to get Batman to that hole prison and make it back to Gothem in such a short time? Why/how did that prison exist? How was there a TV with electricity in it, and how did it get a Gothem/American news channel? How did street rats, Sean Connery, and the crazy lady from Inception pull the biggest terrorist act in America? Why did it take that cop so long to figure out that Bruce Wayne was Batman? Really. Why/how did the capturers feed 3,000 cops a day? Why didn't those cops have guns when they escaped? Why wasn't the city blown up earlier if that was the master plan the whole time? Why/how did Batman take the time to poor gasoline into the bat symbol on a bridge? Oh yea, hope. Really, there is no concept of time in this movie.

There are a million other things, but ponder these for now.

4.title: Disappointing
4.content:
Im a big comic fan and Batman is one of the big one's and so far I loved the recreation of the Batman movies. The first one was awesome and the second one almost as good but now that I finally got the time to see the third one I must say I walked away disappointed.

Not sure where to start but lets try from the beginning. Some funny talking guy in a mask hijacks and kills a bunch of people on a plane to kidnap a scientist. One which he had already pretty much in his possession but I guess he wanted to prove that he is some kind of bad- ass by killing a bunch of CIA people on a plane. Mmkay... doesn't make much sense to me but I guess it was an excuse for a "big" beginning.

Then it moves on with Batman allegedly retired because people didn't need him anymore. Now why a huge cosmopolitan city didn't need him anymore begs the question why they needed him in the first place? I guess to get rid of the Ras Al Ghul threat and then the Joker but those two were hardly the only opponents of Batman but apparently in the movies they were? Mmkay...

But then this new psycho bad guy comes to come and finish Ras Al Ghul's work but the way he does it was way to convoluted. Something about some fusion technology and how it can be turned into a bomb but he seems pretty capable to bomb the city to ruins without it so why he needs a fusion bomb from it does again not make much sense. But I guess they need a plot so let's move on.

I have to say that this psycho mask guy was pretty scary, despite of his funny voice, and he seemed to be a full fledged psycho, terrorist. However in the end it turns out that he was just some stooge for some diabolical women who was the real person behind it all. Yeah you know political correctness, feminism and all that where girls can dish it out as much as guys. Alright I guess but the problem is that she was never nearly as convincing as this Bane guy (psycho mask guy) so it all just feels contrived just to capture the female audience.

To top it of we now also got a female heroines, and I use that therm loosely, because she was just a self serving crook who steals and betrays Batman but for some inexplicable reason Batman somehow forgives her not only once but twice!

Yep she robs Batman and then somehow he still trusts her but then she betrays him but still after having his back broken and thrown into a jail he trusts her yet again? Makes no sense at all but again it seems to be a motive her to catch the female audience because she is your typical condescending, self-serving girl who we are now told is alright for women to be like because they are just surviving in a male dominated world... I think I am going to puke.

The ending was alright I guess but no explanation given to how a junior cop is supposed to take over as Batman. Where will he get the training and motivation for that? Bruce spent years in various criminal organizations and trained in a highly fanatical, militaristic assassination clan before he became Batman but this guy is just a normal cop. Again does not make any sense at all and I think it was just put there to continue squeezing money from the Batman IP.

Terrible and a very disappointing "ending" to an otherwise excellent trilogy.

4.title: The Dark Knight Rises is Obvious and Tedious
4.content:
The film generates so much anticipation from fans of Batman through the world, and I as a fan of Batman, along with having enjoyed fully the previous two, go after my job just to get the entry for the first function available ... but what I saw was disappointing. The plot is obvious and poor, a fallen hero and damaged without explanation of why, inconsistencies with the two previous films, cliché after cliché creating something very corny, relationships and events without explanation (if you're not a fan of Batman and not notice the name Catwoman in a document, it could be any female character in the comics, but this is a mistake of the director not the actress) impossible situations even for a superhero movie, much validation to vehicles and little of the intelligence, creativity and skills of the Bat, and finally the announcement of the end film (which is not representative of the character of Batman) leaves a bad mouth taste.

Nobody says that the film is not entertaining at times, or that it devoid of action, but if you compare it with the two previous films this is less than one tenth its quality, in the end the film serves just to change the actor, was a sad end to the Nolan trilogy since Batman Begins and The Dark Knight rescued much of what makes Dark Knight one of the most enduring and popular character in the comic book industry, with two of the best movies make for the Batman.

4.content: Starts really well. Moving scenes between the great actors. Gearing up nicely and then.....too many characters and missing plot lead to nonsense scenes and all action no substance.
